entries.heading: A working minimal build is included
entries.text: examples/acim-minimal/ contains a dependency-free C++20 functional MVM simulator, ADC clamp, CMake target policy, Ninja presets for GCC/Clang/MSVC, CTest unit and smoke lanes, optional GoogleTest discovery, clang-format/clang-tidy configuration, installation rules, and an AArch64 Linux toolchain example. It is a software reference model, not an analog circuit model. First configure, build and test Run inside examples/acim-minimal # Linux baseline cmake --preset gcc cmake --build --preset gcc ctest --preset gcc # Independent compiler and sanitizer lane cmake --preset clang cmake --build --preset clang ctest --preset clang cmake --preset asan-clang cmake --build --preset asan-clang ctest --preset asan-clang # Windows host path from a Visual Studio Developer PowerShell cmake --preset msvc cmake --build --preset msvc ctest --preset msvc ABI rule: record compiler ID/version, target triple, C++ standard library, build type, sanitizer mode and public ABI version. Do not pass C++ standard-library objects across a plugin boundary compiled with incompatible libstdc++ , libc++ or MSVC CRT/ABI settings; keep the stable external boundary in C handles, fixed-width fields and explicitly versioned structures. Build graph and configuration

entries.heading: CMake owns native targets; pyproject owns the Python product
entries.text: Keep target relationships explicit in CMake, package and tool entry points explicit in pyproject.toml , and runtime/test choices in validated configuration files. Environment variables may override a declared option, but the resolved value must appear in the run manifest. Generate Contract code acim_schema_codegen emits C++, Python and firmware definitions Foundation Artifact and common Versioning, hashing, status, logging, target and executable readers Core Compiler and HAL API Host-only compiler plus backend-neutral device interfaces Execute Runtime and backends Functional, queued simulation and hardware implementations Expose C API and Python Installed ABI, bindings, wheel, CLI and framework adapters Verify Tests and packages Link public targets, install tree and selected private test helpers Recommended native target graph One target per ownership boundary; private dependencies stay private acim_schema_codegen -> acim_common -> acim_artifact -> acim_compiler -> acim_hal -> acim_hal_functional -> acim_hal_queued_sim -> acim_hal_hardware -> acim_runtime -> acim_c_api -> acim_python_binding -> acim_tools acim_gtest_contracts # schema, artifact and ABI layout acim_gtest_compiler # IR, passes, mapping and encoding acim_gtest_runtime # lifecycle, queues, memory and recovery acim_gtest_hal_conformance # same cases for every backend acim_gtest_firmware_model # descriptor validation and state machines Configuration Owns Required fields or profiles Validation rule CMakePresets.json Repeatable native configure/build/test modes dev , release , asan , ubsan , coverage , cross-compile presets CI invokes the same presets documented for developers. pyproject.toml Python package, build backend, dependencies, optional groups and CLI entry points Supported Python versions, core/runtime extras, test/docs tools, wheel contents Build and test a wheel in a clean environment; model tests use the installed package. pytest.ini Test discovery, markers and default diagnostics unit , integration , hardware , smoke , nightly , performance , model tiers Unknown markers fail; hardware tests cannot enter the default host-only lane. configs/targets/*.yaml Target class and capabilities Schema/ABI version, revision, arrays, converters, memory, engines, commands, limits and units Schema validation plus compiler/runtime compatibility tests; every compile records the target hash. configs/test-matrices/*.yaml Where each test lane runs SKU, topology, marker, runner label, timeout, exclusivity, firmware, cleanup and retry policy CI validates that each required lane has a compatible runner and bounded timeout. configs/performance-thresholds/*.yaml Versioned regression policy Workload ID, metric, baseline, absolute limit, allowed change, owner and review date A threshold change is reviewed separately from the implementation it would excuse. configs/model-manifests/*.yaml Reproducible model workload Model/input hashes, preprocessing, shapes, precision, backend, accuracy metric, fallback, performance scenario E2E jobs reject implicit downloads, mutable model names and missing reference thresholds. Configuration rule: defaults belong beside their schema; overrides are typed, bounded and logged; units are part of the field name or type; deprecated fields have migration tests; and the fully resolved configuration hash is attached to every artifact, benchmark and failure bundle. Implementation chain

entries.heading: Build one executable path before expanding the surface area
entries.text: Each milestone adds exactly one new responsibility and must leave a testable artifact behind. This sequence prevents the model zoo, framework plugin, and hardware backend from hiding an unstable compiler/runtime contract. 1. Bootstrap Build and lint CMake presets, Python package, warnings, format, sanitizers 2. Contract Schema and ABI Target, artifact, command, status, trace, compatibility 3. Reference Functional model One MVM, digital epilogue, deterministic golden vectors 4. Compile One vertical slice Import, legalize, map, emit artifact, inspect 5. Execute Runtime and fake HAL Load, allocate, bind, submit, wait, trace, reset 6. Correlate Hardware and model Bring-up backend, framework path, accuracy, performance Milestone Code added Required proof Do not add yet M0: reproducible checkout Build presets, dependency lock, package metadata, pre-commit, minimal docs Clean machine configures, builds, installs, imports Python, and runs an empty CTest/pytest lane Board support, model integrations, optimization M1: machine contract Target schema, artifact envelope, commands, status codes, generated readers Round-trip, malformed-input, old/new schema, and cross-language compatibility tests Compiler policy hidden in ad hoc YAML M2: numerical reference FP32, quantized, ideal-array, and configurable nonideality implementations Golden MVM vectors and property tests across shapes, signs, saturation, and rounding Cycle claims or silicon accuracy claims M3: one-op compiler MatMul import, validation, mapping, command emission, artifact inspector Golden IR, illegal-target diagnostics, deterministic artifact hash, reference equivalence General fusion and broad operator coverage M4: executable runtime C API, sessions, buffers, queues, events, fake/functional HALs, trace Backend conformance, timeout/reset, resource cleanup, multithreaded lifecycle tests Framework-specific state in the runtime M5: first hardware path KMD/UMD or platform driver, firmware transport, DMA, interrupt, health, recovery Discovery, loopback, one-command smoke, reset after fault, simulator/hardware trace correlation Performance optimization before correctness and recovery M6: first model path Framework partition, package, one representative model, preprocessing/postprocessing End-to-end accuracy, fallback accounting, reproducible latency and power manifest Large model catalog with duplicate utilities M7: optimization and release Cost model, scheduling, fusion, caching, profiler, package and compatibility policy Measured regression thresholds, stress, multi-device if required, qualification report Optimization accepted without an attributed measurement Verification architecture

entries.heading: The test chain grows in cost, realism, and diagnostic distance
entries.text: Lower levels answer narrow questions quickly. Higher levels validate integration and product behavior, but they should never be the first place a compiler rule, allocator invariant, or command encoding is tested. Qualification Chip populations, PVT, aging, drift, defects, power and thermal limits Release or silicon gate Stress and soak Long duration, concurrency, repeated reset, memory pressure, fault injection Nightly or weekly End to end Framework through preprocessing, compile, runtime, device, fallback, postprocessing Merge and nightly tiers Performance Kernel, operator and model latency, throughput, bytes, utilization, energy Controlled runners Sweep and differential Shapes, dtypes, layouts, precision, faults and calibration against a reference Post-commit and nightly Integration Compiler-artifact-runtime-simulator contracts and selected real-device paths PR routes and merge Smoke Discover, open, allocate, execute one operation, compare, close and reset Fast hardware confidence Unit One class, pass, encoding, state transition or Python API with deterministic inputs Every relevant PR Static checks Format, lint, schema, docs, dependency rules, generated files and compilation Local and every PR

entries.heading: Give every test lane one precise contract
entries.text: Lane Question answered Environment Typical trigger Acceptance and saved evidence Static Is the change structurally valid and reproducible? No hardware; clean source checkout Pre-commit and every PR Formatting, warnings-as-errors, lint, schema validation, docs links, dependency checks, generated-diff check all pass. C++ unit Does one low-level contract or state machine behave correctly? Host process with fakes; ASan/UBSan variants Every relevant PR GoogleTest assertions identify the exact invariant; no board, network, sleeps, or shared mutable lab state. Python unit Does one public Python API, importer rule, or analysis function behave correctly? Installed wheel or source package with mocks Every relevant PR pytest result, stable exception/status, parametrized shapes and dtypes, no hidden hardware requirement. Smoke Can the minimum supported execution path complete now? One simulator or reserved device Selected PRs, deployment, lab health Discover, open, allocate, execute one known vector, compare, close; save serial, firmware, artifact hash, trace, and reset result. Integration Do two or more owned components honor the same contract? Functional/queued simulator; selected hardware Changed-path PR route and post-commit Artifact loads across public C API; compiler/runtime/backend traces correlate; fault and cleanup paths are checked. Sweep Where does behavior fail across the supported state space? Parallel host simulation, then sampled hardware Post-commit and nightly Vector source, parameter set, random seed, expected result, actual result, first divergence, and minimized reproducer are stored. Performance Did a measured metric regress under a controlled configuration? Dedicated, thermally stable runner Kernel/model changes, nightly, release Warmups, sample distribution, p50/p95, cycles, bytes, energy, clocks, temperature, artifact and calibration IDs; compare with versioned threshold. End to end Does a real user workflow meet correctness and service-level goals? Packaged SDK and representative hardware Model tier policy, merge, nightly Real preprocessing/postprocessing, accuracy metric, fallback share, compile/load/execute timing, peak memory, throughput and power. Stress Does the system remain correct under time, load and recovery pressure? Isolated lab allocation Nightly, weekly, pre-release Soak duration, concurrency, memory pressure, injected faults, reset count, leak trend, temperature and terminal device state. Qualification Is the product robust across the deployed device population and operating envelope? Characterization and production labs Silicon, firmware, calibration or release change Device sample plan, PVT corners, defect classes, drift/retention, guard bands, confidence intervals and signed release report. GoogleTest, pytest, and test data

entries.heading: Choose the framework by the contract being protected
entries.text: Recommended test subtree Names describe scope, not just language tests/ |-- cpp/ | |-- unit/ | | |-- compiler/ | | |-- artifact/ | | |-- runtime/ | | |-- hal/ | | `-- firmware_model/ | `-- integration/ | |-- compiler_runtime/ | `-- runtime_backend/ |-- python/ | |-- unit/ | |-- integration/ | `-- package/ |-- smoke/ | |-- simulator/ | `-- hardware/ |-- sweeps/ | |-- operators/ | |-- numerical/ | |-- faults/ | `-- manifests/ |-- end_to_end/ | |-- vision/ | |-- transformer/ | `-- application/ |-- performance/ | |-- microbenchmarks/ | |-- operators/ | `-- models/ |-- stress/ |-- qualification/ |-- common/ | |-- fixtures/ | |-- device_pool/ | |-- artifact_capture/ | `-- comparisons/ `-- data/ |-- golden/ |-- models/ |-- calibration/ `-- target_descriptors/ Use GoogleTest pytest Best fit C++ IR utilities, encoders, allocators, queue/event state, HAL contracts, firmware host models Python API, framework import, parameter sweeps, model execution, lab fixtures, report validation Fixture scope Process-local fake objects and deterministic temporary files Function fixture by default; session fixture only for expensive immutable setup or reserved device lifecycle Selection Small executables or labels plus --gtest_filter Markers such as unit , hardware , smoke , nightly , performance Do not duplicate Test a C++ invariant once in GoogleTest; add a Python test only for binding behavior or an end-user contract, not the same private branch. Failure output Expected/actual typed values, state transition, command bytes, seed and target descriptor Node ID, parameters, backend, device identity, artifact hash, seed, trace path and minimized reproducer TT-Metal precedent: its root test CMake enables CTest and GoogleTest, while focused C++ executables and extensive pytest directories cover different layers. The model CI tier document further separates end-to-end, module, sweep, device-performance, PR-gate, and stress coverage rather than treating all model tests as equivalent. Performance discipline

entries.heading: A performance test is a controlled experiment, not a timed unit test
entries.text: Pin the workload Model/operator hash, shape, batch, sequence length, precision, layout, compiler options and fallback policy. Pin the machine Board SKU, device serial, firmware, clocks, power mode, temperature window, target descriptor, calibration and defect-map IDs. Separate phases Report compile, weight program, load, warmup and steady-state execution separately; do not hide setup in token or frame throughput. Use distributions Record sample count, warmup count, p50, p95, variability and outliers. One best run is not a regression baseline. Count causes Cycles, bytes, queue wait, DMA, array active time, ADC occupancy, digital fallback, stalls, saturation and retries explain the headline metric. Version thresholds Store absolute limits and allowed regression percentages with owner, reason, baseline commit and expiry/review date. Prove correctness first A faster incorrect result fails. Associate accuracy output and numerical-policy identity with every accepted performance record. Control instrumentation Use detailed traces to diagnose, then measure the official result with the declared low-overhead counter set. ACiM-specific rule: report cold programming, warm resident-weight inference, recalibration, and degraded/remapped execution as different scenarios. A resident-weight MVM number cannot stand in for the latency or energy of deployment, model switching, digital fallback, or recovery. Tracy and device profiling

entries.heading: Use Tracy directly on the host and preserve device time at the source
entries.text: Tenstorrent is a useful reference because its tooling exposes both host work and device-side RISC-V work. The reusable architecture is a split design: normal Tracy instrumentation for code running on the host, plus bounded cycle-stamped records for bare-metal firmware and accelerator engines. A clock-correlation and export layer brings the evidence together without changing when the device work appears to have happened. Recommended ACiM design: use upstream Tracy for host C++ and Python-visible runtime phases; use one fixed-record trace buffer per device producer; drain through the UMD/KMD path; fit each device clock to the host monotonic clock; then export an accurate device trace. Put device intervals into the Tracy UI only through a maintained bridge that accepts their original timestamps.

entries.heading: What the Tenstorrent implementation teaches
entries.text: The current TT-Metalium Tracy guide covers host C++, Python, and device views. The more detailed device program profiler guide shows the device mechanism: kernels emit bounded records, and the host runtime drains them for analysis. These are related views, but not the same instrumentation path. TT path Observed interface Reusable lesson for ACiM Host C++ Normal Tracy ZoneScoped or named zones execute in the host process. Instrument compiler, SDK, UMD, queue, DMA request, wait, fallback and postprocess directly. Device kernel DeviceZoneScopedN writes device-side scope records through TT's kernel profiler support. Use a device-native emit primitive around dispatch, data movement, MVM, converter and epilogue phases. Runtime enable TT_METAL_DEVICE_PROFILER=1 enables collection; device close drains automatically, or ReadDeviceProfilerResults(device) drains explicitly. Make profile mode and drain points explicit runtime policy, not unconditional firmware behavior. Evidence The documented device output includes profile_log_device.csv and can be inspected in device timeline lanes. Keep a machine-readable raw trace even when a richer profiler UI is available. Limits The guide warns about annotation cost, finite L1 records, inter-core skew, unsynchronized devices, and conflicts with DPRINT/Watcher. Publish buffer, clock, overhead and tool-exclusion contracts for every ACiM profiling mode. TT host pattern Runs where the host work occurs #include <tracy/Tracy.hpp> void submit_program() { ZoneScopedN("submit_program"); // Pack, enqueue, submit, and wait phases. } TT device-profiler pattern Reference pattern, not an ACiM header #include <tools/profiler/kernel_profiler.hpp> void kernel_main() { DeviceZoneScopedN("device_kernel"); // Device RISC-V work. }

entries.heading: Choose the path from the execution context
entries.text: 1. Locate Where did it run? Host process, firmware controller, analog engine, converter, DSP, DMA, or fabric 2. Host? Use Tracy zones Instrument the C++ call where it executes; preserve thread, nesting, frame, and lock context 3. Device? Read device cycles Firmware records the local cycle immediately before and after the operation 4. Transport Drain bounded records Per-producer SRAM buffer, sequence, drop count, capture ID, ABI, and clock metadata 5. Align Correlate clocks Multiple ping samples fit device cycles to the host monotonic timeline 6. Inspect Join by command ID Host Tracy capture plus accurate device trace, counters, numerical result, and machine state

entries.heading: Two data paths, one correlated investigation
entries.text: Host path: timestamps are created by Tracy in the process that performs the work. Application Request and frame Preprocess, compile/load policy, inference request, postprocess SDK / UMD Scoped host zones Session, buffer, queue, submit, wait, callbacks, locks, DMA requests Client TracyClient On-demand event collection in each instrumented process Transport Local socket Live event stream from the host process to the profiler Capture Tracy profiler Threads, zones, frames, plots, messages, memory and OS context Result Host attribution Compile, queue, DMA request, wait, callback, fallback, and CPU overhead Device path: timestamps are created on the controller or engine and survive the later drain. Controller Read cycle CSR Command dispatch, validation, programming, calibration, sequencer work Engines Emit IDs and counters DAC/input drive, array MVM, settle, ADC, accumulation, DMA, retries Device SRAM Fixed trace records One bounded single-producer buffer per source; no strings or allocation KMD / UMD Drain and validate DMA or MMIO, ABI sizes, sequence, drop count, capture and command IDs Runtime Fit clock and decode Per clock domain affine map plus generated event dictionary Exporter Preserve history CSV/JSON, Perfetto, or explicit-timestamp Tracy bridge Do not create ordinary host zones while draining records and label them as device work. Those zones describe the drain time. Upstream Tracy's normal scoped-zone API is excellent for host execution, but it is not a generic public API for injecting an arbitrary accelerator interval that finished earlier. Keep the raw correlated device timeline authoritative unless the profiler bridge explicitly supports external timestamps.

entries.heading: Use each output for the question it can answer
entries.text: Question Recommended mechanism What it preserves Important limit Why is the host request slow? Upstream Tracy zones, frames, plots, locks, messages, allocation and OS scheduling Original host timestamps, thread nesting and live context It cannot infer what happened inside an opaque accelerator command. Which device phase consumed cycles? Firmware/device records with begin/end cycles and fixed event IDs Original device time, source/core identity, sequence, counters and dropped records Instrumentation consumes device SRAM and cycles; a finite buffer can overflow. How do host and device overlap? Clock-correlated device export joined to host command/capture IDs Queue, DMA, command, MVM, ADC, DSP and completion ordering Every independent or variable-frequency clock domain needs its own fit. Must everything appear in Tracy? Maintained profiler fork or bridge with explicit timestamp/context support A unified interactive view when the integration is tested and versioned This is profiler integration code, not ordinary application-zone instrumentation. Is a regression real? Uninstrumented benchmark plus low-overhead hardware counters Official latency, throughput, energy, accuracy and machine configuration A rich diagnostic capture may perturb the result and cannot be the only baseline.

entries.heading: End-to-end capture sequence and ownership
entries.text: Step Application / SDK UMD / KMD Firmware / ACiM device Collector 1. Configure Select profiling mode, capture ID, command ID and event mask. Reserve DMA-visible trace storage and enforce ownership/isolation. Reset selected per-producer buffers and dropped counters. Open host Tracy capture and the raw device-trace output. 2. Synchronize Record host send and receive monotonic timestamps around several clock pings. Transport the ping without interpreting profiler semantics. Return local device cycle and clock-domain ID with the host cookie. Reject malformed samples; retain round-trip uncertainty. 3. Submit Open host zones for pack, enqueue, submit and wait; attach the command ID. Map buffers, ring doorbell, account bytes, and record interrupt path. Record dispatch receive and descriptor validation cycles. Keep host and device records under one capture manifest. 4. Execute Remain asynchronous where possible; do not hide blocking in a broad request zone. Expose queue and DMA progress counters. Record programming/calibration, input drive, settle/MVM, ADC, accumulation, fallback and output DMA. Detect sequence gaps, mismatched begin/end, and nearing capacity. 5. Complete Record wait completion, callback, D2H visibility and postprocess. Acknowledge interrupt/fence and make trace bytes visible safely. Close zones, publish record count, drop count, clock rate and terminal status. Associate terminal status, output hash and numerical counters. 6. Drain Request a drain after completion or at an explicit live-trace watermark. DMA records; KMD owns privileged transport, not event-name policy. Hand off a completed buffer; switch to the other buffer for live collection. Validate ABI before decoding any record. 7. Correlate Provide the host monotonic time base and command intervals. Provide transport counters and reset/DVFS epochs. Provide device cycles, source ID, clock domain and frequency metadata. Fit each domain, calculate residual/error bounds, and map cycles to host time. 8. Publish Save the Tracy capture reference and run manifest. Save driver counters and faults. Preserve raw records and firmware/event-dictionary versions. Write an accurate device trace, summary, and optional unified-view capture.

entries.heading: Add Tracy to host code without making it a hard dependency
entries.text: The working example under examples/acim-minimal/ implements this pattern. Profiling macros compile to no-ops by default; the opt-in preset fetches Tracy 0.13.1 at an exact commit, enables on-demand collection, and limits the client to localhost. CMake integration Target-scoped and opt-in option(ACIM_ENABLE_TRACY "Instrument host targets" OFF) option(ACIM_FETCH_TRACY "Fetch pinned Tracy" OFF) if(ACIM_ENABLE_TRACY) if(ACIM_FETCH_TRACY) include(FetchContent) set(TRACY_ENABLE ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE) set(TRACY_ON_DEMAND ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE) set(TRACY_ONLY_LOCALHOST ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE) set(TRACY_NO_BROADCAST ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE) FetchContent_Declare(tracy URL https://github.com/wolfpld/tracy/archive/05cceee0df3b8d7c6fa87e9638af311dbabc63cb.zip) FetchContent_MakeAvailable(tracy) else() find_package(Tracy CONFIG REQUIRED) endif() target_compile_definitions(acim_profiling INTERFACE ACIM_TRACY_ENABLED=1) target_link_libraries(acim_profiling INTERFACE Tracy::TracyClient) endif() Host instrumentation Zones match owned phases #include "acim/profiling.hpp" Result Runtime::submit(const Request& request) { ACIM_PROFILE_ZONE("Runtime::submit"); { ACIM_PROFILE_ZONE("validate_and_pack"); validate(request); pack_descriptors(request); } { ACIM_PROFILE_ZONE("queue_and_doorbell"); queue_.submit(request.command_id()); } { ACIM_PROFILE_ZONE("wait_for_completion"); completion_.wait(request.command_id()); } ACIM_PROFILE_PLOT("ACiM queue depth", queue_.depth()); ACIM_PROFILE_FRAME("ACiM inference"); return collect_result(request); } Zone the phase, not every loop iteration Start with request, compile, artifact load, H2D, submit, queue wait, D2H, fallback, and postprocess. Add inner zones only after evidence identifies a broad phase. Carry IDs as messages or structured metadata Command, graph, artifact, device, queue, capture, calibration, and defect-map IDs make host zones joinable to runtime logs and device records. Use frames deliberately A frame can mean one image inference, one decode token, or one service iteration. Do not mix meanings in one capture. Use plots for low-rate state Queue depth, outstanding DMA, temperature, power, fallback count, and device utilization are useful; per-element plots create noise and overhead. Build and run the included host integration Run inside examples/acim-minimal/ cmake --preset tracy cmake --build --preset tracy ctest --preset tracy # Start the Tracy profiler, connect locally, then run: ./build/tracy/acim_smoke-debug # Linux build\tracy\acim_smoke-debug.exe # Windows The fetched CMake target builds and links TracyClient ; obtain or build the desktop Profiler from the same Tracy version separately. With on-demand collection and broadcast disabled, connect to 127.0.0.1 before starting the workload.

entries.heading: Add a firmware-safe device trace
entries.text: Controller or engine instrumentation No strings, allocation, socket, or host timestamp #include "acim/device_events.h" #include "acim/device_trace.h" void run_tile(Command* command, AcimTraceBuffer* trace) { const uint16_t source = command->tile_id; acim_trace_set_command_id(trace, command->id); acim_trace_zone_begin(trace, read_device_cycles(), ACIM_EVENT_INPUT_DRIVE_DAC, source); drive_inputs(command); acim_trace_zone_end(trace, read_device_cycles(), ACIM_EVENT_INPUT_DRIVE_DAC, source); acim_trace_zone_begin(trace, read_device_cycles(), ACIM_EVENT_ARRAY_SETTLE_MVM, source); start_array_mvm(command); wait_array_done(); acim_trace_zone_end(trace, read_device_cycles(), ACIM_EVENT_ARRAY_SETTLE_MVM, source); acim_trace_counter(trace, read_device_cycles(), ACIM_EVENT_ADC_SATURATION_COUNT, source, read_adc_saturation_count()); } Runtime drain and correlation Pseudocode for the real UMD path samples = [] for cookie in range(sync_sample_count): host_send_ns = monotonic_ns() device_cycle = firmware.clock_ping(cookie) host_receive_ns = monotonic_ns() samples.append((host_send_ns, device_cycle, host_receive_ns)) correlation = fit_clock_correlation(samples) batch = device.dma_read_trace(capture_id) validate(batch.abi_version, batch.header_size, batch.record_size, batch.record_count, batch.dropped_records) for record in batch.records: host_ns = correlation.map(record.cycle) exporter.write(host_ns, record.source_id, event_name(record.event_id), record.kind, record.value)

entries.heading: The trace ABI is a hardware/software contract
entries.text: Field Why it exists Validation rule Typical failure it exposes abi_version , header/record size Allows firmware and runtime to reject incompatible layouts before parsing. Exact supported version and sizes; little-endian encoding declared by the platform ABI. Old UMD with new firmware, wrong packing, stale generated reader. capture_id , command ID Joins a batch to the host capture and every record to its queued command, including interleaved commands. The header capture ID identifies the epoch; every record carries a command ID that is unique within that capture. Trace from a previous capture or another queued command attached to the current result. cycle , clock rate/domain Preserves when work happened in the source clock. Monotonic inside a source and epoch; re-synchronize after reset, wrap, rate change, or power transition. Negative duration, cross-domain ordering error, DVFS-induced drift. sequence Distinguishes record order when timestamps tie and detects missing records. Monotonic modulo declared wrap behavior for each producer. Partial DMA, overwrite, malformed live-buffer ownership. event_id , kind Represents begin, end, counter or sync without device-side strings. ID dictionary is generated/versioned; every begin has a legal matching end for the same source. Unknown firmware event, unbalanced zone, decoder mismatch. source_id Names controller, tile, array, converter, DSP, DMA engine or virtual lane. Must be legal for the target descriptor and capture mode. Wrong routing, unexpected engine, overlapping use of one resource. value , flags Carries signed counters, host sync cookie, error state or event attributes. Meaning is fixed by event dictionary and unit metadata. Saturation, retry, remap, timeout, converter contention, fallback. record_count , dropped count Makes a truncated profile visibly incomplete. Count cannot exceed capacity; a nonzero drop count marks the timeline incomplete. Trace mask too broad, buffer too small, drain too late. Concurrency rule: make each device buffer single-producer so the hot emit path needs no shared atomic reservation. For live profiling, use two buffers with explicit device-owned , ready-for-host , host-owned , and free states. The device never writes a host-owned buffer; the host never decodes a device-owned buffer.

entries.heading: Correlate clocks instead of assuming they are synchronized
entries.text: For sync sample i , record host send t0[i] , device cycle c[i] , and host receive t1[i] . Approximate the host time of the device read as m[i] = t0[i] + (t1[i] - t0[i]) / 2 , then fit host_ns = reference_host_ns + ns_per_cycle * (cycle - reference_cycle) . Save maximum fit residual and round-trip time; they are evidence about alignment quality, not decoration. Use several samples Two points define a line but cannot reveal jitter. Collect samples before and after the workload, reject malformed/outlier exchanges by an explicit policy, and retain the raw samples. Fit each domain independently Controller, array sequencer, converter, DSP, and a second chip may have different clocks. Never order unrelated raw cycle values directly. Start a new epoch Reset, clock gating, DVFS, wrap, suspend/resume, firmware restart, or device replacement invalidates the old map unless the hardware contract proves continuity. Expose uncertainty Round-trip asymmetry and fit residual bound confidence in cross-domain ordering. Events closer than the uncertainty may be concurrent; do not invent a precise order.

entries.heading: Record the phases that distinguish ACiM from a digital NPU
entries.text: Layer Zones Counters and state Likely diagnosis Host/compiler Import, partition, quantize, map arrays, schedule, allocate, package, cache lookup Graph ops, fallback ops, compile cache hit, artifact bytes, mapped arrays, padding/expansion Compile overhead, unsupported op, poor utilization, excess digital fallback. Runtime/transport Open, program artifact, H2D, enqueue, doorbell, wait, interrupt, D2H, postprocess Queue depth, DMA bytes, descriptors, interrupts, retries, IOMMU faults Host serialization, PCIe/DMA limit, command starvation, completion delay. Weight lifecycle Erase/program, verify, calibration, defect scan, remap, refresh Pulses, verify failures, bad rows/columns, spare use, calibration age, drift estimate Cold-start/model-switch cost, endurance pressure, degraded capacity. Analog datapath Input encode/DAC, word-line drive, array settle/MVM, sense, ADC conversion Active arrays, input slices, output slices, converter occupancy, saturation, clipping, retries ADC/DAC bottleneck, settle-time increase, limited parallel converters, range mismatch. Digital epilogue Bit-slice reconstruction, partial-sum reduction, bias, activation, normalization, unsupported DSP op DSP/vector cycles, SRAM bytes, NoC bytes, reduction steps, fallback percentage Analog core is fast but digital accumulation or data movement sets end-to-end latency. Reliability/power Thermal throttle, recalibration, recovery, reset, power-state transition Temperature, voltage, clock, power, ECC, fault, retry, remap, reset reason Performance drift across time/PVT, intermittent stalls, instrumentation-induced power change.

entries.heading: Read the combined timeline as a causality graph
entries.text: Host gap Request to submit is long Inspect preprocessing, compile/cache miss, artifact packing, allocation, locks and queue policy. Evidence: host Tracy zones and lock timeline Dispatch gap Doorbell to device begin is long Inspect queue backlog, PCIe/MMIO, descriptor DMA, firmware dispatch, power wake and command validation. Evidence: command ID across host and device Input starve Array waits for input Inspect H2D, on-chip DMA, SRAM banking, input slicing, DAC/input-driver availability and scheduling. Evidence: bytes, DMA zone, array idle cycles Converter bound MVM is short; ADC is long Inspect ADC sharing, resolution/cycles, output slicing, saturation, range selection and converter scheduling. Evidence: ADC occupancy and conversion cycles Digital tail Analog work ends early Inspect partial-sum reduction, dequantization, activation, normalization, routing and unsupported-operator DSP fallback. Evidence: DSP cycles, SRAM/NoC bytes, fallback Accuracy tax Retries or calibration dominate Inspect program/verify, drift, remap, redundant reads, high-resolution re-read and layer precision policy. Evidence: retries, saturation, remap, profile ID

entries.heading: Make profiling depth an explicit runtime mode
entries.text: Mode Enabled evidence Use Acceptance rule off No Tracy client activity; minimal architectural counters only if always-on by design Official latency, throughput, energy and accuracy benchmark Configuration is recorded and reproducible. host Host Tracy zones, frames, plots, messages, locks and allocation Compiler, runtime, queue, callback and CPU diagnosis A/B overhead versus off is measured. device-summary Command begin/end plus aggregate DMA, array, ADC, DSP, retry and saturation counters Low-overhead continuous regression explanation Counter read cost and wrap behavior are characterized. device-scoped Selected phase begin/end records per source plus counters One operator/model bottleneck investigation Zero drops for accepted capture; buffer and clock-fit quality reported. deep-debug Fine engine/NoC/converter records, waypoints, selected data snapshots Short controlled reproduction only Resource conflicts and probe effect are documented; never used as headline performance. Budget device instrumentation before enabling it. Tenstorrent's device-profiler documentation describes finite per-core L1 storage, small inter-core clock skew, generally unsynchronized clocks across devices, annotation overhead, and resource conflicts with DPRINT and Watcher. An ACiM implementation should publish its own bytes/record, records/source, emit cycles, drain bandwidth, exclusions, and overflow behavior.

entries.heading: Measurement protocol and exit gates
entries.text: 1. Freeze Workload and machine Artifact, input, precision, firmware, clocks, power, temperature, calibration 2. Warm Separate setup Compile, program weights, calibration, allocator and cache warmup reported apart 3. Capture Diagnostic profile Selected host zones, device events, counters, correctness and IDs 4. Validate Trace quality ABI, sequence, balanced zones, zero unexpected drops, clock residual, no faults 5. Compare Measure probe effect Same run with profile off, summary, and selected scoped mode 6. Report Official evidence Uninstrumented distribution plus diagnostic explanation and archived manifests Trace completeness Every accepted command has submit, device begin/end, terminal status and output correlation; all device zones balance; record drop count is zero unless the report is explicitly marked incomplete. Clock quality Sync sample count, maximum round trip, fit residual, frequency/epoch, and cross-domain ambiguity are reported against a project-defined budget. Compare 1e9 / ns_per_cycle with the header clock rate to catch a wrong domain or unreported rate change. Numerical validity The profiled output still passes the same accuracy policy; saturation, retries, remap, fallback and calibration identity accompany the performance trace. Performance validity Warmup, sample count, p50/p95, temperature/power state and profile mode are fixed. Rich capture explains the result; the uninstrumented run supplies the claim. Working code: the included example provides opt-in host zones, the pinned Tracy CMake target, a C-compatible 32-byte device record, event IDs, overflow accounting, clock-sync samples, affine correlation, and unit tests. It intentionally stops before pretending to be a real PCIe drain or a custom Tracy protocol extension; those require the actual device memory map, timer domains, firmware ownership protocol, and profiler API. Continuous integration

entries.heading: Route cheap certainty early and expensive evidence deliberately
entries.text: TT-Metal explicitly describes its pull-request gate as a fast minimum bar and relies on broader post-commit coverage. Use the same principle with declared time budgets and changed-path routing. Developer Local loop Format, focused unit, functional simulator; target under 2 minutes Pull request Fast host gate Static, build, sanitizers, affected unit and golden tests; target under 8 minutes Selected PR Hardware smoke Changed-path route on reserved SKU; one known operation and cleanup Post-commit Integration All host tests, packaged SDK, simulator E2E, broader device matrix Nightly Depth Sweeps, models, performance, stress, sanitizer variants, multiple SKUs Release Qualification Compatibility, population/PVT, recovery, packages, reproducibility, reports Changed path Always run Selected hardware Deferred depth docs/ examples/ Format, spelling/link, code-snippet compile or execution Only when an example declares hardware Documentation build and packaged tutorial run schemas/ generated/ Regeneration diff, old/new compatibility, C++/Python/firmware round-trip Artifact-load smoke if command or ABI semantics changed Full consumer matrix and upgrade tests src/compiler/ Compiler unit, verifier, golden IR, deterministic artifact, functional reference One affected operator if lowering or command output changed Operator sweeps, model tier, compile-time and artifact-size trends src/runtime/ src/hal/ GoogleTest lifecycle, fake backend conformance, ASan/UBSan, multithread tests Open/load/submit/wait/timeout/reset smoke Concurrency, stress, recovery and multi-device tests src/driver/ src/firmware/ Build, static analysis, ABI/layout checks, firmware host model Boot, DMA/interrupt, bad descriptor, timeout and reset Soak, fault injection, power transitions and upgrade/rollback kernels/ Compile, static checks, numerical golden, simulator comparison Affected kernel correctness and health monitor Shape/precision sweep, device profiler and regression benchmark python/ bindings/ Wheel build, import, pytest unit, API and exception behavior Minimal public Python execution path Supported Python/platform matrix and framework integration models/ Manifest validation, reference/module tests, preprocessing checks Critical model tier selected by manifest Full accuracy, E2E performance, stress and fallback accounting Workflow ownership Keep routing visible instead of hiding every lane in one CI file .github/workflows/pr-fast.yml # CPU-only minimum bar .github/workflows/pr-hardware-smoke.yml # changed-path device route .github/workflows/post-commit.yml # broad integration .github/workflows/nightly-sweeps.yml # parameter and model depth .github/workflows/nightly-performance.yml # controlled runner baselines .github/workflows/release-qualification.yml # compatibility and product evidence configs/test-matrices/*.yaml # SKU, topology, marker, timeout configs/performance-thresholds/*.yaml # metric, limit, baseline, owner scripts/ci/changed_path_router.py # path -> required lane mapping scripts/ci/collect_failure_bundle.py # standard artifacts on failure Executable example: .github/workflows/acim-minimal.yml applies this pattern to the included simulator. It defines GCC Debug, Clang Debug, Clang ASan+UBSan, staged-install smoke, and pinned GoogleTest and Tracy integration jobs, plus clang-format and clang-tidy checks, whenever the example or its workflow changes. Contribution and code conduct

entries.heading: Make the engineering agreement executable and easy to find
entries.text: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md defines respectful project behavior. CONTRIBUTING.md defines how technical changes are proposed, built, tested, measured, reviewed, and merged. They solve different problems. 1. Frame Problem and evidence Reproducer, requirement, trace or measured bottleneck 2. Design Contract impact ADR for ABI, architecture, schema or ownership changes 3. Test Failure and gate Smallest deterministic test plus required deeper lanes 4. Implement Focused commits Each commit builds and preserves relevant behavior 5. Prove Correctness and metrics Reports, traces, compatibility and performance evidence 6. Review Owners and follow-through CODEOWNERS, docs, release note and monitored merge Repository file What it should answer Practical content README.md What runs, for whom, and what is the shortest successful path? Supported targets, architecture map, build/install, first simulator example, first hardware example, test commands, documentation links. CONTRIBUTING.md How does a change become trusted code? Environment, style, commit rules, test selection, PR categories, design/ADR threshold, review, performance evidence, debugging bundle. CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md How do contributors work together? Expected behavior, unacceptable behavior, reporting path, enforcement responsibility and scope. .github/CODEOWNERS Who understands and approves each contract? Named owners for schema/ABI, compiler, runtime, driver, firmware, kernels, models, CI, performance and qualification. docs/adr/ Why does a durable architecture decision exist? Context, options, decision, consequences, compatibility, migration, tests, owners and review date. PR template What changed and what proves it? Category, affected boundaries, test commands/results, hardware/SKU, accuracy, performance, docs, compatibility and rollback. Code style Format automatically; compile with strong warnings; use static analysis; keep public headers minimal; prefer typed units, enums and spans over unstructured integers and pointers. Error behavior Stable status category, subsystem, operation/graph ID, device ID, cause, recovery hint and machine-readable fields. Do not make users decode a generic timeout. Logging Structured events with severity and correlation IDs. Avoid hot-loop logging and sensitive/raw tensor dumps by default. Commit quality Descriptive subject, one coherent purpose, builds independently, relevant tests pass, generated output and docs remain synchronized. Review depth Architecture/schema changes need contract owners; kernel performance changes need correctness and profiler evidence; model claims need reproducible manifests. Definition of done Implementation, focused regression test, required lanes, observable failure path, documentation, compatibility decision, and measured acceptance evidence. Debugging playbook

entries.heading: Find the first layer that diverges, then instrument only that layer
entries.text: TT-Metal treats debug print, Watcher, Inspector, Tracy, device profiling, assertions, triage and NoC dumps as explicit tools. An ACiM repository needs equivalent host, compiler, runtime, device, numerical and performance views. 1. Reproduce Freeze the run Commit, target, artifact, calibration, seed, inputs, backend 2. Classify Name the symptom Build, compile, load, hang, wrong result, intermittent, performance 3. Compare Find first divergence Reference, ideal array, nonideal model, queued sim, RTL, silicon 4. Inspect Narrow the layer IR, artifact, buffers, queue, firmware, array, digital epilogue 5. Prove Minimize and fix Small vector, deterministic failure, explicit invariant 6. Preserve Add regression Focused test, failure bundle, docs and applicable deeper lane Host C++ Memory, lifetime, threads Debug symbols, GDB/LLDB, ASan, UBSan, TSan, core dumps, queue/event state and ownership logs. Start: failing GoogleTest under sanitizer Python and bindings API, conversion, exceptions pytest -x -vv , one node ID, faulthandler , typed boundary logs, native debugger for binding crashes. Start: installed package, one parametrization Compiler Semantics and lowering Verify after every pass, dump canonical IR, pass bisect, target legality report, mapping explanation, deterministic artifact diff. Start: first different IR operation Artifact and runtime Compatibility and execution Artifact inspector, schema/ABI versions, buffer ownership, command list, correlation IDs, queue timeline, timeout reason and cleanup trace. Start: load transcript and command ID Firmware and device Hang, fault, bad command Watcher-style health monitor, waypoints, device print, bounded asserts, command validation, register snapshot, interrupt history, safe reset and triage bundle. Start: last completed waypoint Analog numerical path Accuracy and variability Layerwise reference, ideal-array, characterized nonideality and silicon outputs; converter saturation, slice sums, calibration, remap and defect-map identity. Start: first tensor exceeding tolerance Performance Latency and utilization Same artifact and machine state, warmup, host/device timeline, DMA bytes, queue waits, array active time, ADC/DSP occupancy, stalls and thermal history. Start: phase with changed cycles or bytes Intermittent failures Race, thermal, state leak Repeat with fixed seed, record preceding tests, serialize device use, vary reset depth, track temperature, allocator state, calibration age and firmware logs. Start: smallest repetition count that fails Scale-out Route and collective failure Topology epoch, logical/physical map, route table, per-link counters, collective step, timeout ownership and before/after recovery trace. Start: first node missing progress

entries.heading: Every failure should produce one portable evidence bundle
entries.text: Proposed triage bundle Machine-readable files plus a short human summary failure-20260711T143100Z/ |-- summary.md # symptom, first divergence, next action |-- run-manifest.json # commit, command, seed, environment |-- model-manifest.json # model, inputs, preprocessing, accuracy policy |-- target-descriptor.json # SKU, revision, topology and capabilities |-- device-state.json # serial, firmware, clocks, temperature, health |-- calibration-manifest.json # calibration and defect/remap identity |-- executable.acx # exact artifact when data policy permits |-- artifact-report.json # sections, versions, hashes, requirements |-- compiler/ | |-- pipeline.txt | |-- first-before.mlir | |-- first-after.mlir | `-- mapping-report.json |-- runtime/ | |-- commands.jsonl | |-- buffers.json | `-- queue-timeline.json |-- device/ | |-- firmware.log | |-- waypoints.json | |-- fault-snapshot.json | `-- reset-transcript.json |-- numerical/ | |-- comparison.json | `-- first-divergent-tensor.bin `-- performance/ |-- counters.json `-- trace.atrace Do not enable every device tool at once. Instrumentation consumes memory, bandwidth, timing margin, or device resources and can change a race or performance result. TT-Metal documentation explicitly notes conflicts among some device debug/profiling modes; document equivalent exclusions in the new stack. Developer loop

entries.heading: Give contributors short, memorable commands for every test depth
entries.text: These are proposed command names for the blueprint, not commands currently supplied by TT-Metal. Local build and focused verification Illustrative interface to implement in scripts and presets # Configure, build and install a host-only development tree cmake --preset dev cmake --build --preset dev --parallel cmake --install build/dev --prefix build/install # Fast checks before a pull request pre-commit run --all-files ctest --preset host-unit --output-on-failure python -m pytest tests/python/unit -m "unit and not hardware" # One complete simulator path python -m pytest tests/smoke/simulator -m smoke acim-compile models/manifests/matmul.yaml -o build/matmul.acx acim-run build/matmul.acx --backend functional --trace build/matmul.atrace # Reserved hardware path python -m pytest tests/smoke/hardware -m "hardware and smoke" --device auto # Broader correctness and performance lanes python -m pytest tests/sweeps -m nightly --maxfail=20 python -m pytest tests/end_to_end -m "model_tier_1" python -m pytest tests/performance -m performance --benchmark-manifest configs/performance.yaml # Diagnostic host/device profile; compare against profile-off benchmark cmake --preset tracy cmake --build --preset tracy ctest --preset tracy # Reproduce a failure bundle acim-triage collect --run-id RUN_ID --output build/triage/RUN_ID acim-triage compare --left functional --right hardware --first-divergence A real implementation should wrap lab reservation, timeout, artifact capture and reset in fixtures or runner services so individual tests cannot leave a shared device unusable. Repository readiness workbook

entries.heading: Eleven checks before broad operator or model development
entries.text: Complete these in order.
