entries.heading: Analog CIM is a lifecycle, not only a crossbar operation
entries.text: The compiler prepares a device-aware artifact, deployment creates per-chip state, inference alternates between digital and analog engines, and maintenance feeds measured drift back into calibration. The four phases have different bottlenecks and must be measured separately. Model and compiler Programming and device state Inference data path Telemetry and recovery Offline Prepare and compile Model accuracy is converted into an explicit hardware error budget. 1 Reference model FP baseline, task metrics, calibration data 2 Quantize and harden W4/W8 baseline, clipping, HWA noise, distillation 3 Partition graph Analog MVM, SRAM, digital engine, CPU fallback 4 Physical lowering Arrays, signed encoding, slices, ranges, partial sums 5 Package artifact Commands, weight plan, calibration schema, debug map Deploy to one physical device Deployment Create device-bound state The same portable model may produce a different programming image for each chip. 1 Discover Revision, healthy arrays, converter modes, firmware ABI 2 Program weights Conductance targets, pulses, references, signed cells 3 Write and verify Retry, remap faults, reject weak cells or arrays 4 Calibrate Gain, offset, ADC range, saturation, temperature 5 Bind state Fault map, calibration version, age, provenance Run a layer or token Steady state Execute hybrid inference The analog array accelerates dense linear work; digital logic completes the operator and graph. 1 Prepare activation Digital norm, scale, clip, tile, route 2 DAC encode Static A8 range, voltage, pulse, or bit phases 3 Analog MVM Conductance products and physical column summation 4 ADC readout Integrate, sense, quantize, detect saturation 5 Digital finish High-precision partial sums, bias, residual, activation 6 Check policy Accept, repeat, use higher fidelity, or fall back Closed-loop maintenance Telemetry → health vectors → drift/saturation decision → recalibrate, refresh, remap, or digital fallback → update the device-state bundle For a 4-bit LLM, the 4-bit boundary normally belongs to weight storage, not to every arrow. A practical hybrid path is W4-like stored weights, 8-bit DAC inputs and ADC outputs, followed by higher-precision digital accumulation. The Analog Foundation Models study uses static 8-bit analog input/output boundaries, keeps attention and other digital work in FP16, and keeps the KV cache in FP16. Its result is evidence for hardware-aware adaptation, not a reason to build a 4-bit ADC and 4-bit accumulator. Inference sequence diagram

entries.heading: One request crosses five ownership boundaries
entries.text: The initialization messages run when a model is loaded. The layer loop repeats for every mapped graph region, and the recovery branch runs only when telemetry crosses a declared limit. Application Model and request Runtime Schedule and policy Digital engine Tensor preparation CIM tile DAC, array, ADC Firmware Calibration and health Initialization and device binding Load compiled model artifact Discover revision, fault map, calibration age, and precision modes Program, write-verify, and calibrate tile Return verified device state to runtime Request and repeated layer/token loop Submit inputs and latency/accuracy policy Dispatch digital pre-processing and mapped region Normalize, scale, clip, tile, and quantize activations Send activation phases, array addresses, ADC range, and fidelity mode DAC encode → analog MVM → integrate → ADC convert Return partial sums, saturation flags, and counters Accumulate, rescale, add bias/residual, and run nonlinear work Layer result and telemetry Only when error, drift, or saturation exceeds policy Request recalibration, refresh, remap, repeat, or digital fallback Return updated state and recovery result Return output with trace and health status CIM bottleneck map

entries.heading: The array MAC is fast; the system around it decides whether CIM wins
entries.text: A bottleneck is not only the slowest stage. It can be the stage that sets the accuracy ceiling, dominates energy or area, prevents useful array utilization, or makes deployment and field maintenance too costly. Accuracy ceiling Representation and analog error Programming spread, noise, nonlinear response, limited dynamic range, ADC clipping, drift, and faults. Throughput ceiling Periphery and movement DAC serialization, integration time, ADC conversion, partial sums, format changes, routing, and low utilization. Product ceiling Lifecycle and evidence Programming time, endurance, calibration, chip variation, thermal corners, validation, recovery, yield, and support. Bottleneck Where it appears What you observe First useful response Cost moved elsewhere ADC/DAC and sensing Mixed-signal periphery before and after every array MVM. Converter energy, area, latency, clipping, unused codes, or low effective precision dominate the array. Layer-aware range selection, fewer active rows, adaptive thresholds, shared converters, or selectable precision phases. More compiler state, calibration, serialization, phases, periphery, or reduced throughput. Dot-product dynamic range Column current, integrator, ADC, partial-sum path. Four-bit weights still create outputs wider than four bits; long reductions saturate or lose small contributions. Scale per layer/channel, split rows or bit slices, accumulate digitally at higher precision, and isolate outliers. Extra passes, metadata, digital additions, SRAM traffic, and conversion energy. Programming variation and hard faults NVM conductance programming and physical cells. Requested weights become distributions; stuck devices create structured, location-dependent error. Write-verify, stable ranges, differential/offset encoding, spares, defect-aware placement, or factorization. Longer load time, write energy, endurance use, redundant cells, capacity loss, or extra MVM stages. Read noise and nonlinearity Cell I-V behavior, sensing, integration, input-dependent array response. Repeated MVMs vary, and error changes with signal magnitude or activation pattern. Measured-noise HWA training, lower read voltage, references, averaging, weight expansion, or digital routing. Training cost, lower signal-to-noise ratio, repeated reads, extra cells, or lower performance. IR drop and parasitics Long wordlines/bitlines, drivers, access devices, large crossbars. The same weight behaves differently by position; larger arrays diverge from ideal matrix multiplication. Smaller subarrays, stronger/local drivers, access devices, IR-aware mapping, and active-row limits. More tiles, ADCs, routes, buffers, partial sums, area, and interconnect energy. Drift, retention, and PVT Stored conductance and analog circuits over time, voltage, and temperature. A deployment that passed qualification gradually loses margin or changes after thermal events. Reference rows, sensors, guardbands, drift-aware training, health vectors, recalibration, and selective refresh. Maintenance traffic, downtime, calibration storage, refresh energy, endurance, and fleet complexity. Activation delivery Input buffers, DACs, pulse/bit phases, routing to rows. The array waits for serialized multibit activations or consumes energy repeatedly charging lines. Local SRAM, broadcast/reuse, pulse-width encoding, phase overlap, sparsity, and input pruning. Larger buffers and control, restricted formats, model changes, or more difficult scheduling. Partial sums and output movement Across subarrays, tiles, chips, SRAM, NoC, and host boundaries. Peak macro TOPS/W looks high while end-to-end latency and energy are dominated by reduction and transport. Local accumulation, fusion, hierarchy-aware tiling, route scheduling, and keeping dependent work near the tile. Digital area, SRAM capacity, synchronization, compiler complexity, and less flexible placement. Mapping and utilization Mismatch between model shapes and fixed physical rows, columns, capacity, and healthy arrays. Padded rows, fragmented weights, replicated tensors, idle columns, load imbalance, or insufficient on-chip capacity. Shape-aware packing, replication only when beneficial, structured sparsity, heterogeneous placement, and utilization-aware cost models. Compilation search time, model restrictions, duplicated storage, or lower theoretical density. Unsupported and sensitive operations Softmax, normalization, nonlinearities, dynamic attention, KV cache, control, and numerically fragile layers. Frequent analog/digital boundaries erase gains or low precision degrades task accuracy. Digital/SRAM engines, operator fusion, mixed precision, sensitivity-based partitioning, and a clean fallback ABI. More silicon, duplicated capabilities, conversions, scheduling dependencies, and software surface area. Programming and model updates Cold start, model replacement, fine-tuning, recovery, and fleet rollout. Slow high-voltage writes, erase granularity, endurance limits, and long deployment windows. Weight-stationary serving, immutable analog regions, transactional programming, staged rollout, and digital adapters. Reduced update flexibility, extra digital memory, operational tooling, rollback storage, and version management. Calibration and validation Manufacturing, deployment, runtime maintenance, and product qualification. Per-chip tuning and broad corner testing cost more than the steady-state kernel and delay release. Automated calibration, compact device-state bundles, representative health vectors, correlation ladders, and explicit evidence levels. Telemetry, storage, test time, simulator ownership, production infrastructure, and support cost. Critical-path rule Optimize in this order: prevent saturation and illegal mappings, meet task accuracy, remove converter and movement stalls, improve utilization, then reduce calibration and lifecycle cost. Optimizing the crossbar MAC first can improve a number that is not limiting the product. Architecture taxonomy

entries.heading: "NPU on RAM" hides several fundamentally different machines
entries.text: The memory device determines how a weight is stored. The compute domain determines how products are formed and accumulated. Those choices set the failure mechanisms that software must model. Architecture Weight and compute Main strength Dominant problems Software consequence Analog SRAM CIM Digital bits in 6T/8T/9T cells gate current or redistribute charge on bitlines and capacitors. Mature CMOS, fast writes, high endurance, no conductance drift. Large cell area, volatility, model-load energy, mismatch, charge leakage, PVT sensitivity, ADC precision. Bit slicing, ADC/row-count selection, PVT-aware calibration, frequent weight loading, and memory-capacity planning. RRAM / memristor crossbar Conductance stores a multilevel weight; voltage or pulse width times conductance creates current; columns sum by physics. Dense non-volatile weights, high parallelism, compact 1T1R arrays. Stochastic programming, stuck cells, nonlinear I-V, relaxation, IR drop, read noise, endurance, limited conductance range. Write-verify, defect maps, differential or offset encoding, hardware-aware training, chip-in-loop tuning, and IR-aware placement. PCM crossbar Phase state controls conductance; pulse-width inputs integrate current into capacitors before time/digital conversion. Dense backend-integrated weight storage and proven multicore/multichip demonstrations. Programming error, conductance drift, read noise, asymmetry, slow/energy-heavy writes, weight-stationary execution. Multi-device weight expansion, optimized programming, HWA training, per-column calibration, recalibration, and strict weight lifecycle. Embedded-flash CIM Floating-gate or charge-trap threshold stores an analog weight; read currents perform dense MVM. Mature non-volatile storage, long retention, high density, useful for fixed inference weights. High-voltage and slow programming, limited endurance, erase granularity, charge variation, asymmetric updates. Offline compilation, infrequent programming, verify-and-calibrate deployment, immutable-weight artifacts, and digital fallback. Heterogeneous mixed CIM Memristor/PCM handles tolerant dense work; SRAM or digital units handle sensitive layers, kernels, reductions, and control. Accuracy and flexibility without forcing every operation through the weakest analog regime. Partitioning, format conversion, duplicated storage, routing, scheduling, wakeup, and a larger control plane. Sensitivity analysis, layer/kernel placement, mixed INT/FP formats, conversion-aware scheduling, and end-to-end cost modeling. Digital CIM is a separate escape route. It can provide exact low-bit arithmetic inside SRAM, RRAM, or MRAM, avoiding analog error at the cost of more bit-level operations, addition circuitry, and often lower density or energy advantage. The 2025 mixed processor uses this principle: route sensitive work to lossless SRAM-CIM or tiny digital units instead of demanding that memristor CIM become exact. Primary-paper solution ledger

entries.heading: What each architecture changed, and what remained outside the claim
entries.text: Filter by memory or contribution. "Measured" does not always mean a complete end-to-end product; the boundary is stated on each card. All papers RRAM PCM SRAM Mixed Software Component Measured SRAM macro

entries.heading: 22-nm charge-domain SRAM CIM
entries.text: Problem: multibit analog SRAM normally loses precision through mismatch, parasitics, noise, and converter cost. Hardware: a passive C-2C charge ladder, 9T SRAM, local weight multiplexing, and an 8-bit MAC design target linearity across PVT. Software: circuit and system analysis selects precision and validates the analog error budget; weights remain ordinary digital SRAM bits. Evidence: 32.2 TOPS/W peak, less than 0.5% MVM error, and less than 1% measured error deviation across PVT. Boundary: macro evidence, not a full model-to-runtime system; SRAM remains volatile and area intensive. Fully measured datasets

entries.heading: NeuRRAM RRAM chip
entries.text: Problem: wire/driver drop, programming resolution, relaxation, coupling, and limited ADC range made software-only simulation optimistic. Hardware: 48 reconfigurable cores, transposable dataflow, differential signed weights, and voltage-mode neuron sensing improve utilization and dynamic range. Software: model-driven calibration, measured-noise training, continuous analog programming, and progressive chip-in-loop fine-tuning. Evidence: complete hardware runs reached 99.0% MNIST, 85.7% CIFAR-10, and 84.7% Google speech-command accuracy. Boundary: FPGA supplied intermediate buffers and partial sums; peak array efficiency excludes intermediate transfer. Measured programming method

entries.heading: Gradient descent-based PCM programming
entries.text: Problem: cell-wise write-verify depends on precise low-current reads and can miss array nonlinearities that determine the actual MVM result. Hardware: two 14-nm PCM cores, each with a 256 x 256 array, execute random-probe MVMs during deployment calibration. Software: gradient descent minimizes measured MVM error and adjusts programming pulses, even when the best physical conductances differ from nominal weight targets. Evidence: a scaled ResNet-9 hardware run improved from 84.75% to 86.01% CIFAR-10 accuracy; the programming-error advantage persisted for 24 hours. Boundary: digital gradient calculation and non-MVM work remained off-array; repeated writes cost time and endurance, and each method received one complete inference run. Integrated mixed-signal chip

entries.heading: 64-core PCM inference chip
entries.text: Problem: an analog tile alone cannot execute activations, communication, convolution support, or complete LSTM layers. Hardware: 64 PCM AIMC cores, an on-chip communication network, and digital activation/processing units form a complete mixed-signal data path. Software: mapping and precision modes select one-phase high-throughput or four-phase high-precision MVM execution. Evidence: near-software accuracy on ResNet and LSTM, with 2.48 TOPS/W high-precision or 9.76 TOPS/W low-precision modes. Boundary: accuracy and efficiency still depend on model mapping, device programming, and the selected precision mode. End-to-end KWS; hybrid RNNT

entries.heading: PCM speech recognition and transcription chip
entries.text: Problem: large speech models amplify programming error, offset, saturation, and cross-tile movement; NVM writes are slow and finite-endurance. Hardware: 34-tile chips, four PCM devices per cell, an AB differential method, bias rows, pulse-duration routing, and five chips for RNNT. Software: HWA training and input pruning for KWS; calibration and per-column rescaling; weight expansion for the 45-million-weight RNNT. Evidence: KWS measured 86.14% versus 86.75%; RNNT measured 9.258% WER versus 7.452% FP baseline. Boundary: RNNT intermediate data and auxiliary computation used an x86 host; the chip lacked product digital cores and SRAM. Measured heterogeneous processor

entries.heading: Memristor, SRAM, and digital mixed CIM
entries.text: Problem: memristor CIM is dense but variation sensitive; lossless SRAM CIM is accurate but large and volatile. Hardware: memristor-CIM, SRAM-CIM, tiny digital units, and INT/FP modes coexist on one edge processor. Software: layer- and kernel-granular sensitivity analysis partitions work by error tolerance and format requirements. Evidence: less than 0.45% degradation with 40.91 TFLOPS/W on ResNet-20/CIFAR-100 and 28.63 TFLOPS/W on MobileNet-v2/ImageNet. Boundary: accuracy is preserved by heterogeneous routing, not by eliminating analog variation. Transformer weight layers in hardware

entries.heading: ALBERT on a 14-nm PCM chip
entries.text: Problem: transformer projections have task-dependent sensitivity, shared weights see different activation distributions, and PCM drifts with time. Hardware: 35 million PCM devices, 34 tiles, multi-device weight encoding, and a 2D mesh store all 7.1 million unique ALBERT weights. Software: task-specific HWA noise fine-tuning, mapping, per-use column scale/offset calibration, and periodic recalibration. Evidence: HWA improved average measured GLUE accuracy by 4.4%; recalibration reduced long-term drift loss. Boundary: attention, GELU, softmax, layer normalization, pooling, and classification ran in software; some tasks used representative subsets. Measured multi-chip full stack

entries.heading: OpenCIMTC full-stack memristor system
entries.text: Problem: fixed hardware dataflow, manual placement, and manual parameter tuning prevent diverse models from deploying reliably. Hardware: eight flexible memristor chips plus FPGA/CPU control support signed inputs/weights, multiple mappings, and model-dependent dataflows. Software: CIM IR, compiler, simulator, optimizer, automatic placement, post-deployment training, and inference-time parameter search. Evidence: six models across four tasks ran automatically; optimizations improved inference accuracy by 3.32% to 9.45%. Boundary: a research platform with FPGA control, but unusually strong evidence for an actual compiler-optimizer-hardware loop. Measured converter devices; system modeling

entries.heading: Adaptive memristor ADC
entries.text: Problem: uniform low-bit ADCs waste codes on layer-specific output distributions; high-bit ADCs dominate area and energy. Hardware: analog-CAM quantization cells implement programmable overlapping thresholds, one-step conversion, recalibration, and paired-ADC super-resolution. Software: layer statistics and a constrained Lloyd-Max optimization choose thresholds; program-and-verify maps them to conductance. Evidence: fabricated 8x8 devices support the model; 5-bit VGG8 reached 89.55% under measured variation and system studies report lower ADC overhead. Boundary: not a complete fabricated CIM accelerator; Q-cell count grows exponentially at high resolution. Measured matrix and wireless prototypes

entries.heading: Fault-free analogue computing
entries.text: Problem: stuck-on/off cells create structured errors that redundancy or retraining may not remove efficiently. Hardware: two cascaded programmable submatrices and optional compensation layers implement an indirect target matrix and eliminate differential pairs. Software: gradient-based hardware-aware matrix decomposition uses the measured defect map and hardware constraints. Evidence: over 99.999% DFT cosine similarity at 39% device faults and a 56-fold wireless bit-error-rate reduction. Boundary: solves static representation faults for tested matrices; random read noise, ADC error, drift, nonlinear arrays, and complete DNN accuracy remain. Large-model simulation study

entries.heading: Hardware-aware training across model families
entries.text: Problem: approximate MVM includes nonlinear and nondeterministic errors that ordinary FP or quantized training never sees. Hardware abstraction: a realistic crossbar model includes weight, input, output, converter, and circuit nonidealities. Software: retraining injects the target error model and searches robust operating points for CNNs, recurrent networks, and transformers. Evidence: many evaluated models recovered floating-point iso-accuracy in simulation; input/output noise was often more damaging than weight noise. Boundary: simulation evidence depends on model fidelity and does not replace silicon population and lifetime testing. June 2026 preprint and modeled GPT-2 study

entries.heading: Unified heterogeneous AIMC mapping workflow
entries.text: Problem: analog/digital assignment is combinatorial, existing methods use incompatible assumptions, and coarse first/last-layer rules do not capture decoder-transformer sensitivity. Hardware abstraction: PCM-calibrated noise, 512 x 512 tiling, roughly 8-bit converters, digital compute units, memory, interconnect, and maintenance costs. Software: characterize hardware, profile projection sensitivity, optimize architecture-aware mapping, then validate the complete system. Evidence: four of 49 GPT-2-small projections dominated marginal sensitivity; 40 had modeled perplexity increase below 3 and became analog candidates. Boundary: only workflow stages 1-2 were executed; no joint mapping, measured chip, runtime drift response, or end-to-end energy and latency result was produced. Deep read 1 | measured IBM PCM hardware

entries.heading: Program the measured function, not each cell in isolation
entries.text: This IEDM paper is the stronger of the two additions because it evaluates the method on fabricated 14-nm PCM cores. Its central lesson belongs in deployment firmware and the compiler/runtime contract. New idea: conventional write-verify tries to make every read conductance equal its nominal target. Gradient descent-based programming instead minimizes the error of the complete on-chip MVM. It can intentionally leave individual readout weights farther from their nominal values when that compensates peripheral nonlinearity and improves the function the application actually consumes. 1. Initialize Roughly program the target matrix with a short iterative sequence or one-shot pulses. 2. Probe Generate synthetic random vectors and execute a batch of MVMs on the physical array; no application dataset is required. 3. Measure loss Compare measured outputs with the ideal target-matrix outputs and minimize normalized MVM error rather than individual-cell error. 4. Update pulses Compute the gradient digitally, convert it into bounded SET/RESET pulse changes, program selected cells, and repeat. 2 fabricated PCM cores 14-nm, measured 256 x 256 unit cells per core four PCM devices per signed cell 84.75% to 86.01% CIFAR-10 accuracy one scaled ResNet-9 run per method 24 h drift observation programming-error advantage retained

entries.heading: What the result establishes
entries.text: Accurate single-device reads are not required when the array can execute MVM probes during programming. Function-level optimization can absorb small static nonlinearities that cell-wise conductance matching ignores. Random inputs generalized across tested input distributions and sparsity levels. Batch sizes of at least 64 beat the baseline; 256 or more performed best in the reported sweep.

entries.heading: What remains unresolved
entries.text: Digital gradient computation scales with probe batch, rows, and columns and adds deployment time. Repeated programming pulses consume energy and endurance; the paper does not provide a product lifetime budget. The experiment does not remove random read noise, ADC energy, saturation, PVT variation, or unsupported digital operators. One network and one complete inference run per programming method are not population-level qualification. IEEE publication arXiv manuscript ResearchGate record Deep read 2 | June 2026 architecture preprint

entries.heading: Profile transformer projections before searching the analog/digital mapping
entries.text: This paper is current and directly relevant to the software stack, but its GPT-2 result is modeled rather than measured. The useful contribution is a disciplined workflow and a finer mapping granularity. New idea: a decoder transformer should not be mapped by a blanket first/last-layer rule or by assigning an entire block to one engine. Sensitivity can differ sharply among Q/K/V, attention-output, and FFN projections in the same block. Projection-level profiling first reduces the search space, after which a hardware-specific optimizer can choose the actual analog/digital assignment. 1. Characterize Hardware Tiles, ADC/DAC, noise, digital units, memory, interconnect, drift 2. Profile Model sensitivity Perturb one projection, repeat noise trials, rank accuracy or perplexity loss 3. Map Architecture-aware search Assign analog/digital paths and produce an accuracy-energy-latency Pareto set 4. Validate Complete system Measure task accuracy, analog coverage, latency, energy, and search cost 49 GPT-2 projections tested one at a time 4 dominant projections localized modeled sensitivity 40 / 49 analog candidates about 82% under a delta-perplexity threshold of 3 490 forward passes 49 projections x 10 noise realizations

entries.heading: What is genuinely useful
entries.text: The four-stage workflow prevents sensitivity profiling from being confused with final system mapping. GPT-2 sensitivity was concentrated, and the largest outlier was an internal block-0 attention-output projection. Projection granularity aligns with transformer datapaths while avoiding weight-level routing complexity. The profile can seed heuristic, analytical, or trainable Stage 3 mapping algorithms.

entries.heading: What must happen next
entries.text: Run Stage 3 jointly: one-at-a-time perturbation does not capture interacting errors from many analog projections. Run Stage 4 on a concrete accelerator and count converters, KV cache, memory, communication, latency, and energy. Validate the ranking on silicon, across PCM, ReRAM, and SRAM models, and after time-dependent drift. Repeat on larger decoder models; GPT-2-small does not prove that the same four projections dominate at scale. arXiv manuscript ResearchGate record Failure-to-solution explorer

entries.heading: Place each fix at the cheapest layer that can actually remove the error
entries.text: 1 Programming and faults Targets, spread, stuck cells 2 Read error Noise and nonlinearity 3 Converters Range and quantization 4 Array scaling IR drop and utilization 5 Drift and PVT Time, chip, temperature 6 System execution Unsupported work and movement Static and programmed state

entries.heading: The written conductance is not the requested weight
entries.text: Hardware layer Iterative write-verify, array-level random-probe MVMs, multi-device weights, reference cells, spare rows/columns, and defect characterization. Compiler and training Differential/offset encoding, defect-aware placement, function-level programming loss, optimized pulse targets, post-deployment training, and matrix factorization for severe static faults. Runtime Bind the executable to a device fault map, run cell-wise verification or gradient-based MVM calibration, reject weak arrays, and preserve programming provenance. Tradeoff More devices, probes, digital optimization, programming pulses, artifact state, deployment time, and endurance consumption. Stochastic and input dependent

entries.heading: The same MVM produces a distribution, not an exact value
entries.text: Hardware layer Low-noise sensing, linear read voltage, voltage-mode readout, differential/AB methods, averaging, integration-time control, and weight expansion. Training layer Inject measured weight, input, output, and activation noise; clip outliers; tune noise scale per task; use chip-in-loop data when the model is incomplete. Runtime Monitor repeated-read variance and saturation, select a precision mode, and route sensitive regions to SRAM or digital units. Tradeoff Longer latency, duplicated weights, lower signal range, more digital work, and model-specific retraining. Peripheral bottleneck

entries.heading: ADC and DAC choices can erase the array advantage
entries.text: Hardware layer Shared or per-column converters, pulse-width inputs, multiple precision phases, voltage-mode normalization, programmable thresholds, bias rows, and converter recalibration. Compiler layer Profile layer/channel distributions, assign ranges and bit widths, split outliers, choose row activation count, and program adaptive thresholds. Training layer Quantization-aware training includes actual clipping, ADC codebook, saturation, offset, and output noise. Tradeoff High resolution costs area and energy; low resolution costs accuracy; adaptive flash-like ADCs can scale exponentially in threshold cells. Physical scale and mapping

entries.heading: Large ideal crossbars become nonuniform physical networks
entries.text: Hardware layer Smaller subarrays, access devices, stronger drivers, local ADCs, hierarchical routing, local SRAM, and balanced tile interfaces. Compiler layer IR-drop-aware placement, physical row/column tiling, partial-sum planning, utilization-aware packing, replication, and communication scheduling. Model layer Prune unimportant inputs, exploit structured sparsity, and choose architectures whose shapes pack efficiently. Tradeoff More tiles, converters, buffers, routing, partial sums, and data movement reduce peak density and TOPS/W. Lifecycle error

entries.heading: A correct deployment can become incorrect with time and temperature
entries.text: Hardware layer Reference/bias rows, temperature sensors, stable operating ranges, refresh support, redundant state, and better retention devices. Training and compiler Drift-aware noise models, time-corner training, guardbands, per-use calibration metadata, and refresh/reprogram policy in the artifact. Runtime Store per-chip scale/offset and age, run health vectors, recalibrate, selectively refresh, fall back, and record every state transition. Tradeoff Calibration data, test time, downtime, maintenance energy, write endurance, and fleet-management complexity. End-to-end boundary

entries.heading: An analog MVM tile is not a complete NPU
entries.text: Hardware layer Digital processing units, SRAM buffers, NoC, DMA, reductions, activation units, control processors, queues, trace, and reset. Compiler layer Capability partitioning, analog/digital placement, fusion, scheduling, memory planning, format conversion, fallback, and a versioned executable artifact. Runtime layer Programming, calibration, queues, synchronization, telemetry, device-specific state, recovery, and compatibility negotiation. Tradeoff Real system efficiency must count auxiliary compute, data movement, utilization, programming, calibration, host work, and idle power. Hardware solution hierarchy

entries.heading: Fix physical errors locally, then expose the residual error as a contract
entries.text: Layer 1 Material and memory cell Improve linearity, symmetry, conductance window, programming resolution, retention, endurance, variability, and CMOS compatibility. Produces: characterized device distributions and legal operating ranges. Layer 2 Array and access Use 1T1R/2T2R selection, smaller subarrays, write-verify, differential/offset encoding, spares, references, and fault maps. Produces: physical array capabilities and defects. Layer 3 Mixed-signal periphery Design DAC/input encoding, integration, sensing, ADCs, gain/offset control, saturation detection, and precision modes together. Produces: calibrated numeric and energy models. Layer 4 Tile and data path Add local SRAM, partial-sum logic, digital activations, routing, control, counters, trace, and a programmable command model. Produces: schedulable engines with observable behavior. Layer 5 SoC and product Integrate DMA, NoC, firmware, driver, power/thermal control, security, reset, test, binning, field calibration, and update policy. Produces: a supportable device rather than a laboratory macro. Software solution stack

entries.heading: Make measured analog behavior a first-class compilation input
entries.text: A normal NPU stack assumes deterministic instructions. An Analog CIM stack also consumes a target profile, nonideality model, per-chip state, and declared numerical tolerance. 1. Characterize Target profile Devices, arrays, converters, faults, PVT, time, energy 2. Harden HWA training Quantization, noise, drift, clipping, sensitivity, chip-in-loop 3. Partition Graph compiler Analog, SRAM, digital, CPU, rejection, conversion cost 4. Map Physical lowering Arrays, signed encoding, slices, ADC range, faults, schedule 5. Package Executable artifact Code, weights, programming plan, calibration schema, debug map 6. Deploy Runtime Write-verify or MVM-optimize, calibrate, bind state, execute, trace, recover 7. Maintain Fleet loop Health vectors, drift, refresh, fallback, rollback, evidence Implementation boundary: this page explains why each hardware/software mechanism is needed. The Analog CIM SDK and compiler guide specifies the concrete libraries, calibration artifacts, C ABI, queues and events, MLIR passes, artifact schema, simulator/HAL backends, framework adapters, and first runnable MatMul slice.

entries.heading: Training and model preparation
entries.text: Start from a quantized digital baseline so analog loss is not confused with quantization loss. Inject measured weight, input, output, ADC, drift, and PVT distributions at the correct graph locations. Search the noise scale instead of assuming more noise always improves robustness. Use per-channel scaling, clipping, outlier splitting, distillation, and sensitivity analysis. Reserve chip-in-loop tuning for residual behavior the simulator cannot model accurately.

entries.heading: Compiler and optimizer
entries.text: Legalize only operators whose numeric and physical contracts the target can satisfy. Partition sensitive layers or kernels to SRAM/digital units and account for conversion overhead. Lower logical tensors into signed cells, bit slices, physical arrays, converter modes, routes, and partial sums. Use defect-, IR-drop-, saturation-, endurance-, and calibration-aware placement and scheduling. Emit a reproducible report explaining every fallback and predicted error contribution.

entries.heading: Runtime, firmware, and driver
entries.text: Discover device revision, array health, fault map, calibration age, firmware ABI, and precision modes. Program weights transactionally, then select cell-wise write-verify or random-probe MVM optimization from the target capability and deployment budget. Record programming loss, iteration count, pulse count, endurance use, and the final measured operator state. Store per-chip scale, offset, fault, temperature, age, and refresh data separately from portable model content. Monitor saturation, read variance, temperature, drift, timeouts, and device loss during execution. Support recalibration, selective refresh, remapping, digital fallback, rollback, quarantine, and replacement devices.

entries.heading: Simulator and validation
entries.text: Maintain FP32, digital-quantized, ideal-array, nonideality, cycle-model, RTL, and silicon references. Use measured distributions and preserve correlation IDs, model/artifact hashes, calibration version, and device state. Report first divergent layer, error distributions, tails, saturation, and task accuracy instead of one average MVM error. Correlate latency, energy, utilization, converter activity, movement, programming, calibration, and fallback. Qualify across chips, process, voltage, temperature, aging, faults, workloads, and time. The June 2026 Nature Electronics result

entries.heading: "Fault-free" changes representation, not the laws of analog hardware
What the paper convincingly solves
entries.text: A target matrix can be factored into two adjustable matrices that route around severe stuck-device maps. The representation can eliminate conventional differential pairs and improve density for tested matrices. Gradient-based optimization can incorporate circuit/device constraints before programming. Measured DFT and wireless demonstrations show that the static-fault technique is real.

entries.heading: What remains unsolved
entries.text: Random read noise, ADC/DAC error, input-dependent nonlinearity, IR drop, coupling, temperature, and drift. End-to-end DNN accuracy, unsupported operators, model partitioning, scheduling, runtime, and field maintenance. The cost of the second MVM, analog bridge, compensation layers, calibration, and intermediate dynamic range for every workload. Population-level yield, long-term retention, endurance, and production qualification. Compiler implication: treat matrix factorization as an optional physical-lowering strategy. It consumes a measured fault map and emits two array programs plus bridge/compensation configuration. The cost model must compare it with spares, remapping, differential encoding, retraining, digital fallback, and replacing the device. The method is valuable precisely because its claim is narrower than "analog is exact." Solution selection matrix

entries.heading: Choose mitigations by error type, not by fashion
entries.text: Observed failure First hardware response First software response Escalation Random programming spread Closed-loop write-verify, random-probe MVM support, and a stable conductance range. Function-level programming optimization plus HWA training. Multi-device expansion, remap, or digital placement. Many stuck devices Characterize fault map; spares where cheap. Defect-aware placement or adaptive matrix factorization. Reject/quarantine array when extra MVM stages lose value. ADC saturation or code waste Gain/offset control, precision modes, adaptive thresholds. Representative calibration, per-layer range, clipping, outlier split. More phases/bits or move the region to digital compute. Read noise and nonlinear error Linear read region, better sensing, differential/AB, references. Measured-noise HWA training and sensitivity routing. Average, expand weights, chip-in-loop tune, or fall back. IR drop and position bias Smaller arrays, access devices, stronger/local periphery. IR-aware mapping, tiling, partial-sum and route planning. Reduce active rows or redesign the tile. Drift over time Reference rows, sensors, refresh/reprogram capability. Drift-aware training, calibration metadata, guardbands. Recalibrate, selectively refresh, remap, or replace. Sensitive model region Provide SRAM/digital units and clean conversion paths. Layer/kernel sensitivity partition and mixed precision. Change model architecture or reject target deployment. Poor application efficiency Local SRAM, DPU, NoC, overlap, counters, power control. Fusion, packing, scheduling, memory planning, pipeline balancing. Redesign dataflow; peak macro TOPS/W is not the product metric. Implementation contracts

entries.heading: Six artifacts make the co-design reproducible
entries.text: 01 Target profile Array geometry, formats, converters, precision modes, memory, digital units, command ABI, and legal operating ranges. 02 Nonideality model Measured programming, read, drift, PVT, parasitic, ADC, saturation, correlation, and uncertainty distributions. 03 Mapping report Partition, physical arrays, signed encoding, slices, ranges, fault decisions, schedule, movement, and predicted error. 04 Executable artifact Code, constants, programming plan, calibration schema, compatibility, hashes, provenance, and source-to-command debug map. 05 Device state bundle Per-chip faults, programmed state, scale/offset, temperature, calibration age, drift, health, refresh, and replacement history. 06 Qualification report Task accuracy, first divergence, latency, energy, utilization, programming/calibration cost, population, corners, and lifetime. Evidence ladder

entries.heading: Do not let a component result silently become a product claim
entries.text: Level 1 Device Conductance states, write error, noise, drift, endurance, retention, PVT Level 2 Macro MVM error, ADC/DAC, parasitics, array size, utilization, energy and area Level 3 Tile / chip Digital units, routing, buffers, synchronization, calibration, trace, faults Level 4 Application Complete dataset, named baseline, hardware boundary, host work, end-to-end metrics Level 5 Product Chip population, temperature, age, field updates, recovery, security, yield, cost The adaptive ADC paper contains measured memristor devices and converter characterization, then model and system evaluation under measured variation. The HWA training paper is a broad simulation study. NeuRRAM reports complete hardware-measured datasets. ALBERT maps the fully connected weights to hardware but keeps attention and activation work in software. These are all useful results, but they occupy different rungs. Study and portfolio labs

entries.heading: iHW's ACiM Patent Stack: What It Solves and What It Does Not
entries.text: Read patent claims critically and connect proposed Analog CIM techniques to implementable architecture. Patent deep read | research snapshot 2026-07-11 iHW's ACiM Patent Stack: What It Solves and What It Does Not Intelligent HW's granted hybrid-computing patent attacks a real analog-memory problem: asking one physical cell to hold many precise conductance levels. Its answer is to build one logical weight from simpler digits, accumulate each positional slice in analog, then reconstruct precision digitally. Later applications add adaptive converter range, grouped quantization, and signed-current cancellation. Together they form a credible accuracy architecture, but they are not public proof that end-to-end analog error is solved. Read the verdict Trace the core patent Audit the accuracy budget Map it into software Core US grant US 12,586,636 B2, granted March 24, 2026 Main mechanism Positional digit slices plus digital reconstruction Supporting layer Adaptive ADC, grouped scales, signed cancellation Research verdict Partial mitigation; system-level proof remains open Evidence boundary

entries.heading: A real granted architecture claim is not the same as a verified product result
entries.text: Best-supported conclusion: iHW has a technically meaningful way to avoid depending on a single highly precise multilevel memory cell. The granted architecture can make logical weight encoding more controllable, while the newer applications address converter range, quantization range, and signed-weight peripheral cost. Public records still do not establish full-model accuracy, yield, energy, latency, or lifetime behavior across production chips. Confirmed legal record The core US patent is active US 12,586,636 B2 was granted on March 24, 2026. Its independent claims cover a particular hybrid line-significance and reconstruction architecture, not every form of bit-sliced CIM. Company-originated claim 8-bit ACiM silicon and MobileNet An iHW recruiting page claims a world-first 8-bit-weight ACiM silicon verification and MobileNet demonstration. No public independent benchmark methodology accompanies that statement. Still unproven publicly Production accuracy and efficiency The patent record does not report complete datasets, chip populations, PVT corners, aging, yield, full-chip energy, or end-to-end latency. Patent or official record Company disclosure Engineering interpretation

entries.heading: Read "8-bit" carefully
entries.text: In the core patent, an 8-bit logical weight may be reconstructed from eight robust binary slices or from fewer multi-bit slices. It does not require one physical cell to reproduce 256 ideal conductance states. Logical precision, converter precision, analog effective precision, and end-task accuracy are four different quantities and should never be reported as if they were interchangeable. Patent landscape

entries.heading: One granted representation architecture plus a surrounding accuracy stack
entries.text: Status below is the US public-record status at this research snapshot. A pending application describes a proposed invention; it must not be presented as a granted right or as proof that the mechanism ships in silicon. Document Status Problem addressed Proposed mechanism Evidence limit US 12,586,636 B2 Hybrid computing method and neuromorphic system Granted 2026-03-24 Multilevel-cell nonlinearity, poor repeatability, and unary-cell density cost Represent a logical weight as positional digits; perform analog accumulation per slice; digitally shift, scale, and add Architecture claims, not a public full-chip benchmark US 2025/0348726 A1 High-accuracy analog computing Pending application ADC saturation or wasted resolution across wide output-current ranges Classify current magnitude and select a matching I-V conversion or ADC range No public product implementation or end-to-end cost result US 2025/0348716 A1 Weight quantization for analog computing Pending application Accuracy loss when one quantization scale covers a layer with uneven channel ranges Use multiple quantization groups and dequantize each group with its own scale Compiler policy and measured model benefit are not public US 2026/0023963 A1 Negative-weight analog computing unit Pending application Peripheral duplication for positive and negative weight paths Alternate positive and negative split-gate cells on one bitline so currents cancel before conversion Claims fewer ADCs; cancellation accuracy and residual range remain design risks US 2026/0024581 A1 Negative-weight array arrangement Pending application ADC count and positive/negative read overhead Rearrange control-line directions and alternate paired read modes One-quarter-ADC claim is an application claim, not a measured product result US 12,268,104 B2 Chalcogenide memory-cell composition and operation Granted 2025-04-01 Threshold drift, read window, stable composition, and manufacturability Material composition plus initialization and read techniques A separate device path; it does not prove the flash ACiM product uses this material Core patent mechanism

entries.heading: Trade one fragile analog level for several simpler positional digits
entries.text: The architecture is hybrid by construction. Memory cells provide parallel analog multiply-accumulate work; converters and digital logic recover the significance of each slice. 1. Quantize Logical weight Choose a signed fixed-point or integer representation. 2. Decompose Weight digits Split the value into binary or mixed-radix digits. 3. Program Cells and lines Map each digit to a cell state and a positional output line. 4. Accumulate Analog MVM Apply encoded inputs and sum current independently per slice. 5. Convert ADC per slice Digitize each output-line current in a suitable range. 6. Rebuild Shift and add Scale by positional significance, combine signs, and accumulate. Conventional pressure point

entries.heading: One cell, many conductance levels
entries.text: A dense direct mapping asks each device to separate many analog states despite program variation, read noise, nonlinear response, drift, temperature, aging, and process spread. More nominal bits do not automatically produce the same number of effective bits. Patent response

entries.heading: Several cells or lines, fewer states each
entries.text: Each slice can use a small, robust state set, including on/off. Positional significance carries the high precision, and deterministic digital arithmetic reconstructs the logical value after conversion. Abstracted computation Notation distilled from the patent architecture W[i,j] = sum_k d[i,j,k] * R[k] I[k,j] ~= alpha * sum_i X[i] * d[i,j,k] Y[j] = sum_k R[k] * ADC(I[k,j]) d[i,j,k] digit stored in a physical memory state R[k] positional significance, such as 1, 2, 4, 8 ... I[k,j] analog output current for significance slice k

entries.heading: Worked example from the disclosed idea
entries.text: If three digit-line currents convert to 9, 1, and 3, and their positional weights are 1, 2, and 4, digital reconstruction produces 9 x 1 + 1 x 2 + 3 x 4 = 23 . The analog array need not create one current that directly encodes 23 with a single precise cell state. Reliability policy

entries.heading: Mixed radix lets significance determine how much cell reliability to buy
entries.text: Low significance Dense storage Lower-order digits may tolerate denser MLC, TLC, or QLC states because their errors contribute less to the final value. Middle digits Balanced mapping Choose radix and cell state count from measured programming spread, ADC range, and array cost. High significance Robust storage Use fewer levels or SLC-like states because an error is multiplied by a larger positional weight. Positive path Signed magnitude Map positive contributions onto a matched physical or logical path. Negative path Differential term Subtract a negative path digitally or cancel paired currents before the ADC. Digital boundary Exact recombination Shifts, scales, sign handling, and accumulation are deterministic after conversion. Residual risk MSB amplification A high-significance slice error is also amplified, so robust storage and converter headroom matter most there. The cost does not disappear. More slices can require more cells, output lines, ADC phases, routing, input cycles, digital shift-add work, and calibration metadata. Fewer slices save area and cycles but reintroduce multilevel-cell variability. The engineering problem becomes an explicit accuracy-area-energy-latency tradeoff. Supporting inventions

entries.heading: The later applications target costs left around digit-sliced representation
entries.text: Pending application

entries.heading: Adaptive output and ADC range
entries.text: A multiplexer selects an output current, a grading step estimates its magnitude, and the circuit selects a matching I-V resistance/capacitance, ADC reference, or oscillator capacitance. Benefit: reduce saturation on large sums and avoid wasting ADC codes on small sums. Moved cost: grading, references, calibration, extra control, and possible multiplexing latency. Pending application

entries.heading: Grouped weight quantization
entries.text: A layer is split into several quantization groups, often aligned with output channels or output-line groups. Each group receives its own scale for quantization and dequantization. Benefit: reduce error caused by one outlier-dominated scale covering a heterogeneous layer. Moved cost: more scale metadata, grouping constraints, compiler decisions, and digital dequantization. Pending applications

entries.heading: Signed-current cancellation
entries.text: Positive and negative split-gate flash cells alternate on a shared bitline so the ADC measures a residual current rather than two independently converted sums. A related arrangement changes control-line direction and paired read modes. Benefit claimed: reduce the ADC count to one-half or one-quarter of a prior separate-path design. Moved cost: device matching, bias control, cancellation accuracy, small-residual resolution, and common-mode headroom. Granted device patent

entries.heading: Chalcogenide drift and read window
entries.text: A separate patent addresses composition, initialization, and read behavior for a chalcogenide memory cell, including threshold drift and stable operation. Benefit: improve a device-level memory path that could support analog computation. Boundary: do not infer that the disclosed flash ACiM product uses this separate material system. Accuracy budget

entries.heading: Trace every error source instead of asking whether "analog accuracy" is solved
entries.text: Error or cost source iHW mechanism that helps What remains Where the cost moves Many levels in one cell Positional digit slicing permits fewer robust states per cell. Each state still has program and read variation. Cells, lines, ADC phases, or cycles plus shift-add logic. High-significance error Mixed-radix mapping can assign more reliable cells to larger digits. An MSB error is multiplied by its significance. Area or density is spent on robust high-order storage. ADC range and resolution Adaptive output-range application selects conversion settings by current grade. Offset, gain, noise, nonlinearity, reference drift, and grading error. Range sensing, references, calibration, multiplexing, and control. Outlier-dominated quantization Group-specific scales narrow the represented range. Group boundaries, scale quantization, activation error, and model sensitivity. Metadata, compiler search, and digital dequantization. Signed weights Differential reconstruction or pre-ADC current cancellation. Mismatch and residual-current precision. Matched devices, bias circuitry, and common-mode control. Array parasitics No complete solution established by the reviewed claims. IR drop, line resistance, sneak paths, coupling, and location-dependent gain. Smaller arrays, models, compensation, remapping, or extra conversion. PVT and lifetime Device patent addresses one drift path; calibration may compensate some effects. Temperature, voltage, process spread, retention, endurance, aging, and read disturb. Characterization, sensors, refresh, redundancy, field policy, and yield loss. Whole-model execution Digital reconstruction makes the matrix primitive usable by a conventional stack. Activations, normalization, reductions, attention, routing, fallback, and communication. Digital engines, SRAM, interconnect, firmware, compiler, and runtime. Accuracy is a budget, not a bit label: task error combines model quantization, cell state, input encoding, array transfer, conversion, digital accumulation, calibration age, and unsupported-operation handling. A defensible result reports each contribution and the hardware or software paid to reduce it. Patent-to-software bridge

entries.heading: Turn each claimed mechanism into a compiler or runtime contract
entries.text: This section traces the patent mechanisms into required software semantics; it is not a disclosure of iHW's implementation. The companion SDK guide defines the module boundaries, public API, artifact schema, simulator/HAL contract, first vertical slice, and CI plan needed to turn those requirements into code. Continue with the build specification: Analog CIM SDK and Compiler: From Model to Running Code separates model calibration, target characterization, and device state, then follows one ONNX MatMul through compilation, packaging, simulation, and execution. Import Graph and ranges Preserve shapes, dtypes, constants, calibration data, and sensitivity. Quantize Groups and digits Select scales, radix, signed encoding, and per-slice reliability. Map Arrays and lines Allocate cells, output lines, ADC ranges, digital fallback, and fault spares. Package Executable artifact Carry weight images, commands, scales, range tables, calibration, and debug maps. Execute Program and infer Validate ABI, bind buffers, issue MVM slices, read ADCs, and reconstruct. Maintain Observe and recover Track saturation, drift, faults, refresh, recalibration, and fallback.

entries.heading: Four compile inputs define one reproducible deployment
entries.text: A model file alone is insufficient because two chips of the same product can have different usable arrays, calibration state, and numerical limits. Model contract graph + tensors Operations, shapes, dynamic dimensions, dtypes, constants, control flow, ranges, and reference outputs. Deployment policy quality + service goals Accuracy floor, latency percentile, power mode, batch, analog coverage target, fallback allowance, and model lifetime. Target descriptor device + ABI Array geometry, memory, NoC, digital engines, ADC sharing, pulse modes, firmware features, and command limits. Characterization database measured transfer model Per-array gain, offset, noise, saturation, IR-drop model, weak cells, PVT curves, drift, and calibration validity. Multi-level IR

entries.heading: Keep graph meaning separate from physical array decisions
entries.text: A staged MLIR design allows target-neutral optimization to finish before hardware commitments become explicit. Each lowering boundary should make previously implicit numerical behavior visible and verifiable. IR level What it represents Required ACiM information Examples of legal transformations Framework IR PyTorch export, ONNX, StableHLO, or another frontend graph Framework semantics, symbolic shapes, constants, state, and reference numerics Constant folding, shape inference, canonicalization, and framework decomposition ACiM graph IR Target-independent tensor operations plus support and sensitivity annotations Candidate precision, error budget, legal fallback, calibration dataset identity, and fusion barriers Operator decomposition, algebraic simplification, fusion, layout-neutral partitioning, and quantization preparation ACiM tensor IR Analog and digital partitions with explicit tensor layouts and scale domains Group scales, clipping, signed representation, partial-sum format, residency, and conversion boundaries Scale propagation, requantization removal, channel grouping, tiling, sharding, and buffer reuse ACiM physical IR Logical tensors placed onto physical cells, lines, converters, and digital units Digit/radix slices, positive and negative paths, fault remap, ADC grade, input pulses, and calibration key Array packing, slice co-location, spare substitution, ADC assignment, phase merging, and digital residual placement Command IR Firmware-visible queues, dependencies, synchronization, and state transitions Program/verify, MVM phase, convert, shift-add, DMA, barrier, health check, refresh, and fallback commands Command fusion, asynchronous overlap, double buffering, converter pipelining, and event elimination Executable artifact Versioned binary delivered to the runtime Target contract, cell image, command streams, buffers, calibration schema, debug maps, and provenance Serialization, signing, compatibility validation, caching, and deterministic rebuild comparison Pass pipeline

entries.heading: The backend should fail early, then lower in measurable steps
entries.text: Order Compiler pass Main decision Emitted evidence 1 Import and semantic normalization Resolve framework-specific operators into a stable supported operation set without changing model meaning. Importer diagnostics, normalized graph, unsupported semantic list, and reference tensor names 2 Shape, range, and sensitivity analysis Infer symbolic shapes and collect activation ranges, outliers, per-layer error sensitivity, and representative data coverage. Range histograms, sensitivity score, calibration dataset hash, and dynamic-shape constraints 3 Capability and legality analysis Enumerate analog, digital, and host implementations for every operation and reject impossible tensor shapes or modes. Support report with reason codes and the legal implementation set per operation 4 Quantization and scale-domain planning Select group boundaries, weight/activation precision, clipping, rounding, accumulator width, and dequantization placement. Quantization manifest and software-equivalent accuracy result 5 Analog/digital partitioning Choose ACiM regions only when saved movement and MVM time exceed conversion, correction, and boundary costs. Partition graph, analog coverage, fallback edges, and boundary tensor costs 6 Weight decomposition Convert each logical weight into radix digits, significance slices, and signed paths under reliability constraints. Logical-to-physical weight map with reconstruction equation 7 Array placement and fault remap Pack slices into arrays while respecting geometry, weak-cell maps, current limits, locality, and spare capacity. Array occupancy, rejected capacity, remap table, and utilization report 8 ADC and phase planning Select range grade, converter sharing, one- or multi-phase reads, repeated sensitive reads, and saturation guard bands. Per-output conversion plan, predicted ENOB/error, phases, and saturation risk 9 Memory and schedule planning Allocate SRAM and host buffers; overlap input encoding, MVM, conversion, shift-add, digital work, DMA, and NoC traffic. Static arena, queue schedule, lifetime graph, bandwidth estimate, and critical path 10 Calibration binding Bind placement to a compatible calibration class or a specific device calibration without embedding stale measurements blindly. Calibration requirements, accepted versions, temperature window, and expiry policy 11 Command lowering and packaging Generate firmware descriptors, program images, digital kernels, debug correlation IDs, and ABI-versioned metadata. Inspectable artifact plus deterministic build manifest 12 Differential verification Compare framework, quantized, physical-simulator, RTL/model, and silicon checkpoints at graph boundaries. Accuracy deltas, first divergent operation, tolerance decision, and release gate result Candidate search

entries.heading: Optimize latency and energy under an explicit error constraint
entries.text: Conceptual cost model Measured coefficients should replace hand-tuned guesses minimize candidate_cost = latency_weight * predicted_latency + energy_weight * predicted_energy + boundary_weight * analog_digital_transfer + programming_weight * weight_program_cost + wear_weight * expected_refresh_and_endurance_cost + risk_weight * numerical_uncertainty subject to: predicted_accuracy_loss <= deployment.error_budget array_current <= adc_range_limit buffers <= available_sram cells + spares <= usable_array_capacity phases <= latency_policy.max_phases calibration is compatible and not expired firmware_abi supports every emitted command Latency T = phases x read + ADC + digital + NoC Use measured queue overlap and contention, not a sum of isolated peak timings. Energy E = input + array + ADC + SRAM + NoC Include calibration, refresh, fallback, idle power, and converter under-utilization. Error risk R = quant + cell + wire + ADC + drift Combine characterized distributions and model sensitivity rather than nominal bit counts. Coverage C = useful analog work / total work Report actual model coverage after fallback and boundary operations. Physical operation contract

entries.heading: One MVM operation needs more attributes than shape and dtype
entries.text: Illustrative ACiM IR Proposed syntax, not an iHW or Tenstorrent interface %result = acim.mvm %activation, %weight_image { logical_type = i8, activation_mode = #acim.pulse<bits = 4, phases = 2>, weight_digits = [#acim.digit<radix = 4, significance = 1>, #acim.digit<radix = 2, significance = 4>], signed_mapping = #acim.differential<positive = 12, negative = 13>, placement = #acim.array<tile = [3, 2], rows = 0:128, cols = 0:64>, adc = #acim.adc<grade = 2, bits = 6, saturation_guard = 0.12>, accumulator = #acim.accum<i24, round = nearest_even, saturate = true>, calibration_key = "family7/revB/tile3x2/class4", fallback = #acim.digital<engine = vector1, trigger = saturation> } : tensor<1x128xi4> -> tensor<1x64xi24> Tool suite

entries.heading: The compiler is one tool inside a closed measurement loop
entries.text: Tool Purpose Required output acim-import Import and normalize ONNX, StableHLO, or framework export while retaining source locations. Graph IR, support diagnostics, shape constraints, and reference tensor manifest acim-characterize Turn wafer, production, and lab measurements into signed target profiles. Versioned per-family and per-device transfer models, PVT curves, fault maps, and confidence intervals acim-calibrate Collect representative activation ranges and optionally run hardware-in-loop measurements. Dataset hash, ranges, clipping choices, sensitivity metrics, and calibration provenance acim-opt Run IR verification, quantization, partitioning, mapping, scheduling, and command lowering passes. Intermediate IR dumps, pass statistics, candidate comparison, and selected plan acim-sim Execute functional, statistical analog, cycle, and command-level models through one API. Outputs, error distributions, saturation events, cycles, bytes, and model-version identity acim-pack Serialize cell images, commands, metadata, digital kernels, and debug maps. Signed and inspectable executable artifact with target and ABI compatibility fields acim-run Load, validate, program, execute, and collect structured runtime results. Result tensors, health state, calibration ID, timing, faults, and recovery actions acim-prof Correlate graph operations with arrays, converter phases, queues, SRAM, NoC, and digital fallback. Timeline, utilization, bandwidth, phase count, converter occupancy, and critical path acim-debug Stop at operation boundaries and compare logical, quantized, simulated, and measured tensors. First divergence, per-slice ADC values, reconstruction trace, and source-level location Validation ladder

entries.heading: One operation should run through every model with the same artifact semantics
entries.text: Level 1 Framework reference Capture deterministic tensors and source locations before quantization. Level 2 Quantized reference Prove scales, clipping, rounding, saturation, and accumulator behavior in software. Level 3 Statistical analog model Inject measured cell, wire, converter, temperature, and drift distributions. Level 4 Cycle and command model Validate resource conflicts, phases, buffers, dependencies, timeout, and recovery. Level 5 RTL or C++ model Correlate command fields, fixed-point arithmetic, interrupts, and firmware state. Level 6 Single-array silicon Compare per-line ADC values and reconstructed outputs against characterization. Level 7 Full-chip silicon Measure contention, thermal gradients, cross-array spread, fallback, and PVT tails. Level 8 Model release gate Require full-dataset accuracy, latency percentiles, energy, coverage, and lifetime policy. Software layer Required ACiM contract Failure if hidden Quantizer Group boundaries, scale format, clipping, rounding, signed policy, and sensitivity budget Software-equivalent accuracy does not match mapped hardware. Compiler IR Logical weight digits, radix/significance, positive/negative paths, converter mode, calibration dependency Optimization passes reorder or fuse operations illegally. Mapper and scheduler Array geometry, line limits, ADC sharing, pulse cycles, fault maps, digital engines, and synchronization Latency, energy, and numerical behavior become unpredictable. Artifact packager Target/ABI, cell programming image, scales, range grades, commands, buffer plan, calibration version, provenance A binary blob cannot be validated, reproduced, cached, or upgraded safely. Runtime and firmware Program/verify lifecycle, queue semantics, saturation and drift counters, refresh, reset, rollback, and fallback Lab accuracy cannot survive deployment or field aging. Debugger and profiler Per-line current, ADC code, positional contribution, reconstructed output, timing, saturation, and calibration ID The first divergent layer and physical cause remain invisible. Minimum deployable-artifact sketch Conceptual schema, not a disclosed iHW ABI acim_artifact: target: {device, revision, firmware_abi, compiler_version} graph: {partitions, tensor_contracts, fallback_edges, source_debug_map} weights: {cell_image, digit_radix, significance, signed_mapping, fault_remap} numerics: {group_scales, clipping, adc_ranges, accumulators, error_budget} schedule: {program_steps, mvm_slices, convert, shift_add, dma, events} memory: {host_buffers, device_sram, constants, mutable_state} calibration: {schema, accepted_classes, version, temperature_window, expiry_policy} recovery: {saturation_action, weak_array_action, timeout_action, digital_fallback} provenance: {model_hash, dataset_id, target_profile_hash, options, build_id} Tenstorrent reuse boundary

entries.heading: ACiM operations
entries.text: A practical backend needs concepts such as program_array , mvm_slice , adc_read , shift_accumulate , calibrate , refresh , and digital fallback. Tenstorrent component or pattern Initial decision ACiM use Required change MLIR infrastructure and TTIR layering Adapt Preserve a high-level tensor IR, source locations, pass pipelines, verification, and dialect conversion structure. Define target-neutral ACiM graph semantics rather than importing TTNN layouts or Tensix execution meaning. TTNN optimizer pattern Adapt Generate legal per-operation candidates and select layouts/configurations with an operation model. Add precision, ADC, characterization, phase, wear, fault-map, calibration, and fallback dimensions to the search. System descriptor and device attributes Adapt Cross-compile against a captured physical target and validate executable compatibility at runtime. Describe arrays, converters, pulse modes, digital companions, calibration classes, firmware commands, and health capabilities. FlatBuffer and ttrt pattern Adapt Use versioned, inspectable artifacts plus read, run, check, perf, and debug tools. Serialize cell images, reconstruction plans, calibration requirements, recovery policy, and physical debug correlation. TT-Explorer workflow Adapt Visualize graphs, compiler overrides, execution traces, memory, and operation results. Add array maps, digit slices, ADC phases, error budget, saturation, drift, faults, and analog coverage views. TTNN, TTMetal, and TTKernel dialect semantics Study only Learn explicit layouts, dataflow, queues, kernels, synchronization, and performance engineering. Replace Tensix-specific operations with program, pulse, MVM, convert, reconstruct, calibrate, refresh, and fallback operations. Metalium device runtime, UMD, and KMD Replace Reuse only proven target-neutral utilities after license and dependency review. Implement the ACiM command ABI, DMA, interrupts, isolation, power, reset, programming, health, and recovery stack. IBM AIHWKit concepts Reference Model device variation, ADC/DAC bounds, noise, hardware-aware training, input scaling, and analog inference. Calibrate models to iHW silicon and connect simulator parameters to compiler IR, target profiles, and release thresholds. Suggested repository ownership Keep physical policy out of framework frontends acim-toolchain/ frontend/ ONNX, StableHLO, and framework import adapters dialect/ Graph, tensor, physical, and command IR definitions analysis/ Shape, range, sensitivity, legality, and error propagation optimizer/ Candidate generation, cost model, partition, map, schedule target/ System descriptors and characterization database schemas codegen/ Firmware commands, digital kernels, and artifact serialization simulator/ Functional, statistical analog, cycle, and command models runtime/ Session, buffers, queues, programming, health, and recovery firmware/ Descriptor validation, scheduling, telemetry, reset, and refresh tools/ Import, characterize, calibrate, inspect, run, profile, and debug tests/ IR, golden, differential, silicon, PVT, aging, and model suites If Tenstorrent built this type of ACiM device, its existing discipline around explicit dataflow, compilation, testing, and observability would still be valuable. The central optimization target would change from mainly moving tiles between DRAM, SRAM, and core grids to jointly controlling analog error, conversion, slicing, programming, calibration, and digital escape paths. See the full reuse decision guide . Paper and patent review checklist

entries.heading: Ten questions answered from the public iHW record
entries.text: "Not disclosed" is an answer. It prevents an architecture document or company statement from quietly becoming evidence for a stronger accuracy or efficiency claim. Review question Answer for the reviewed iHW record Confidence 1. Fabricated silicon, device traces, or simulation? The patents describe architectures. A company recruiting page claims 8-bit-weight ACiM silicon verification and a MobileNet demo, but no independent silicon report or raw trace set was found. Mixed evidence 2. Did the complete validation dataset run through hardware? Not disclosed. "MobileNet demo" does not establish dataset coverage, which layers ran in analog, sample count, or repeated-chip testing. Open 3. What accuracy baseline was used? Not disclosed in the reviewed public claim. Require FP32, production digital quantized, software-equivalent ACiM, and measured silicon results on the same model and data. Open 4. Which work remained off-chip or digital? The patent explains matrix representation and reconstruction, not complete-network placement. Activation, normalization, pooling, attention, routing, partial sums, and host work are not quantified. Open 5. How much retraining, calibration, redundancy, or refresh? Digit slicing, range selection, and grouped quantization imply software and calibration support, but the training recipe, chip-in-loop burden, spare capacity, refresh interval, and field policy are not public. Open 6. Are energy and latency end to end? No public end-to-end result was identified for this patent stack. Count programming, input encoding, all ADC phases, digital reconstruction, companion operations, SRAM/interconnect, host traffic, calibration, and idle power. Open 7. Accuracy across chips, PVT, defects, and time? No public population distribution, process-corner sweep, voltage/temperature sweep, defect policy, retention curve, endurance result, or calibration-age curve was identified. Open 8. Does mitigation preserve density and efficiency? Not automatically. Digit slices, adaptive ranges, group scales, matched signed paths, and digital recombination can move cost into cells, lines, converters, cycles, metadata, calibration, or digital logic. Conditional 9. Inference, training, or both? The reviewed architecture is most directly supported as an inference-weight path. Static inference weights avoid the update-linearity and endurance burden of on-chip training; do not treat the patents as training proof. Inference focus 10. Can it scale to the target model? Not established for large LLM parameter counts, irregular tensor shapes, long context, KV-cache traffic, attention, communication, or multi-chip execution. A 4-bit LLM weight format alone does not answer these system questions. Open Interview and technical due diligence

entries.heading: Questions that turn patent language into a product contract
entries.text: Precision What exactly is 8-bit? Logical weights after reconstruction, cell states, ADC output, accumulator, software-equivalent model, or measured effective precision? Physical cost How many resources per MAC? Report cells, lines, ADCs, read phases, input pulses, shift-add operations, and spare capacity. Implementation Which claims are in silicon? Separate the granted core patent from pending ADC, quantization, and signed-weight applications and identify the implemented revision. Accuracy Where is the full ablation? Compare FP32, digital INT8/INT4, software ACiM, measured raw ACiM, calibrated ACiM, and hybrid fallback. Population What are the tails? Ask for lot count, chip count, weak arrays, rejected devices, remapping rate, yield, and worst-case accuracy. Lifecycle Who owns calibration? Define factory, boot, thermal, periodic, workload, aging, refresh, rollback, and field-update responsibilities. System What remains digital? Quantify analog coverage, unsupported operators, transfer boundaries, digital correction, SRAM, DRAM, and host work. Software What is the stable ABI? Inspect importer, IR, compiler, simulator, artifact, runtime, firmware, driver, profiler, debugger, and version negotiation. Final assessment

entries.heading: Technically plausible, complementary, and still evidence-limited
entries.text: The core iHW grant solves a narrower and more defensible problem than "analog accuracy": it reduces reliance on fragile high-level-count cells by moving precision into positional representation and digital reconstruction. The pending ADC, grouped-quantization, and signed-current ideas address important adjacent costs. This is a coherent hardware/software strategy. It becomes a product-level accuracy solution only when the company shows complete models, analog coverage, correction cost, chip distributions, PVT and lifetime behavior, yield, and end-to-end energy and latency against clear digital baselines.
