Add a custom device model, fake transport, or co-simulation bridge when the Kernel-Mode Driver (KMD), firmware, queue protocol, and analog model must run together. Terms here BSP = bootloader, kernel, device tree, and board support rootfs = Linux userspace files HAL = transport-neutral device interface JTAG = low-level hardware debug port Co-simulation = coordinated execution of two or more simulator models Direct answer There is no universal "QEMU, SD card, then device kernel" sequence Choose the deployment topology first; build, load, and debug each artifact through its actual owner. A desktop PCIe card normally needs no SD card: Linux is already running, the KMD loads controller firmware when the device has a programmable controller, and the runtime submits a compiled model artifact. An embedded host may boot a BSP image from SD/eMMC and then load accelerator firmware, when present, through remoteproc or a vendor driver. A device compute kernel or microcode payload is not the Linux kernel, and should be named separately. Topology A: Linux host + PCIe card Typical workstation, server, or evaluation-card setup Host boot Boot the existing x86-64 or AArch64 Linux installation. Do not prepare an SD card unless the host platform itself requires one. Install Install the signed KMD, udev rules, controller firmware under the configured firmware search path, UMD/runtime, compiler, and diagnostics. Discover PCIe enumerates the endpoint. The KMD claims BARs, configures DMA masks and MSI-X, creates an IOMMU-protected context, and exposes a device node. Boot device If a programmable controller exists, the KMD obtains firmware with the Linux firmware API, verifies compatibility, transfers it through BAR or DMA boot windows, starts it, and waits for READY. A fixed RTL controller instead publishes its ROM/logic ABI directly. Run The application loads a compiled .acx artifact and tensors through the runtime. The model image is usually session data, not permanently flashed firmware. Recover Collect host and device evidence before reset; then use context reset, Function Level Reset (FLR), secondary-bus reset, or power cycle according to fault scope. Topology B: embedded Linux host SoC Typical camera, robot, appliance, or edge-module setup Build BSP Cross-compile the bootloader, Linux kernel, Device Tree Blob (DTB), root filesystem, KMD, UMD/runtime, application, and board diagnostics. Deploy host image Write the vendor-defined boot image to SD, eMMC, UFS, or network boot media. Verify the physical target before using any imaging tool. Boot host Capture bootloader and early kernel serial output. Confirm clocks, regulators, reset GPIOs, IOMMU, reserved memory, PCIe or on-chip interconnect, and device-tree bindings. Boot controller Use Linux remoteproc , a platform KMD, or a boot ROM to load the controller Executable and Linkable Format (ELF) image and create messaging/queue resources. Feed input The host application receives camera, network, sensor, or storage input, preprocesses it, and submits buffers through the same runtime/HAL contract used in simulation. Field update Version and update host BSP, controller firmware, model artifact, and calibration independently, with an atomic rollback policy for compatible sets. Question PCIe card Embedded host SoC Engineering rule Make QEMU first? Optional for host driver and protocol tests Useful when QEMU supports the selected host CPU/board Start with native functional tests; add QEMU where CPU/OS behavior matters. What does QEMU simulate? Host CPU/Linux plus only implemented virtual devices Host or controller CPU and modeled peripherals A generic QEMU machine does not contain the custom ACiM endpoint or analog physics. Flash an SD card? Normally no Often yes, if SD/eMMC is the board boot source The boot source comes from the board design and BSP, not from ACiM itself. Build a host binary? Yes: application, compiler tools, runtime/UMD, diagnostics, and possibly KMD module Cross-compile when the target architecture differs from the development machine. Build a device kernel? Build controller firmware and compute microcode/kernels if the architecture has programmable engines Reserve "Linux kernel" for the host OS; call device payloads firmware or compute kernels. How does input reach ACiM? Application buffer to UMD/KMD to PCIe DMA Application buffer through shared memory, DMA, NoC, or PCIe The runtime owns live buffer bindings; the compiler artifact owns logical dataflow.

entries.heading: Name and version the deployable artifacts
entries.text: Artifact Built for Loaded by Typical deployment Required identity Host boot image Host CPU Boot ROM / bootloader SD, eMMC, UFS, SPI flash, or network; embedded only BSP version, DTB, kernel config, rootfs hash KMD Host kernel and CPU Kernel module loader or built into Linux .ko , package, initramfs, or kernel image Kernel release, UAPI major/minor, device IDs Runtime / UMD / app Host userspace CPU Dynamic loader and service manager Rootfs package, container, or development tree Build ID, UAPI range, artifact ABI range Controller firmware, if present Device RISC-V/Arm/controller CPU; omitted for fixed RTL control KMD, remoteproc, boot ROM, or JTAG in the lab Firmware directory, dedicated partition, or RAM load Firmware ABI, register-map version, image hash, entry point Compute program Device digital engines and ACiM arrays Runtime and controller firmware Inside .acx or a versioned kernel package Opcode ISA, array geometry, precision, scratch requirements Model artifact Named accelerator target Runtime session Application data partition or model store Compiler provenance, target ID, ABI, graph and constant hashes Calibration / health profile Chip, board, voltage, and temperature domain Firmware/runtime under controlled policy Protected per-device state with factory/default fallback Chip serial, profile version, conditions, age, integrity hash

entries.heading: The top-level build, boot, and test flow
entries.text: 1. Freeze contracts One version set Register map, queues, UAPI, firmware ABI, artifact ABI, memory map, fault and trace schema. 2. Build host BSP + KMD + UMD Compile for the host CPU; retain symbols, manifests, reproducible presets, and test utilities. 3. Build device Firmware + kernels Link the controller memory map; emit ELF, binary, map file, symbols, and image metadata. 4. Emulate HAL + QEMU + co-sim Prove CPU software, queues, DMA semantics, faults, reset, and numerical reference before a board. 5. Bring up transport Enumerate + boot Power, clock, reset, PCIe/interconnect, BAR, IOMMU, DMA, MSI-X, firmware READY. 6. Correlate workload One MVM to full model Compare tensors, counters, timestamps, energy, temperature, calibration, and recovery.

entries.heading: Ten-stage verification ladder
entries.text: Do not advance because a demo looks plausible. Advance when the stated output, timeout, error behavior, and evidence bundle pass automatically. Every later stage reruns the earlier contract tests. 0 Contract lint Generated headers agree; ABI sizes, IDs, endianness, reserved fields, and compatibility tests pass. 1 Golden model Native host functional HAL matches reference tensors and injects saturation, defects, drift, and timeouts. 2 Queue model Fake PCIe/MMIO/DMA backend proves ownership, wraparound, ordering, interrupt, reset, and malformed descriptors. 3 Host OS in QEMU BSP, KMD lifecycle, UAPI, service startup, permissions, and fake/custom device probe pass. 4 Controller ISA sim Firmware boots on a matching CPU/machine model; GDB reaches READY and queue unit tests complete. 5 Host-device co-sim KMD and firmware exchange real descriptors while the analog backend supplies deterministic MVM results and faults. 6 RTL / FPGA Register, DMA, interrupt, boot, queue, and reset behavior correlates with the protocol model under stress. 7 Board transport Enumeration, firmware boot, loopback DMA, MSI-X, IOMMU isolation, teardown, and recovery pass on silicon. 8 One analog MVM Raw ADC, reconstructed output, calibration ID, temperature, and error distribution match the acceptance envelope. 9 Model + operations Subgraph and full model pass accuracy, latency, throughput, power, soak, reset, and support-bundle gates.

entries.heading: Choose the QEMU boundary deliberately
entries.text: Start here Native process + functional HAL Run compiler, runtime, queue library, numerical model, and fault injection as ordinary host processes. Fastest correctness and continuous integration loop Host OS QEMU host + fake/custom device Boot Linux to test BSP, KMD, UAPI, packaging, startup, and permissions. Implement the ACiM PCIe model or use a fake transport. Generic virt alone cannot probe the real endpoint Controller CPU QEMU firmware target Run device firmware only when the chosen QEMU machine matches the controller ISA, address map, interrupt controller, timer, and modeled peripherals. CPU emulation does not reproduce analog variation Whole chain QEMU + co-simulation bridge Forward MMIO, DMA, queues, and interrupts to functional, cycle, RTL, or analog models through a defined socket/shared-memory protocol. Highest pre-silicon fidelity; also highest integration cost Environment It can prove It cannot prove alone Required exit evidence Native functional model Graph semantics, quantization, command construction, error policy Kernel behavior, real timing, PCIe, analog distributions Golden tensor diff and deterministic fault tests QEMU host Host architecture, Linux boot, KMD/UAPI lifecycle, packages Unimplemented ACiM device and real DMA/interrupt timing Automated boot/probe/open/submit/reset test QEMU controller Firmware CPU code, exceptions, memory map, modeled IRQ and timer behavior Custom engines and analog physics unless explicitly modeled Firmware unit tests, READY handshake, GDB-readable fault state Cycle/RTL co-sim Protocol ordering, contention, queue and engine timing, RTL behavior Unmodeled package/board effects and silicon variation Trace correlation and bounded cycle deltas Real board Physical link, DMA, interrupts, converters, arrays, power and thermal behavior Broad corner coverage from one device Population-aware correctness, performance, soak, and recovery reports Build and emulator command templates Replace target presets and machine names with the versioned BSP; proposed names are not existing QEMU devices # 1. Fast host loop: compiler/runtime/fake HAL cmake --preset host-debug cmake --build --preset host-debug ctest --preset host-debug --output-on-failure ./build/host-debug/bin/acim-run --hal functional --model smoke.acx # 2. Embedded host Linux in QEMU. This boots the host BSP only. qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -cpu cortex-a72 -m 4096 -nographic \ -kernel out/host/Image -initrd out/host/rootfs.cpio.gz \ -append "console=ttyAMA0 earlycon" # A KMD can probe ACiM only after implementing a custom/fake endpoint, for example: # -device acim-pcie,backend=unix:/tmp/acim-model.sock # "acim-pcie" above is a proposed project device model, not built into QEMU. # 3. Device controller firmware. The machine must match the real controller map. qemu-system-riscv64 -M acim-controller -nographic -bios none \ -kernel out/device/acim-fw.elf -S -gdb tcp::1234 riscv64-unknown-elf-gdb out/device/acim-fw.elf \ -ex "target remote :1234" # "acim-controller" is also a proposed custom machine name. Until it exists, # run firmware libraries as host tests or use the vendor ISA/RTL simulator. Embedded image safety: use Buildroot, Yocto, or the vendor BSP to produce deployable images, and use the board vendor's imaging procedure for SD/eMMC. Record the output image hash and confirm the target device path before writing. The files in a Buildroot output/images/ directory are deployment artifacts; intermediate build directories are not.

entries.heading: Board boot and capability handshake
entries.text: 1 Power and reset Rails, clocks, reset, refclk, link training, boot straps; UART emits a ROM identifier. 2 Enumerate Host finds endpoint or platform device; IDs, BAR sizes, IOMMU, DMA width, MSI-X, and AER match the specification. 3 Start control plane KMD/remoteproc loads and starts compatible firmware when present; otherwise it verifies the fixed ROM/RTL control ABI and optional microcode. 4 Negotiate Firmware reports READY, boot epoch, ABI, capabilities, memory/array health, calibration state, trace clock, and fatal status. 5 Publish device KMD enables queues and userspace node; UMD queries caps, creates context, verifies artifact compatibility, and starts a session. Checkpoint Host evidence Device evidence Timeout action Physical discovery lspci -nnvv or platform-device sysfs, link width/speed, AER ROM UART banner or JTAG halt state Inspect power, clocks, reset, straps, refclk, lanes, DTB KMD probe Driver-bound sysfs path, BAR resources, DMA mask, MSI-X vectors, IOMMU group Mailbox visible, ROM state readable Check IDs, BAR mapping, endian/access width, IOMMU and module log Firmware READY Requested image/hash, transfer bytes, boot command, deadline and response Last boot stage, exception registers, crash buffer, firmware ABI Halt with JTAG/GDB before reset; dump mailbox and load memory Userspace open Device node, permissions, UAPI query, context and queue IDs Context table and queue generation Compare UMD/KMD ABI, udev rules, health and reset epoch

entries.heading: One inference request and completion
entries.text: 1. Application Prepare input Capture/preprocess tensor; assign run, request, graph, and correlation IDs. 2. Runtime / UMD Bind buffers Load .acx , select compatible profile, allocate/import Buffer Objects (BOs), create dependencies. 3. KMD Map and submit Validate handles/ranges; map scatter-gather pages to IOVA; publish SQ entry; ring MMIO doorbell. 4. Firmware Validate and schedule Check generation, context, opcode, bounds, program, health, deadline, and dependency state. 5. ACiM data plane Transfer and compute DMA to SRAM; DAC/input encoding; array MVM; ADC; reconstruction; digital operators and partial sums. 6. Completion Return result DMA output; write CQ; raise MSI-X; KMD wakes poll/event; UMD resolves event; app consumes tensor. Boundary Control path Data path Ordering proof App to UMD API call, session, event, timeout Tensor views or imported dma-buf Buffer lifetime and dependency test UMD to KMD ioctl, mmap, poll/eventfd Buffer handles resolved to pinned/imported pages UAPI conformance, process-exit and malicious-input tests KMD to device SQ, CQ, doorbell, mailbox, MSI-X DMA over IOVA mappings Publish descriptor before doorbell; write result before CQ and interrupt Firmware to engines Command processor, dependencies, watchdog SRAM/NoC streams, array inputs/outputs, partial sums Cycle trace with command and tile IDs Analog to digital Profile, calibration, range and retry policy DAC code, cell current/charge, ADC code, reconstructed value Raw/reconstructed sample capture and golden-model correlation

entries.heading: Capture one causally connected log, not five unrelated files
entries.text: 1. Identify Create run manifest Run/correlation IDs, git commits, hashes, ABIs, serial, clocks, voltage, temperature, calibration. 2. Arm host Tracing before submit App JSONL, Tracy, UMD events, KMD tracepoints/ftrace, kernel journal, PCIe AER and IOMMU faults. 3. Arm device UART + trace ring Firmware stages, queue events, DMA, engine cycles, counters, ADC flags, watchdog and crash buffer. 4. Run workload Known request IDs Warm-up separately; execute fixed inputs; preserve first fault; avoid reset until evidence is drained. 5. Correlate Join clocks and IDs Use synchronization markers and an affine clock transform; align host, firmware, engine, and instrument timelines. 6. Diagnose Find first divergence Compare expected/observed state, tensors, queue positions, bytes, cycles, faults, power and temperature. Proposed support-bundle layout and capture interface Make this one command in the SDK; paths and utility names form a product contract support/run-20260712T103000Z-7f3a/ manifest.json # versions, hashes, ABIs, topology, serial, environment host/app.jsonl # request and graph correlation IDs host/runtime.jsonl # sessions, buffers, submissions, waits, fallback host/tracy.tracy # host spans and optional imported device zones host/kernel.dat # trace-cmd/ftrace events: acim, irq, iommu, sched host/journal-kernel.txt # probe, firmware, reset, AER and IOMMU messages host/pci.txt # config space, link, BAR and AER snapshot device/uart.txt # ROM and early firmware boot device/trace.bin # timestamped firmware/engine trace schema device/crash.bin # preserved first-fault context device/counters.json # DMA, NoC, SRAM, array, ADC, DSP, stalls, energy model/artifact-manifest.json # target, graph, constants, compiler and debug-map hashes model/input.npz # reproducible non-sensitive test input model/output-device.npz # observed tensors or selected checkpoints analysis/timeline.json # normalized clock domain and decoded events analysis/tensor-diff.json # golden comparison and first divergent operation # Proposed SDK command: implementation should gather data without manual copying. acim-smi support collect --run-id 7f3a --include-trace --output support/ # Useful host evidence while reproducing a failure. lspci -nnvv -s "$ACIM_BDF" journalctl -k --since "$RUN_START" trace-cmd record -e acim -e irq -e iommu ./acim-smoke --run-id 7f3a # Device evidence should be read through a versioned KMD/firmware interface. acim-smi trace snapshot --run-id 7f3a acim-smi health show --json Clock correlation: a host timestamp and device cycle counter are different clocks. Emit repeated synchronization pairs around the run, fit host_ns = a * device_cycles + b , report fit error, and keep raw timestamps. A single offset hides drift and makes a long trace look causally wrong.

entries.heading: Diagnose from the first failed boundary
entries.text: Observed symptom First layer to inspect Evidence to compare Focused experiment No device enumeration Board power/reset/PCIe or platform DTB Rails, clocks, reset, refclk, link state, boot straps, root-port AER Hold controller in ROM; reduce link speed/width; inspect endpoint with JTAG Enumerates but no device node KMD probe IDs, BAR resources, DMA mask, MSI-X, IOMMU group, firmware request Bind driver manually in a lab; enable dynamic debug and probe tracepoints Device node exists but open fails UMD/KMD contract Permissions, UAPI major/minor, device health, reset generation Run capability query as the service user; compare expected ioctl sizes Submit succeeds but firmware never starts SQ publication and doorbell Producer/consumer indices, descriptor bytes, barriers, MMIO readback, generation Submit one no-op command; poll rather than interrupt; inspect queue memory on both sides Device completes but host never wakes CQ and MSI-X path CQ entry visibility, interrupt cause/mask/vector, KMD handler and wakeup Use interrupt self-test; switch to CQ polling; verify write-before-interrupt ordering DMA corruption or IOMMU fault Buffer mapping IOVA, scatter/gather segments, length/alignment, direction, cache ownership Use one coherent page and loopback; add guard patterns; reduce transfer size Stable transport but wrong tensor Compiler/artifact/analog boundary Layout, quantization, scale/zero point, program/profile ID, calibration, ADC saturation, remap Run one MVM with fixed operands; capture raw ADC and reconstructed values; bypass fusion Correct but slow Timeline and counters Host queue, H2D, SRAM/NoC, DAC, MVM, ADC, reconstruction, DSP, D2H and postprocess time Sweep batch/shape; force resident weights; disable retries; compare full and partial utilization Intermittent after many runs Lifetime, thermal, drift, and reset Epoch, queue wrap, leaked mappings, temperature, voltage, calibration age, corrected faults Run soak with periodic known-answer tests and fault injection; preserve the first failing bundle Whole-chain exit gate A reproducible run survives both success and deliberate failure One command builds, deploys, tests, collects, and decodes a versioned evidence bundle. The minimum convincing result is not merely a YOLO image. It is a cold boot, capability negotiation, one known-answer MVM, one model inference, tensor correlation, latency breakdown, injected timeout, context or function recovery, and a support bundle that identifies the first failed boundary without guessing. Compile and deploy flow

entries.heading: Do not make MLIR responsible for PCIe
entries.text: MLIR selects and encodes legal hardware work. The runtime resolves physical buffers and live device state. The KMD protects host resources. Firmware owns device scheduling. Keeping these decisions separate permits the same artifact to run in simulation and on a board. Terms here ONNX = model graph format MLIR = compiler lowering infrastructure ORT = ONNX Runtime EP = framework backend plugin 1. Import ONNX graph Validate opset, infer shapes, normalize layouts and constants. 2. Analyze Target support Match operators, precision, tensor bounds, calibration, and fallback. 3. Partition Analog islands Cluster resident dense or convolution work; minimize analog/digital crossings. 4. Lower Device programs Map arrays, digital kernels, transfers, dependencies, and scratch memory. 5. Package .acx artifact Code, constants, profiles, commands, ABI, hashes, and graph debug map. 6. Execute HAL backend Simulator or UMD/KMD/firmware uses identical buffer and command semantics. Decision Compiler owns Runtime owns Device owns Operator legality Static support and diagnostic reason Capability/firmware compatibility check Descriptor validation before dispatch Memory Logical buffers, lifetimes, offsets, alignment Buffer objects, imports, bindings, reuse SRAM allocation, DMA windows, bounds check Analog mapping Array slices, precision, profile ID, alternatives Select live profile and healthy placement Program ID, calibration table, remap, saturation policy Scheduling Dependencies and legal overlap Batching, queue and latency policy Resource arbitration, watchdog, completion order Failure Fallback-capable variants Retry, rebind, digital fallback, session loss Fault isolation, abort, reset and health update First model dataflow

entries.heading: A YOLO demo should prove the whole hybrid path, not only one analog convolution
entries.text: This placement is a proposed starting point, not a claim about an iHW or Mythic product. The exact YOLO version, supported operators, array geometry, digital engines, precision, and SRAM capacity must decide the final partition. Keep host fallback available until each device segment passes differential tests. Terms here BO = Buffer Object H2D = Host-to-Device transfer D2H = Device-to-Host transfer NMS = detection deduplication mAP = detection accuracy metric Host Capture + preprocess Decode, resize/letterbox, normalize, quantize, pack layout. PCIe Input DMA Imported or allocated input BO; one H2D transfer per frame. Device analog Backbone Conv Resident weights, calibrated array MVM, ADC and reconstruction. Device digital Neck transforms Activation, resize, concat, routing, unsupported operators. Device mixed Head projections Analog eligible convolution/linear plus digital decode preparation. PCIe Output DMA Return compact logits/boxes, not intermediate feature maps. Host Decode + NMS Dequantize, box transform, confidence filter, NMS, annotate. Partition rule: one analog operator surrounded by host fallback can be slower than CPU/GPU execution because every boundary moves a feature map over PCIe. Prefer the largest accuracy-safe contiguous device island, keep weights resident across frames, and transfer only input and final output once the device path is validated. YOLO stage Preferred placement Compiler proof Runtime/board proof Input preprocessing Host initially; device later if a validated image engine exists Exact resize, padding, color order, normalization, quantization Golden tensor immediately before first device operator Conv + static weights Analog when dimensions, precision, and accuracy are legal Weight slicing, sign mapping, bias, scale, activation fusion, array utilization Program/verify result, calibration profile, saturation and error counters Activation / elementwise Digital vector engine or firmware kernel Quantization domain and rounding are explicit Cycle and numerical checkpoints at each partition boundary Resize / concat / route Digital engine; avoid host round-trip Layout and memory plan fit SRAM and DMA rules No hidden copy; measured bytes and stall reason Detection head Hybrid; target profile selects analog-eligible projections Tensor shapes and output scale remain compatible with decode Layer error distribution plus end-to-end mAP on full validation set Decode / NMS Host for the Minimum Viable Product (MVP), device only with a measured benefit Model-specific anchors/strides and thresholds packaged as metadata Deterministic postprocess and identical evaluation configuration T_frame = T_pre + T_H2D + T_queue + T_device + T_D2H + T_post Report each term, median, and tail latency. FPS_steady <= 1 / max(stage_time) Frames Per Second (FPS): with pipelining, the slowest non-overlapped stage limits throughput. coverage = device_ops / supported_candidate_ops Also report bytes crossing every partition, not only operator count. accuracy_delta = mAP_device - mAP_reference Use the same dataset, preprocessing, decode, and thresholds. Platform requirements

entries.heading: Freeze a host profile and device profile before writing the KMD
entries.text: PCIe generation, lane width, BAR sizes, DMA address width, queue count, and memory capacity are target facts, not values to infer from a demo. Encode them in machine-readable target and capability records. Terms here IOMMU = DMA translation and isolation IOVA = device-visible mapped address FLR = PCIe function reset AER = PCIe error reporting Host requirement profile Minimum supported Linux environment CPU and OS Document x86-64 and/or AArch64, distribution, kernel range, page size, endianness, and 32-bit userspace policy. PCIe root Required link generation and width, 64-bit BAR support, MSI-X, AER, hot reset/FLR behavior, and link retraining policy. IOMMU Enable Intel Virtualization Technology for Directed I/O (VT-d), AMD-Vi, or an Arm System Memory Management Unit (SMMU) for isolation. Qualify IOVA width, page sizes, and IOMMU group topology. Memory Locked-memory limits, pinned-memory budget, scatter/gather limits, alignment, Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA) node, and optional hugepage policy. Build Compiler, CMake/Ninja, kernel headers, Dynamic Kernel Module Support (DKMS) or in-tree build, packaging, symbols, sanitizers, and reproducible toolchain image. Access udev rules, device group, least-privilege permissions, firmware search path, module signing, and secure-boot policy. Observability lspci , sysfs, debugfs or tracefs, dynamic debug, ftrace, perf, AER counters, and support-bundle command. Media interop Optional dma-buf import for camera/display pipelines; define synchronization and supported exporters explicitly. Device requirement profile RTL, board, firmware, and analog contract Identity Vendor/device/subsystem IDs, revision, serial, board Stock Keeping Unit (SKU), capability bits, hardware ABI, and manufacturing state. PCIe endpoint BAR type/size, DMA address width, maximum payload/read request, MSI-X vectors, FLR, AER, and power states. Boot ROM state, mailbox, firmware image format, authenticity check, load window, entry point, timeout, rollback, and recovery mode. Queues Submission/completion entry formats, count, depth, alignment, ownership, generation, doorbells, interrupt moderation, and reset. Memory SRAM banks, address map, DMA engines, segment limits, alignment, coherency, ECC, bandwidth counters, and reserved regions. Compute Analog macro geometry, DAC/ADC modes, accumulators, digital engines, supported operators, precision, and scheduling constraints. Reliability Row/column/tile fault map, temperature/voltage sensors, watchdog, saturation flags, ECC, calibration age, and reset domains. Debug Trace SRAM, timestamp domain, correlation ID, performance counters, crash dump, firmware log, and safe register snapshot. PCIe endpoint implementation

entries.heading: Start with a small versioned control BAR, DMA rings, and MSI-X
entries.text: The layout below is a proposed v0 example for RTL, firmware, KMD, simulator, and documentation to implement from one register specification. It is not a disclosed register map for any company. Generate C, C++, SystemVerilog, simulator, and documentation definitions from the same schema. Terms here BAR = device address region MMIO = register access by CPU load/store DMA = bulk device/host transfer MSI-X = multi-vector PCIe interrupts RO/RW/WO/RW1C = register access modes BAR0: control Example size: 64 KiB Identity, mailbox, queues, IRQ, fault, trace control BAR2: aperture Optional and capability-gated Device SRAM/program window for bring-up, not raw production mapping BAR4: trace Optional read-only window Snapshot or streaming trace when DMA trace is unavailable Offset Register Access Required semantics 0x0000 DEVICE_ID RO Magic, hardware revision, register-layout major/minor. 0x0010 CAPS0 / CAPS1 RO DMA width, queues, MSI-X, reset, trace, memory, analog and digital features. 0x0020 DEVICE_STATUS RO Reset, ROM, firmware ready, quiesced, fatal, thermal, calibration-required. 0x0024 DEVICE_CONTROL RW Quiesce, function reset request, firmware start, trace enable; reserved bits must be zero. 0x0040 FW_MAILBOX_* RW Image location/length/hash, command, response, boot epoch, ABI and timeout reason. 0x0100 SQ_BASE_LO/HI RW DMA address of coherent submission ring; write only while queue disabled. 0x0110 SQ_SIZE / SQ_TAIL RW Power-of-two entry count and producer position; size bounded by capability. 0x0120 CQ_BASE_LO/HI RW DMA address of coherent completion ring and consumer record. 0x0130 QUEUE_CONTROL RW Enable, interrupt vector, moderation, context and queue generation. 0x0140 SQ_DOORBELL WO New producer index. Descriptor writes and ownership change must precede this MMIO write. 0x0200 IRQ_CAUSE / MASK / ACK RW1C Completion, fault, firmware, thermal and health causes with defined clear semantics. 0x0240 FAULT_CODE / INFO RO First-fault record, context, queue, command, engine, IOVA, and reset generation. 0x0300 TRACE_CONTROL / HEAD RW Snapshot trigger, filter, buffer location, overflow and timestamp frequency. 0x1000 + q*0x100 QUEUE_q RW Per-queue register block; stride and queue count are capability values. Endianness Specify little-endian MMIO and ring fields. Convert explicitly in firmware and KMD; do not rely on host layout. readl/writel + cpu_to_leXX/leXX_to_cpu Atomicity Define which 64-bit values use paired 32-bit writes, latch order, and commit register. Never assume a 64-bit MMIO write is atomic everywhere. BASE_LO, BASE_HI, then QUEUE_ENABLE Posted writes PCI memory writes are posted. Use ordered accessors and read a harmless device register when the protocol requires confirmed arrival before reset or teardown. writel(...); readl(DEVICE_STATUS); Reset generation Increment an epoch on every firmware or function reset. Reject stale queues, buffer handles, completions, and artifacts. submission.generation == device.generation Register ownership Declare ROM-only, KMD-only, firmware-only, debug-only, and safe userspace doorbell pages. Production userspace never maps the full control BAR. spec/registers.yaml: owner + access + side_effect Discovery Unknown major layout fails closed. New minor capability bits are ignored only when their documented default is safe. major mismatch -> -EPROTO Command and queue ABI

entries.heading: Descriptors carry handles and bounded references, not trust
entries.text: A KMD resolves process-owned buffer handles into IOVAs. Firmware accepts only ranges registered in the context table. Keep fixed-width fields, natural alignment, explicit reserved fields, and static size checks. Add a new ioctl or opcode for new semantics instead of silently changing an old one. Terms here SQ = Submission Queue CQ = Completion Queue ABI = binary command contract IOVA = mapped DMA address Doorbell = MMIO queue notification Proposed firmware queue entries Illustrative v0 shared header; all fields little-endian /* include/hw/acim_queue_v0.h - generated from the protocol schema */ struct acim_sq_entry_v0 { __le16 opcode; /* EXECUTE, PROGRAM, VERIFY, COPY, TRACE, ABORT */ __le16 flags; /* interrupt, priority class, retry permission */ __le32 command_bytes; /* bounded command-buffer length */ __le64 context_id; /* firmware-created context, never a pointer */ __le64 command_iova; /* IOVA already registered for this context */ __le64 user_cookie; /* opaque value returned in completion */ __le64 deadline_ns; /* relative or zero; clock semantics are specified */ __le32 generation; /* rejects work submitted before reset */ __le32 crc32; /* optional transport corruption check */ }; struct acim_cq_entry_v0 { __le64 user_cookie; __le32 status; /* OK, INVALID, FAULT, TIMEOUT, RESET, RETRY */ __le32 fault_code; __le64 device_cycles; __le64 completed_bytes; __le32 generation; __le32 reserved0; }; static_assert(sizeof(struct acim_sq_entry_v0) == 48); static_assert(sizeof(struct acim_cq_entry_v0) == 40); Proposed Linux UAPI surface KMD-managed queues first; map a fast doorbell only after isolation is proven /* include/uapi/linux/acim_accel.h - no C pointers or implicit padding */ #define ACIM_IOCTL_QUERY_CAPS _IOWR('A', 0x00, struct acim_query_caps) #define ACIM_IOCTL_CREATE_CONTEXT _IOWR('A', 0x01, struct acim_create_context) #define ACIM_IOCTL_CREATE_BO _IOWR('A', 0x02, struct acim_create_bo) #define ACIM_IOCTL_IMPORT_DMABUF _IOWR('A', 0x03, struct acim_import_dmabuf) #define ACIM_IOCTL_CREATE_QUEUE _IOWR('A', 0x04, struct acim_create_queue) #define ACIM_IOCTL_SUBMIT _IOWR('A', 0x05, struct acim_submit) #define ACIM_IOCTL_WAIT _IOWR('A', 0x06, struct acim_wait) #define ACIM_IOCTL_QUERY_FAULT _IOWR('A', 0x07, struct acim_query_fault) #define ACIM_IOCTL_RESET_CONTEXT _IOWR('A', 0x08, struct acim_reset_context) struct acim_submit { __u32 size; /* must equal the known v0 structure size */ __u32 flags; __u64 context_handle; __u64 queue_handle; __u64 command_bo_handle; __u64 command_offset; __u64 command_bytes; __u64 user_cookie; __u64 reserved[4]; /* userspace writes zero; kernel validates zero */ }; Object UMD representation KMD proof Firmware proof Lifetime ends Context Opaque handle tied to an open device FD Owner process/file, credentials, generation, quotas Valid context table entry and allowed engine mask FD close, explicit destroy, fatal reset Buffer object Handle, size, usage, optional CPU map Allocation/import, pages, DMA direction, IOMMU map, reference count IOVA range belongs to context and command access is in bounds All dependent fences signal, then unmap/unpin Queue Handle plus event or pollable FD Depth, ring memory, MSI-X vector, context, reset epoch Base, size, owner, head/tail and generation are valid Quiesce, drain/abort, disable, free IRQ/ring Artifact/program Loaded module and binding table Header, ABI, size, hashes, BO access and firmware compatibility Opcode, section bounds, program ID, target/profile compatibility Last in-flight execution finishes and program is evicted Fence/event Monotonic sequence or opaque event Queue/context membership, timeout, cancellation, wakeup Exactly one terminal CQ record per accepted submission Waiter releases it after completion or device loss UMD, KMD, and firmware split

entries.heading: Put mechanisms at the lowest layer that can enforce them
entries.text: Terms here Runtime = model execution orchestration UMD = userspace device library KMD = privileged host driver Firmware = device-side scheduler and control Responsibility Runtime / UMD KMD Firmware Do not do Discovery Enumerate device nodes and select compatible target Bind PCI IDs, publish capabilities and health Report hardware/firmware ABI and engine inventory Infer capabilities from board name Artifact Parse semantic metadata, choose variants, bind buffers Validate top-level sizes, compatibility and access Validate every command and program section used Trust compiler-generated bytes because they are signed by the same process Memory Choose usage, reuse, import, copy and synchronization Allocate/pin/import, map to IOMMU, enforce context and quota Use only registered IOVA windows and declared access Expose physical addresses to userspace or firmware commands Submission Batch commands, choose queue, attach trace and deadline Validate handles and publish protected descriptors Arbitrate resources, execute and complete Let userspace rewrite a descriptor after validation Interrupt Wait through poll/eventfd and drain completions Own MSI-X, acknowledge cause, schedule completion work, wake waiters Write CQ before MSI-X and moderate according to contract Depend on a userspace process to mask a fatal interrupt Analog state Select compatible characterization and retry/fallback policy Serialize privileged programming/reset and expose health Apply calibration, remap, program/verify, monitor saturation/drift Treat calibration files as ordinary unvalidated model constants Recovery Cancel work, rebuild session, recompile/rebind or fall back Quiesce DMA, reset context/function, coordinate AER and device loss Abort engines, capture fault, reset domains and increment generation Continue using handles from before reset Tenstorrent lesson to adapt: Tenstorrent publishes separate tt-kmd and tt-umd repositories; its UMD requires the KMD and handles IOMMU/host-memory configuration. Reuse the separation, testing habits, packaging ideas, and observability patterns. Do not copy its Tensix-specific address spaces, TLB model, queue protocol, or ioctl ABI into an Analog CIM device whose hardware contract is different. Kernel-mode driver (KMD) skeleton

entries.heading: Probe in dependency order; remove in reverse after quiescing DMA
entries.text: The skeleton shows order and failure ownership, not drop-in production code. Select current managed PCI APIs for the supported kernel range, implement every unwind path, and test probe failure after each resource acquisition. Terms here KMD = Kernel-Mode Driver IRQ = Interrupt Request DMA = Direct Memory Access Probe = Linux device initialization callback Proposed Linux PCI probe path Enable, claim, map, configure DMA, IRQ, firmware, then expose userspace static int acim_probe(struct pci_dev *pdev, const struct pci_device_id *id) { struct acim_dev *adev; const struct firmware *fw = NULL; int ret, i; ret = pcim_enable_device(pdev); if (ret) return ret; ret = pcim_iomap_regions(pdev, BIT(0), "acim"); if (ret) return ret; adev = devm_kzalloc(&pdev->dev, sizeof(*adev), GFP_KERNEL); if (!adev) return -ENOMEM; adev->bar0 = pcim_iomap_table(pdev)[0]; pci_set_drvdata(pdev, adev); ret = acim_read_and_validate_caps(adev); /* ROM-visible; no DMA yet */ if (ret) return ret; if (adev->caps.dma_bits != 32 && adev->caps.dma_bits != 64) return -EPROTO; ret = dma_set_mask_and_coherent(&pdev->dev, DMA_BIT_MASK(adev->caps.dma_bits)); if (ret) return dev_err_probe(&pdev->dev, ret, "unsupported DMA mask\n"); pci_set_master(pdev); /* device may now initiate DMA */ ret = acim_alloc_admin_rings(adev); /* dma_alloc_coherent */ if (ret) goto err_clear_master; ret = pci_alloc_irq_vectors(pdev, 1, adev->caps.max_vectors, PCI_IRQ_MSI | PCI_IRQ_MSIX); if (ret < 0) goto err_free_rings; adev->nr_vectors = ret; for (i = 0; i < adev->nr_vectors; ++i) { ret = request_threaded_irq(pci_irq_vector(pdev, i), acim_irq, acim_irq_thread, 0, "acim", adev); if (ret) goto err_free_irqs; } ret = request_firmware(&fw, adev->caps.firmware_name, &pdev->dev); if (ret) goto err_free_irqs; ret = acim_boot_firmware(adev, fw); /* reset, load, hash, start, ABI */ release_firmware(fw); if (ret) goto err_free_irqs; ret = acim_register_accel_or_chardev(adev); /* userspace opens only now */ if (ret) goto err_quiesce; return 0; err_quiesce: acim_quiesce_and_reset(adev); err_free_irqs: while (i--) free_irq(pci_irq_vector(pdev, i), adev); err_free_vectors: pci_free_irq_vectors(pdev); err_free_rings: acim_free_admin_rings(adev); err_clear_master: pci_clear_master(pdev); return ret; } 1. Block Stop new opens/submits Mark device removing or lost; wake waiters with a terminal error. 2. Quiesce Mask and drain Disable queues, stop engines and DMA, synchronize IRQ handlers. 3. Reclaim Finish ownership Signal/cancel fences, unmap streaming DMA, detach dma-buf and unpin pages. 4. Release IRQ and rings Free vectors, coherent control memory, firmware state and device node. 5. Disable Clear bus master Confirm no bus transaction remains before managed BAR/device release. Important: do not enable processing engines or expose a device node immediately after pci_set_master() . First validate the register ABI, allocate protected control rings, install interrupts, boot compatible firmware, and complete a health handshake. A failed firmware boot is a detected device that is not ready for userspace. User-mode driver (UMD) skeleton

entries.heading: Expose a transport-neutral HAL to the runtime
entries.text: The application should not issue ioctls directly. The UMD translates stable SDK objects into Linux UAPI objects and can later support VFIO, simulator, Windows, or an SoC transport without changing model execution. Terms here UMD = User-Mode Driver HAL = Hardware Abstraction Layer API = callable source interface ioctl = Linux device-control system call Proposed C HAL surface Opaque handles, explicit ownership, stable status values AcimStatus acimEnumerate(AcimDeviceInfo *items, size_t *count); AcimStatus acimOpen(uint32_t index, const AcimOpenOptions *, AcimDevice **out); AcimStatus acimQueryCaps(AcimDevice *, AcimCaps *out); AcimStatus acimCreateContext(AcimDevice *, const AcimContextDesc *, AcimContext **out); AcimStatus acimCreateBuffer(AcimContext *, const AcimBufferDesc *, AcimBuffer **out); AcimStatus acimImportDmaBuf(AcimContext *, int fd, const AcimImportDesc *, AcimBuffer **out); AcimStatus acimMapBuffer(AcimBuffer *, AcimMapMode, void **ptr); AcimStatus acimFlushBuffer(AcimBuffer *, size_t offset, size_t bytes); AcimStatus acimLoadExecutable(AcimContext *, const void *acx, size_t bytes, AcimExecutable **out); AcimStatus acimCreateQueue(AcimContext *, const AcimQueueDesc *, AcimQueue **out); AcimStatus acimSubmit(AcimQueue *, const AcimSubmission *, AcimEvent **out); AcimStatus acimWait(AcimEvent *, uint64_t timeout_ns, AcimCompletion *out); AcimStatus acimQueryFault(AcimContext *, AcimFaultReport *out); AcimStatus acimResetContext(AcimContext *); void acimReleaseEvent(AcimEvent *); void acimReleaseQueue(AcimQueue *); void acimReleaseExecutable(AcimExecutable *); void acimReleaseBuffer(AcimBuffer *); void acimReleaseContext(AcimContext *); void acimClose(AcimDevice *); Capability cache Cache immutable identity only. Refresh health, topology epoch, thermal state, and calibration validity before binding work. immutable_caps != live_state Thread safety Document object-level concurrency. Queues may be single producer first; device/context queries and waits should be safe across threads. one owner per mutable queue tail Fork and exec Use close-on-exec FDs. Either reject use after fork or reinitialize explicitly; never duplicate live queue ownership accidentally. O_CLOEXEC + PID generation check Timeouts Use monotonic nanoseconds and distinguish queue wait timeout from device execution timeout and reset timeout. WAIT_TIMEOUT != DEVICE_HANG Diagnostics Every failure carries stable status, source layer, context/queue/command IDs, firmware code, reset epoch, and a human-readable message. status + structured detail Backend parity Functional, statistical, cycle, VFIO-lab, and KMD hardware backends run the same conformance suite. same artifact, buffers, events, errors DMA and interrupt dataflow

entries.heading: Map only for the device lifetime of the transfer, then complete ownership
entries.text: Use coherent DMA for small long-lived queue/control structures and streaming mappings or managed buffer objects for payloads. The DMA address returned by the kernel is a device bus address, not a CPU physical address. Terms here DMA = Direct Memory Access IOMMU = address translation and isolation IOVA = device-visible DMA address MSI-X = completion/fault notification 1. Create/import Buffer object KMD allocates or imports pages and records owner, size, usage and direction. 2. Map IOMMU / DMA API Create IOVA or scatter/gather mapping; check every mapping result. 3. Publish Validated descriptor Write command and ring fields, transfer ownership, then ring doorbell. 4. Execute DMA + engines H2D stage, analog/digital compute, D2H result; enforce range and direction. 5. Complete CQ + MSI-X Device writes completion before interrupt; KMD acknowledges and wakes waiter. 6. Reclaim Fence then unmap CPU reads result only after completion/sync; unmap, detach, or retain for reuse. Producer and consumer ordering Linux kernel pseudocode for coherent ring memory plus MMIO doorbell /* KMD producer: descriptor fields before ownership and MMIO notification */ sq[idx].command_iova = cpu_to_le64(cmd_iova); sq[idx].command_bytes = cpu_to_le32(cmd_bytes); sq[idx].user_cookie = cpu_to_le64(cookie); sq[idx].generation = cpu_to_le32(adev->generation); dma_wmb(); WRITE_ONCE(sq[idx].owner, ACIM_OWNER_DEVICE); writel(new_tail, adev->bar0 + ACIM_SQ_DOORBELL(qid)); /* KMD completion path: ownership before completion fields */ if (READ_ONCE(cq[idx].owner) == ACIM_OWNER_HOST) { dma_rmb(); complete_submission(le64_to_cpu(cq[idx].user_cookie), le32_to_cpu(cq[idx].status)); } /* Before reset/teardown, force a posted MMIO write to reach the endpoint. */ writel(ACIM_CONTROL_QUIESCE, adev->bar0 + ACIM_DEVICE_CONTROL); readl(adev->bar0 + ACIM_DEVICE_STATUS); Ordering boundary: coherent memory does not remove the need for barriers. dma_wmb() and dma_rmb() order shared DMA memory; they do not themselves order arbitrary MMIO. Use the kernel MMIO accessors and the hardware protocol's readback rule. MSI/MSI-X is preferred because PCI ordering ensures the device's preceding memory writes arrive before the interrupt-generating write. First inference sequence

entries.heading: One correlation ID follows the frame across every boundary
entries.text: The sequence assumes weights were programmed and verified during session creation. Do not erase/program flash weights for every frame. A reset or changed placement/calibration epoch invalidates the resident program binding. Terms here ORT = ONNX Runtime BO = Buffer Object SQ / CQ = command/completion rings IRQ = Interrupt Request Application / ONNX Runtime (ORT) Runtime / User-Mode Driver (UMD) Kernel-Mode Driver (KMD) Firmware Direct Memory Access (DMA) + ACiM engines 01 Run(frame, correlation_id) -> bind executable and input 02 CREATE/IMPORT BO + validate context -> 03 SUBMIT handles, offsets, sizes, deadline -> 04 Validate, map IOVA, publish SQ, doorbell -> 05 Validate command, reserve SRAM/engines, start DMA -> 06 H2D, analog MVM, ADC/reconstruct, digital stages, D2H 07 <- CQ record then MSI-X 08 <- IRQ ack, drain CQ, signal event/fence 09 <- completion, output BO, counters, analog status 10 Decode/NMS; release or recycle event and buffers Horizontal direction shows request or completion ownership; empty lanes remain active but do not own that transition. Firmware implementation

entries.heading: Boot establishes trust; the scheduler validates every submission again
entries.text: Terms here ROM = immutable first-stage boot code Firmware = device-resident scheduler/control code ABI = host/device binary contract Generation = reset epoch rejecting stale work ROM Reset-safe state DMA off, IRQ masked, mailbox available, immutable identity readable. KMD Load image Request firmware, validate host-side container, stage image and command ROM. ROM Authenticate + start Verify image according to product security policy, initialize SRAM and engines. Firmware Publish ABI Version, build hash, capabilities, generation, health, queue requirements. KMD Enable userspace Negotiate compatible ABI, run admin loopback, then register the device node. Proposed firmware scheduler loop Validation precedes resource reservation and side effects for (;;) { wait_for_doorbell_or_admin_event(); while (sq_has_entry()) { SqEntry e = sq_acquire(); Validation v = validate_entry(e, device_generation, context_table); if (!v.ok) { cq_complete(e.cookie, STATUS_INVALID, v.fault_code); continue; } Command cmd = map_and_validate_command(v.context, e.command_iova, e.command_bytes); if (!cmd.ok) { cq_complete(e.cookie, STATUS_INVALID, cmd.fault_code); continue; } Reservation r = reserve_resources(cmd.engines, cmd.sram, cmd.deadline); if (!r.ok) { defer_or_complete_busy(e, r); continue; } TraceScope trace(e.cookie, cmd.graph_correlation_id); Result result = execute_dma_analog_digital(cmd, r); release_resources(r); cq_publish_before_msix(e.cookie, result); } service_health_watchdog_and_calibration_events(); } Accepted Descriptor owned Generation and context valid. Validated All ranges legal Opcode, buffers, artifact and profile checked. Reserved Resources held SRAM, DMA, array and digital engine assigned. Running Watchdog armed Trace and performance counters active. Completing Writes visible Output and CQ committed before MSI-X. Terminal OK or fault Exactly one completion and resources released. Analog-specific device contract

entries.heading: PCIe moves bytes; the analog lifecycle determines whether those bytes are correct
entries.text: A digital NPU can often load deterministic code and weights. An Analog CIM board also needs a controlled program, verify, characterize, bind, monitor, and refresh lifecycle. These operations are privileged and should not be hidden inside an ordinary inference command. Terms here MVM = Matrix-Vector Multiplication DAC = Digital-to-Analog Converter ADC = Analog-to-Digital Converter PVT = Process, Voltage, Temperature 1. Package Weight program Logical tensor, slices, sign method, target cells, tolerances, hash. 2. Program Device operation Erase/program pulse policy and wear budget are device-specific. 3. Verify Readback quality Detect bad cell/row/column, retry within limits, record residual error. 4. Calibrate Converters + paths Gain/offset, ADC range, temperature bucket, digital correction. 5. Bind Logical program ID Compiler placement maps to healthy physical resources and profile epoch. 6. Monitor Inference health Saturation, drift, ECC/fault, temperature and accuracy sentinels. Artifact / state Required fields Owner Invalidated by Target descriptor Array geometry, supported precision/modes, converter limits, digital ops, SRAM and alignment Hardware team; compiler consumes Hardware revision or incompatible firmware ABI Characterization profile Chip/lot/device ID, temperature/voltage bucket, gain/offset/noise, bad resources, measurement method, timestamp Silicon/test team; runtime verifies Age, PVT excursion, repair/remap, recalibration policy Program manifest Model/weight hashes, physical placement, slice/sign scheme, programming algorithm, verify tolerance, wear count Compiler + privileged service Reprogram, remap, failed verify, reset if state is volatile Live health map Unavailable rows/columns/tiles/converters, saturation, thermal, calibration age, topology epoch Firmware + KMD Any new fault, reset, thermal transition or service action Executable binding Artifact hash, program IDs, physical resources, profile hash, device generation, fallback variant Runtime/UMD Any mismatch in the fields above Fail closed: if the runtime cannot prove that the resident program, physical placement, calibration profile, live fault map, firmware ABI, and executable agree, it must rebind/reprogram or choose a digital fallback. Silently running with a stale analog profile creates an accuracy failure that ordinary DMA and queue tests will not catch. Fault, reset, and security

entries.heading: Every failure has an owner, a containment boundary, and a terminal event
entries.text: Terms here AER = PCIe Advanced Error Reporting ECC = Error-Correcting Code FLR = Function Level Reset Fail closed = reject work when compatibility or safety is unknown Failure Detect Contain Recover Evidence retained Malformed ioctl KMD size, flags, reserved fields, overflow and handle checks Reject before allocation or MMIO Return stable -EINVAL / -E2BIG / -ENOENT Rate-limited audit counter, command ID Illegal IOVA IOMMU fault plus firmware range check Stop offending context/queue; do not reset unrelated contexts first Abort context, signal all fences, reset context or function if needed IOVA, access type, context, command, engine Execution timeout Firmware watchdog and host deadline Stop queue, then engine/reset domain Queue abort -> context reset -> function reset escalation Last command, trace tail, engine status, temperature Firmware panic Fatal mailbox/IRQ, heartbeat loss Mask new work and stop DMA Capture bounded dump, reset, reload, increment generation Build hash, panic code, logs, registers, in-flight IDs PCIe AER PCI core AER callbacks and counters error_detected() quiesces without new I/O Recover, slot reset and reinitialize, or mark permanently lost AER severity, requester, TLP header where available Analog saturation/drift ADC saturation, sentinel inference, profile age, temperature Stop affected program/tile; preserve other healthy capacity Change range/profile, recalibrate, remap, retry or digital fallback Array/tile, inputs summary, profile, PVT, before/after error Uncorrectable array fault Program verify, health scan, accuracy sentinel Remove row/column/tile from live resource map Rebind spare/replica or recompile placement; increment topology epoch Fault location, first seen, wear, remap and accuracy result No raw addresses Userspace passes handles and offsets. KMD resolves IOVA and validates overflow; firmware validates ranges again. offset + bytes <= BO.size No mutable-after-check Copy command metadata into protected memory or enforce ownership so a process cannot change it after validation. validate -> publish immutable descriptor No global reset first Contain to queue, context, engine, tile, then function when hardware supports it. smallest effective reset domain No stale completion Generation and context identify work. Device loss completes every waiter exactly once with a terminal status. cookie + generation + terminal status No debug backdoor Gate raw BAR/SRAM/register access behind build-time and privilege policy; disable it in production images. debug aperture off by default No silent firmware swap Record image hash and ABI; enforce signature/rollback policy according to the product threat model. measured boot metadata in support bundle Profiling and correlation

entries.heading: A fast array is irrelevant if the frame stalls at a boundary you cannot see
entries.text: Terms here H2D = Host-to-Device transfer D2H = Device-to-Host transfer Correlation ID = identifier joining one request across layers Tail latency = high-percentile slow-request latency Host Queue and copy time CPU preprocessing, BO allocation/import, map, submit, wait, postprocess, scheduler delay. PCIe Bytes and efficiency H2D/D2H bytes, DMA segments, payload size, link width/speed, replay/AER, effective bandwidth. Device digital Movement and stalls SRAM bank conflicts, DMA idle, digital kernels, format transforms, partial sums, dependencies. Device analog Useful work and correction Array utilization, DAC/ADC cycles, saturation, retries, calibration, reconstruction and fallback. Trace field Origin Purpose Required clock relation graph_node_id Compiler debug map Relate device work to original ONNX node/subgraph Identifier only correlation_id Application/runtime Join frame/request across host, KMD, firmware and engines Identifier only command_id / cookie UMD/KMD Queue ownership, wait and completion diagnosis Identifier only host_submit_ns KMD monotonic clock Host queue and interrupt latency CLOCK_MONOTONIC nanoseconds device_start/end_cycles Firmware hardware timer DMA, analog and digital stage duration Publish timer frequency and reset epoch profile/topology epoch Firmware/runtime Explain numerical or performance changes after calibration/remap Monotonic per device generation Minimum profiler output: one line per command with model/artifact hash, graph node, context, queue, correlation ID, input/output bytes, queue delay, H2D, compute stages, D2H, interrupt/wakeup, analog profile, saturation/retry count, status, and reset generation. Aggregate only after raw correlation works. Implementation repository

entries.heading: The skeleton is reasonable; make code, artifacts, data, and loaders traceable
entries.text: A directory tree is only the first layer of the design. Every owned source path should produce a named build target or validated data file, identify who loads it, state how long it remains valid, and name the smallest test that proves the boundary. The separate repository blueprint covers CMake, compilers, CI, GoogleTest, and contribution mechanics in greater depth; this section maps those mechanics onto ACiM board boot and model execution. Terms here RTL = Register-Transfer Level hardware UAPI = kernel/userspace interface files CI = Continuous Integration Build target = named output in the build graph Loader = component that places an artifact into its execution context Generated code = mechanical output from the protocol schema Repository verdict: a monorepo is reasonable for the first end-to-end vertical slice because protocol, simulator, compiler, runtime, KMD, firmware, tools, and tests can change atomically. Split a component only when ownership, access control, release cadence, or build tooling requires it. A split repository must consume a versioned protocol package and run the same cross-version compatibility suite before release. Proposed source layout Source, generated contracts, platform integration, tests, and packaging have different owners acim-stack/ |-- CMakeLists.txt |-- CMakePresets.json |-- .github/ | `-- workflows/ # fast, hardware, nightly, release lanes |-- cmake/ | `-- toolchains/ # host and controller cross builds |-- configs/ | |-- targets/chip-rev.yaml # arrays, SRAM, ISA, precision, costs | |-- boards/pcie-card.yaml # IDs, BARs, DMA, MSI-X, clocks | |-- boards/integrated-soc.yaml # MMIO, DMA, SMMU, IRQ, power domains | |-- models/yolo.yaml # preprocessing, shapes, accuracy gates | `-- test-matrices/ # simulator, FPGA, board, PVT lanes |-- spec/ # authoritative binary contracts | |-- registers.yaml | |-- queue.yaml | |-- firmware_abi.yaml | |-- artifact.schema.json | |-- calibration.schema.json | `-- trace.schema.json |-- tools/codegen/ # schema validation and emitters |-- generated/ # optional distributable generated output | |-- include/hw/ | |-- rtl/ | |-- firmware/ | `-- docs/ |-- include/ | |-- uapi/linux/acim_accel.h # stable userspace/kernel contract | `-- acim/ # supported SDK and HAL interfaces |-- compiler/ | |-- import/ dialect/ transforms/ | `-- target/ scheduling/ packaging/ |-- runtime/umd/ | |-- device.cpp buffer.cpp queue.cpp artifact.cpp | `-- backends/kmd_linux.cpp fake.cpp cosim.cpp |-- driver/kmd/ | |-- pci.c platform.c uapi.c context.c memory.c queue.c irq.c | `-- firmware.c reset.c trace.c health.c Kbuild |-- firmware/ | |-- boot/ mailbox/ scheduler/ dma/ | `-- analog/ digital/ health/ trace/ tests/ |-- kernels/ | |-- analog/ # array programs and descriptors | `-- digital/ # DSP/vector/scalar fallback kernels |-- sim/ | |-- functional/ analog/ cycle/ | `-- pcie_model/ platform_model/ # transport, reset and fault models |-- platforms/ | |-- linux-pcie/ # udev, module config, packages | |-- linux-soc/ # DTB, clocks, power, platform package | `-- embedded/board-name/ # Buildroot/Yocto and boot scripts |-- apps/ | |-- acim-smoke/ | `-- acim-yolo/ |-- models/ | |-- manifests/ quantization/ | `-- golden/ # small redistributable test tensors |-- calibration/ | `-- fixtures/ # synthetic/non-production device profiles |-- tools/ | |-- acim-info/ acim-fw/ acim-memtest/ | `-- acim-trace/ acim-health/ acim-support-bundle/ |-- scripts/ | |-- build/ test/ package/ | `-- ci/ # orchestration, not duplicated test logic |-- tests/ | |-- unit/ contract/ smoke/ integration/ | |-- differential/ fault-injection/ end-to-end/ | `-- performance/ soak/ qualification/ |-- packaging/ `-- docs/ spec/ is authoritative CI regenerates headers and fails on a diff. Every register includes access, owner, reset value, side effects and revision. generated/ is mechanical Generate into the build tree by default. Keep a source-tree mirror only when separate RTL/KMD builds or source packages require it; CI must regenerate with no diff. Generator version and schema hash travel with the output. uapi/ is append-only in behavior Run ABI layout checks on 32-bit and 64-bit builds; explicit reserved fields replace compiler padding. configs/ is validated product data A chip target, board, model, and test matrix have schemas, units, revisions, and compatibility tests. They are not informal command-line flags. platforms/ owns boot integration Keep PCIe packages, integrated-SoC resources, and embedded BSP files outside runtime logic. The same UMD API should work after any supported platform reaches READY. Transport models come before the board Model PCIe BAR or integrated MMIO side effects, ring wrap, ordering, interrupts, reset epochs, malformed commands and DMA faults. tools/ are release deliverables Enumeration, firmware, memory test, trace, health and support bundle are necessary to debug customer systems. models/ stores provenance, not arbitrary datasets Record model/dataset versions, preprocessing, quantization statistics, artifact hash, board profile and expected metrics. Keep only permitted small golden inputs in Git. calibration/ contains test fixtures only Model quantization data and per-chip analog calibration are different. Production chip profiles belong in the provisioning/service store, not source control. out/ is ignored build output Never mix source with binaries, firmware, model artifacts, board images, traces, or test results. Package them from a reproducible preset and manifest.

entries.heading: Build output is a versioned handoff, not another source directory
entries.text: Illustrative output layout Produced below an ignored out/<preset>/ directory or CI artifact store out/linux-x86_64-release/ |-- host/ | |-- bin/acim-run | |-- bin/acim-smi | `-- lib/libacim_runtime.so |-- kmd/acim_accel.ko |-- device/ | |-- acim-fw.elf # optional programmable controller | |-- acim-fw.bin | |-- acim-fw.map | `-- acim-fw.sym |-- generated/protocol-manifest.json |-- models/yolo-int8.acx |-- packages/acim-sdk.tar.zst `-- evidence/build-manifest.json out/edge-board-release/ |-- images/sdcard.img |-- images/Image |-- images/board.dtb |-- images/rootfs.ext4 `-- evidence/bsp-manifest.json Host code acim-run , acim-smi , and libacim_runtime.so execute on the Linux host CPU. They never execute inside the analog array. Privileged host code acim_accel.ko executes in the Linux kernel and owns PCIe, IOMMU, DMA mappings, interrupts, reset, and firmware loading. Device control code acim-fw.elf/bin executes on a device controller only when the hardware has a programmable CPU. Keep symbols and the link map for debug. Model executable data yolo-int8.acx contains target-specific commands, constants, weight placement, kernel references, metadata, and debug maps; it is loaded by the runtime. Embedded host image The SD/eMMC image contains the host BSP and userspace. It is separate from device firmware and may be absent for a workstation PCIe card. Evidence Every package records source commits, dirty state, compiler/tool versions, schema hashes, target/profile IDs, ABI ranges, and artifact hashes. 1. Select inputs spec/ + configs/ Protocol schemas, chip target, board profile, model manifest, toolchain preset. 2. Generate tools/codegen/ Validate schemas; emit C/C++/firmware/RTL definitions, docs, hashes, and compatibility fixtures. 3. Build host SDK + UMD + KMD CMake/Ninja builds userspace; Kbuild builds the module; package symbols and manifests. 4. Build device Firmware + kernels Cross-compile, link to the controller memory map, emit ELF/bin/map/symbols and size report. 5. Compile model ONNX to .acx Use target and calibration inputs to lower, schedule, place, package, and preserve debug mapping. 6. Package + prove Installable set Run contract/smoke tests; assemble host, device, model, optional BSP, and evidence manifests. Source owner Named output Loader / consumer Validity lifetime Smallest proof spec/ + tools/codegen/ acim_protocol_codegen : generated headers, RTL package, docs, protocol manifest Compiler for KMD, UMD, firmware, simulator and RTL Protocol version Regenerate-with-no-diff plus cross-language encode/decode fixture driver/kmd/ Kbuild modules : acim_accel.ko and debug symbols; or built-in object Linux module loader or kernel image link Host boot/module load Probe, query caps, remove, reprobe, and leak check firmware/ + kernels/ acim_firmware , when present: controller ELF/bin/map and kernel package KMD, remoteproc, boot ROM, or JTAG lab flow Device boot epoch; kernels may be session resident READY handshake plus no-op/admin queue command runtime/umd/ acim_runtime : runtime library and HAL backends Application dynamic loader Host process/session Same buffer/queue test against fake, co-sim, and KMD backends compiler/ acim-compile : .acx executable artifact Runtime validates and extracts command/program payloads for firmware Target/profile compatibility; then session binding Inspect, validate, deserialize, and execute one golden MVM platforms/embedded/ edge_board_image : bootloader, kernel, DTB, rootfs and media image Host boot ROM/bootloader Embedded host boot/update slot QEMU-supported BSP boot or physical serial boot to SDK health check calibration/fixtures/ plus external provisioning store Test fixture or production per-device calibration/health profile Provisioning tool, runtime and firmware Chip, PVT range, age and calibration generation Integrity, serial/profile match, known-answer operation, stale-profile rejection

entries.heading: Boot flow: code is loaded, then capabilities and mutable state are negotiated
entries.text: 1. Host boot platforms/ Embedded only: bootloader, Linux, rootfs and DTB. A workstation PCIe flow starts at KMD probe on its supported OS. 2. KMD probe pci.c or platform.c Reads PCI BAR/caps or platform MMIO/DT resources; creates device state; configures DMA, IOMMU/SMMU, IRQ/MSI-X, reset, power and trace. 3. Device control driver/kmd/firmware.c Works with firmware/boot/ ; loads firmware when present, checks image/ABI, then starts the controller or verifies fixed RTL control. 4. Admin queues driver/kmd/memory.c Works with queue.c ; allocates rings and exchanges IOVAs, depth, generation, vectors, heartbeat and trace clock. 5. Publish UAPI driver/kmd/uapi.c Works with health.c ; exposes the device only after READY and returns capabilities, health, calibration generation and ABI. 6. Open runtime runtime/umd/device.cpp Queries caps; creates context/queue; records run identity; rejects incompatible SDK, firmware or target. Boot step Executing code Data entering State produced Failure evidence Host boot Bootloader and Linux BSP Boot image, DTB, rootfs configuration PCIe root or platform bus, IOMMU/SMMU, filesystems, services Bootloader/earlycon/kernel serial log Device discovery PCI or platform KMD probe and reset modules PCI config/BARs or DT/MMIO resources, generated board constants and live caps Kernel device object, mapped MMIO, DMA mask, IRQ/MSI-X vectors Kernel tracepoint, AER/platform fault, IOMMU/SMMU and probe log Control-plane start Boot ROM, KMD firmware loader, optional controller firmware Firmware bytes/hash, entry point, compatibility range READY, boot epoch, firmware build/ABI, crash area Mailbox stage, ROM UART, JTAG/GDB, crash buffer Queue negotiation KMD queue/memory plus firmware scheduler Ring IOVAs, size, generation, IRQ/MSI-X vector, context limits Enabled admin/data queues and heartbeat Queue indices, descriptor dump, IRQ cause, timeout stage Userspace open UMD/HAL and KMD UAPI Requested API version, process identity and policy Context, Buffer Object namespace, queue/event handles errno, UAPI trace, negotiated capabilities and reset epoch

entries.heading: Model flow: separate immutable weights, per-device calibration, session state, and request tensors
entries.text: 1. Offline compile compiler/ Inputs: ONNX, target, and model-quantization statistics. Output: commands, constants, placement and debug map in .acx . 2. Validate artifact artifact.cpp Checks hashes, target, ABI, tensor contract, required features, scratch size and fallback variants. 3. Program session firmware/analog Combines immutable weights with chip calibration/health; programs, verifies and remaps arrays; returns program handle. 4. Submit request buffer.cpp + queue.cpp Per-request input BO and descriptor reference resident program, output BO, deadline and correlation ID. 5. Execute graph DMA + ACiM + digital Moves activations, performs MVM/ADC/reconstruction and digital operators; weights remain resident when legal. 6. Complete + inspect CQ + runtime + app Returns output tensor, status, counters and trace IDs; compares selected checkpoints with the golden model. Data class Examples Owner Lifetime Must invalidate when Executable code KMD, host runtime, controller firmware, digital microcode Packaging/KMD/boot ROM Module, process, boot epoch or kernel version ABI, security, target or firmware generation is incompatible Immutable model data Graph commands, weights, scales, constants, debug map Compiler artifact and runtime Artifact version; may become session resident Artifact hash, target, layout or precision contract changes Per-device state Calibration, defect map, remap, temperature/voltage bucket Manufacturing/service plus firmware Chip/profile generation and valid PVT range Serial mismatch, age/temperature threshold, recharacterization or fault update Per-session state Program handle, resident placement, context, queues, mapped BOs Runtime, KMD and firmware Session and reset generation Reset, firmware restart, device loss, remap or calibration generation changes Per-request data Input/output tensors, descriptor, deadline, dependencies, correlation ID Application/runtime and queue owners Submission through terminal completion Completion, abort, timeout or reset releases ownership safely Evidence data Logs, traces, counters, raw ADC samples, tensor checkpoints Support/profiling tools Run bundle and retention policy Never silently reused as current calibration or executable input Staged delivery

entries.heading: Reach the board through nine evidence-producing milestones
entries.text: Each milestone is a vertical slice with owned code, a reproducible operation, named boundary data, a measurable exit gate, and an explicit capability that it unlocks. Transport semantics remain common while an integrated SoC uses MMIO/DMA/SMMU/IRQ and a PCIe device uses BAR/DMA/IOMMU/MSI-X. Terms here Protocol v0 = first versioned hardware/software contract FPGA = Field-Programmable Gate Array prototype MVM = Matrix-Vector Multiplication Exit gate = evidence required before depending on this milestone Unlock = new work that becomes technically meaningful after the gate passes Qualification = evidence required before product release Two plans with different jobs: the ten-stage verification ladder answers where and at what fidelity a test runs, from native model through silicon. These nine delivery milestones answer which dependency-ordered code slice the team implements. For example, the queue slice should pass first in the fake backend, then QEMU/co-simulation, FPGA, and finally silicon without changing its descriptor semantics or whether the physical transport is integrated or PCIe. Phase A | milestones 1-2 Contracts and virtual hardware Prove interfaces and failure behavior without a physical device. host CI | fake | co-sim Phase B | milestones 3-5 Device and transport Boot, transfer exact bytes, and complete commands reliably. integrated SoC | PCIe | FPGA Phase C | milestones 6-8 Analog compute and model Correlate one MVM, a subgraph, then the complete workload. calibrated simulator | silicon Phase D | milestone 9 Product operations Package, isolate, recover, update, and diagnose supported systems. platform matrix | qualification

entries.heading: Dependency graph: each exit artifact becomes the next milestone's input
entries.text: M1 | Contract Protocol package Registers, UAPI, queues, faults, trace schema, fixtures, and compatibility rules. feeds simulator + KMD + firmware + RTL M2 | Virtual device Transport behavior MMIO/BAR state, DMA address spaces, interrupts, reset, ordering, and injected faults. feeds physical probe expectations M3 | Boot READY device Identity, mapped resources, firmware/control ABI, capabilities, health, and reset epoch. feeds memory and queue setup M4 | Memory Verified data path BO ownership, IOVA mappings, exact payloads, cache rules, DMA counters, and fault cleanup. feeds trusted ring memory M5 | Commands Reliable execution path SQ/CQ ownership, doorbells, IRQ/MSI-X, timeout, abort, and one terminal completion. feeds analog command transport Transport foundation Exact bytes + deterministic completion required before numerical correlation Compute foundation M6 | One MVM Calibrated operation Resident weight program, chip profile, raw ADC, reconstructed output, error distribution, and mitigation cost. feeds legal analog placement M7 | Subgraph Hybrid device island Partition, SRAM schedule, boundary tensors, analog/digital trace, fallback, and resident program handle. feeds complete model assembly M8 | Full model Qualified workload Accuracy, placement, latency percentiles, throughput, energy, thermal behavior, and recovery evidence. feeds product regression baseline M9 | Operations Release evidence Packages, compatibility matrix, isolation, updates, rollback, recovery, health, and support bundles. feeds release qualification

entries.heading: Sequence graph: code, commands, tensors, and evidence cross different owners
entries.text: Build / compiler / CI Host runtime / KMD Device control DMA + ACiM + digital Evidence store M1 Generate protocol package -> compile host consumers ABI/layout report M2 Submit conformance suite -> virtual device Deterministic protocol/fault trace M3 Probe resources, reset, load/start control plane -> Boot stages and image/ABI hashes M3 <- READY, caps, health, calibration and reset generation Cold-boot and failure bundle M4 Register BO/IOVA + submit loopback command -> Mapping, ownership and command record M4 DMA pattern H2D/D2H -> verify guards -> unmap Pattern, guard, counter and fault result M5 Publish SQ + doorbell + deadline -> Descriptor and ordering trace M5 <- CQ status + IRQ/MSI-X + wake event One terminal status per cookie M6 Program weights + bind chip profile -> Program/verify, placement and profile IDs M6 Start MVM -> DAC/array/ADC/reconstruct Raw values, error, cycles and energy M7 Load and dispatch hybrid subgraph -> Partition and SRAM schedule M7 Execute analog + digital island -> Boundary tensors and fallback trace M8 Dispatch declared validation and performance scenarios -> Run manifest, placement and scenario IDs M8 Execute full graph -> return detections and counters mAP, latency, power, thermal, recovery M9 Install/update qualification set -> exercise supported host Compatibility and support bundle M9 Release gate accepts or rejects the evidence set Each row is an ownership handoff. The evidence lane stores machine-readable records keyed by build, artifact, device, reset generation, and run/correlation IDs.

entries.heading: Detailed implementation and exit gates
entries.text: Phase A

entries.heading: Contracts and virtual hardware
entries.text: Entry: architecture decisions are documented. Exit: host software can exercise the real command semantics and faults without silicon. 1 Freeze protocol v0 Create one machine-readable contract before KMD, firmware, simulator, and RTL implementations diverge. host CI | no board Implement spec/ , tools/codegen/ , generated C/C++/firmware/RTL definitions, Linux UAPI structures, version rules, ownership, endianness, reset values, and memory ordering. Exercise Regenerate every consumer; encode and decode golden capability, mailbox, SQ, CQ, fault, and trace fixtures across languages; reject unknown major versions and nonzero reserved fields. Data and evidence Schema and generator hashes, generated diff, structure sizes/offsets, round-trip fixtures, compatibility matrix, and malformed-input results. Exit gate Regeneration is clean; all consumers agree bit-for-bit; old/new combinations behave exactly as declared; fuzzed lengths, enum values, overflow, and alignment fail safely. Unlocks milestone 2: simulator, RTL, KMD, and firmware teams can implement against the same stable contract in parallel. 2 Build the transport and device model Represent the control registers, host/device memory, queues, interrupts, reset, and faults before a board is required. native fake | QEMU/co-sim Implement sim/pcie_model/ and/or sim/platform_model/ , fake/co-sim HAL backends, MMIO side effects, DMA address spaces, IRQ/MSI-X, posted-write behavior, reset epochs, firmware mailbox, and fault injection. Exercise Run the real UMD queue library against the model; wrap rings, fill queues, reorder notifications, drop/duplicate interrupts, issue malformed descriptors, reset in flight, and simulate illegal DMA. Data and evidence Register snapshots, queue memory, DMA transactions, interrupt events, command/fault timelines, deterministic seeds, and expected KMD/firmware status codes. Exit gate The same conformance suite passes for every transport enabled by the target profile; every accepted command has one terminal completion; every injected fault is bounded and reproducible. Unlocks milestone 3: physical discovery and boot can be compared with a known protocol model instead of debugged from intuition. Phase B

entries.heading: Device and transport bring-up
entries.text: Entry: protocol/model tests pass. Exit: one physical device moves exact data and completes queued work across reset and interrupt corner cases. 3 Discover, reset, and boot the device Establish identity, resources, firmware/control-plane readiness, health, and a repeatable teardown path. integrated SoC | PCIe FPGA/board Implement driver/kmd/platform.c and/or pci.c , reset.c , firmware.c , board/DTB integration, resource mapping, SMMU/IOMMU setup, IRQ/MSI-X allocation, health handshake, and safe remove. Exercise Cold boot; read IDs/caps; map MMIO/BARs; start optional controller firmware; negotiate ABI and reset generation; publish the device node; open/close; remove/reprobe; force boot timeout and incompatible firmware. Data and evidence DTB/platform resources or PCI config, register map version, firmware hash/ABI, READY stages, health/calibration generation, serial log, KMD trace, AER or platform fault state. Exit gate Cold boot and controlled failure are deterministic; no device node appears before READY; teardown leaves no mapping/IRQ; repeated bind/reset succeeds, targeting 1000 cycles before qualification. Unlocks milestone 4: the host can safely allocate device-visible memory and test data movement without analog compute. 4 Pass DMA and shared-memory loopback Prove byte-exact ownership transfer through every supported buffer type, size, alignment, and mapping mode.
