SMMU/IOMMU | DMA | SRAM Implement driver/kmd/memory.c , firmware DMA handlers, BO allocation/import, IOVA registration, coherent admin memory, streaming payload mappings, cache synchronization, scatter/gather limits, and acim-memtest . Exercise Loop deterministic patterns H2D and D2H across boundary sizes, page crossings, unaligned requests, maximum segments, concurrent buffers, wrong direction, unmapped IOVA, context exit, timeout, and reset. Data and evidence BO handle, physical pages/scatterlist, IOVA, direction, bytes, pattern hash, guard regions, cache-operation trace, DMA counters, bandwidth, IOMMU/SMMU fault and cleanup record. Exit gate Payload and guards are exact for the complete matrix; illegal access is contained; every map has one unmap after completion/device loss; bandwidth is explained by transfer and memory counters. Unlocks milestone 5: queue failures can be investigated without wondering whether descriptor or completion memory is corrupt. 5 Pass queues and completion interrupts Prove command ownership, ordering, wakeup, timeout, abort, and reset semantics under concurrency. IRQ | MSI-X | polling Implement driver/kmd/queue.c , irq.c , runtime/umd/queue.cpp , firmware scheduler, SQ/CQ ownership barriers, doorbells, moderation, poll/event integration, watchdog, abort, and generation checks. Exercise Wrap and fill rings; run multiple queues/processes; switch polling/interrupt mode; delay, lose, and duplicate interrupts; complete out of order where legal; close during work; timeout, abort, reset, and submit stale entries. Data and evidence Producer/consumer indices, descriptor bytes, command cookie, queue/context/generation, doorbell and IRQ timestamps, CQ status, watchdog state, wakeup latency, and first-fault trace. Exit gate Every accepted cookie receives exactly one terminal status; no deadlock or queue corruption occurs at wrap/full; stale generations never execute; polling and interrupt paths return identical results. Unlocks milestone 6: analog numerical debugging can rely on a trustworthy command, transfer, and completion path. Phase C

entries.heading: Analog compute and model correlation
entries.text: Entry: transport is exact and recoverable. Exit: one operation, one subgraph, and one full model meet declared numerical and performance gates. 6 Execute one resident MVM Make the smallest analog operation observable from programmed weights through reconstructed output. analog simulator | calibrated device Implement compiler/target/ , kernels/analog/ , firmware programming/verify/remap, analog simulator, range/profile selection, raw ADC capture, reconstruction, saturation/retry reporting, and golden reference. Exercise Compile a tiny .acx ; program and verify a known weight block; bind the correct chip profile; run fixed vectors and corner values; force bad rows, saturation, stale calibration, remap, retry, and digital fallback. Data and evidence Weight/program hash, physical placement, defect/remap table, calibration ID/PVT, DAC codes, raw ADC codes, reconstructed values, golden accumulations, error distribution, cycles, energy, and temperature. Exit gate Program verify succeeds; error distribution stays inside the predeclared budget across required devices/PVT; first numerical divergence is identifiable; all mitigation cost is visible in cycles, arrays, and digital work. Unlocks milestone 7: compiler partitioning and SRAM scheduling can combine trusted analog and digital operations. 7 Execute a YOLO subgraph Prove one contiguous hybrid island with resident weights, local activation scheduling, and explicit fallback boundaries. simulator parity | one device Implement compiler/transforms/ , scheduling/memory planning, artifact loading, analog Conv/GEMM placement, digital activation/route operators, fallback, layer debugger, boundary tensor capture, and graph-to-command mapping. Exercise Compile a fixed Conv/activation/route island; program weights once; run one H2D input and one D2H output; sweep supported shapes; disable fusion to isolate layers; force digital fallback and one SRAM-pressure case. Data and evidence Partition report, target/artifact hash, resident program handle, SRAM allocation timeline, boundary tensors/distributions, command trace, fallback reason, H2D/D2H bytes, per-stage cycles, and saturation/retry counts. Exit gate Every boundary tensor meets its error budget; SRAM lifetimes do not overlap illegally; simulator/device placement agrees; fallback is numerically equivalent; repeated warm runs reuse weights and avoid unexplained transfers. Unlocks milestone 8: full-model accuracy and end-to-end latency become meaningful rather than hiding a broken layer or excessive host fallback. 8 Qualify end-to-end YOLO Measure the complete deployed workload, including preprocessing, fallback, postprocessing, power, thermal behavior, and recovery. validation set | performance lab Implement Versioned model/run manifests, complete application pipeline, validation harness, golden host backend, latency/power collection, profiler correlation, cold/warm scenarios, stream/queue policy, soak, and model-level recovery. Exercise Run the declared validation dataset; compare host, simulator, ACiM, and fallback variants; measure cold load, first inference, steady state, throughput, queue depth, thermal soak, calibration refresh, timeout, reset, and model rebind. Data and evidence Dataset/model/preprocess versions, detections, mAP and per-class deltas, fallback/operator placement, latency percentiles, FPS, energy/frame, clocks, temperature, transfer bytes, profiler timeline, and recovery bundles. Exit gate Pre-agreed accuracy and SLO thresholds pass on the complete pipeline; all host/off-chip work is disclosed; stage times explain end-to-end latency; independent reruns reproduce metrics inside declared variance. Unlocks milestone 9: product hardening can preserve a known-good workload while platform, update, isolation, and recovery behavior expands. Phase D

entries.heading: Product operations and supportability
entries.text: Entry: the target model meets numerical/performance gates. Exit: supported systems can install, isolate, update, recover, and produce actionable evidence. 9 Harden the product path Turn the working board stack into a maintainable platform with explicit compatibility, failure, and service behavior. platform/kernel matrix | qualification Implement packaging/ , platform integration, permissions, multi-process isolation, dma-buf where required, power states, AER or on-chip fault handling, reset escalation, firmware/model updates, rollback, diagnostics, profiler, and support-bundle tools. Exercise Clean install/uninstall; old/new ABI matrix; concurrent users; process death; suspend/resume; device removal; link/interconnect faults; firmware panic; calibration/profile update; interrupted update; rollback; thermal fault; and field-style reproduction from one command. Data and evidence Package and image hashes, compatibility matrix, permissions/IOMMU groups, update state, reset/fault timeline, resource-leak report, performance regression result, dependency/build provenance, health snapshot, and complete support bundle. Exit gate Supported platforms pass clean install, isolation, update/rollback, soak, recovery, and regression thresholds; failures never leave stale DMA or silent corruption; one bundle identifies the first failed boundary. Unlocks release qualification: release approval can be based on a versioned evidence set rather than a successful laboratory demo. One developer entry point: provide a repository wrapper such as scripts/test/run.py --lane <contract|dma|queue|mvm|yolo-e2e> --backend <fake|cosim|fpga|silicon> . It should select CTest/KUnit/firmware/model tests, capture the build and run manifests, and return a non-zero status on a failed gate. The wrapper orchestrates existing test tools; it must not hide their raw reports. Verification matrix

entries.heading: Separate transport correctness, numerical correlation, and product qualification
entries.text: Test layer Representative cases Pass condition Automation Schema and ABI Generated register diff, struct sizes/offsets, reserved bits, unknown versions, endian conversion RTL/C/C++/docs agree; old UMD works with new KMD inside declared compatibility Every change, 32/64-bit cross-build KMD UAPI Fuzz ioctls, invalid handles, overflow, race/close, fork, quotas, permissions, compat mode No crash/leak; recover or report permanent device loss without stale DMA Lab qualification and platform matrix First board Enumeration proof 1000 bind/unbind/reset cycles without resource leak or host crash. First data DMA proof Pattern-exact transfer across required sizes, alignments, IOMMU and scatter/gather cases. First compute MVM proof Simulator-to-silicon checkpoints identify the first numerical divergence. First model YOLO proof Full validation accuracy and end-to-end performance, power and thermal provenance. Information to obtain

entries.heading: Questions that must be answered by the chip, board, and firmware teams
entries.text: Public demos cannot answer these details. They are the minimum inputs for turning the architecture into code without guessing at hidden hardware behavior. entries.heading: Kernel behavior is sourced; hardware details remain proposed until disclosed
entries.text: Linux PCI driver guide Probe order, BAR resources, DMA masks, bus mastering, IRQ registration, engine enablement and teardown responsibilities. Linux DMA mapping guide CPU/physical/bus address distinction, coherent versus streaming mappings, masks, errors, map/unmap lifecycle and barriers. Linux memory barriers dma_wmb() / dma_rmb() ownership example and the distinction between shared DMA memory and MMIO ordering. Linux MSI/MSI-X guide Message-signaled interrupt ordering, vector allocation and advantages over shared pin interrupts. Linux device I/O Portable MMIO accessors, ordered access, PCI posted writes and readback for completion. Linux VFIO IOMMU-protected userspace device access, groups, BARs, interrupts and DMA mapping for a trusted lab path. Linux UIO guide Small userspace drivers for mappable memory and interrupts; not a universal interface. Linux compute accelerators Common accelerator subsystem, command queues/DMA context, DRM reuse and /dev/accel/accel* . Linux ioctl design Command macros, backward compatibility, structure layout, explicit padding, compat mode and information-leak prevention. Linux dma-buf Buffer export/import, attachment, scatterlist access, CPU synchronization and pollable fences. Linux PCIe AER Error classes, counters and driver recovery callback requirement. Linux PCI error recovery error_detected , reset, resume, permanent failure and interrupt behavior during recovery. Linux firmware loading request_firmware() lifecycle and synchronous/asynchronous image loading APIs. QEMU system emulation Full-system CPU, memory, and device emulation; the virtual machine contains the devices implemented by its selected machine model. QEMU RISC-V system target Board selection, firmware behavior, and the warning that an image built for unsupported real hardware is unlikely to boot on a different virtual machine. QEMU RISC-V virt machine Generic virtual platform capabilities, including its PCIe host bridge; it is not a model of a private ACiM controller or endpoint. QEMU GDB usage -s -S , remote debugging, breakpoints, registers, and memory inspection for emulated CPU bring-up. Buildroot manual Cross-toolchain, bootloader, Linux kernel, root filesystem, images directory, deployment, and QEMU runtime-test workflow. Linux remoteproc Loading and starting remote-processor firmware, ELF images, resource tables, trace buffers, virtio, and RPMsg integration. OpenOCD flash programming Lab-oriented image programming, verification, reset, and scripted startup through a debug adapter. Linux ftrace Kernel tracing through tracefs for latency, event, interrupt, driver, and scheduling correlation. Linux tracepoints Low-overhead static instrumentation hooks suitable for a versioned accelerator event vocabulary. Linux ABI documentation Kernel ABI stability categories and the requirement to document interfaces exposed to userspace. ONNX concepts Official definitions for models, graphs, nodes, tensors, attributes, types, shapes, and versioned operator sets. StableHLO specification Normative syntax, verification, and semantics for the versioned high-level ML operation set. MLIR documentation Official compiler infrastructure, dialect, operation, pass, and progressive-lowering concepts. MLIR ODS documentation Operation Definition Specification and TableGen-based generation of operation classes, verifiers, builders, and documentation. OpenXLA PJRT Uniform device API and plugin boundary connecting framework/compiler clients to accelerator backends. SPDX specifications Machine-readable software, license, component, security, and provenance information standards used for SBOM workflows. Tenstorrent tt-kmd Public KMD repository with character device, PCIe, memory, interrupt, message queue, telemetry and device-specific modules. Tenstorrent tt-umd Public UMD repository, KMD dependency, IOMMU/host-memory setup, simulator tests, logging and profiling patterns. Analog CIM SDK guide Compiler, artifact, HAL, runtime and first software vertical slice that this board backend implements. NPU/SoC software architecture Control/data planes, runtime-driver-firmware contracts, profiling, debugger and production platform context. iHW patent study Public patent mechanisms and evidence limits; no private iHW register, driver, firmware or YOLO implementation is assumed here. Evidence boundary: no public source identified in this study discloses an iHW production UMD, KMD, firmware ABI, PCIe register map, operator placement, or complete YOLO run manifest. Every concrete ACIM_* name, offset, structure, and repository path on this page is an engineering proposal to be replaced or confirmed by the actual hardware contract.

entries.heading: Analog CIM Scale-Out, Fault Tolerance, and LLM Inference
entries.text: Map LLM inference across Analog CIM devices and reason about communication, memory, precision, and throughput. System design | research snapshot 2026-07-11 Analog CIM Scale-Out, Fault Tolerance, and LLM Inference A concrete software architecture for turning imperfect analog arrays into a logical accelerator mesh. It adapts selected Tenstorrent ideas at the descriptor, virtual-device, simulator, collective, and observability boundaries while replacing Tensix execution with calibration-aware Analog CIM placement and a hybrid digital backend. Read the LLM verdict Open the fault model Inspect the contracts 6 resource and fault levels 2 explicit execution planes 5 LLM partition modes 1 shared artifact and HAL Measured silicon Patent mechanism Simulation Company claim Engineering design Executive answer

entries.heading: Can a Mythic- or iHW-style Analog CIM system run an LLM?
entries.text: Architecture conclusion Yes, as a hybrid inference system No public evidence yet establishes a legacy M1076 or an iHW product running a production decoder LLM end to end. Put static dense projections and feed-forward weights on Analog CIM arrays. Keep dynamic attention, KV-cache writes, normalization, nonlinear functions, routing, sampling, and precision recovery on digital engines and SRAM/DRAM. Scale the model with explicit tensor, pipeline, and expert parallelism. Judge success in tokens/second, time-to-first-token, inter-token latency, accuracy, energy/token, capacity, and recovery time, not array TOPS alone. Measured silicon

entries.heading: Transformer feasibility is real but bounded
entries.text: A 2025 IBM-led study mapped 7.1 million unique ALBERT weights to a fabricated 14 nm PCM chip and reported average accuracy 1.8 percentage points below FP. Attention, activations, pooler, and classifier remained in software, so this is strong evidence for analog linear layers, not an end-to-end decoder LLM. Read the Nature Communications paper Circuit and model simulation

entries.heading: Dynamic attention needs different memory
entries.text: A 2025 gain-cell proposal stores K/V values in write-friendly charge memory and computes both attention dot products in the analog domain. Results use 64 × 64 SPICE simulations and PyTorch model evaluation, not fabricated full-system silicon. It should be a separate target capability, not assumed for flash arrays. Read the Nature Computational Science paper Mythic evidence

entries.heading: Legacy product facts and current roadmap differ
entries.text: The M1076 brief documents 80 million weight capacity, 76 tiles, 25 TOPS, and a PCIe interface. Mythic's 2025 announcement claims a rebuilt chiplet architecture for 1T+ LLMs and publishes internal efficiency projections; public independent silicon results for that roadmap are not yet identified here. Open the M1076 brief Hybrid confirmation

entries.heading: Mythic's acquisition reinforces this partition
entries.text: Mythic describes analog compute for dense matrix operations and the acquired Videantis digital architecture for attention, control, programmability, and other high-performance workloads. That is the system boundary this design makes explicit. Read the acquisition announcement iHW boundary: the public material reviewed for this study supports analog inference positioning, patent mechanisms, and smaller-model demonstrations, but does not establish a public decoder-LLM silicon result. The architecture below is a target-neutral proposal, not a disclosure of iHW's internal implementation. Physical execution

entries.heading: What actually happens during one Analog CIM matrix-vector operation
entries.text: Mythic publicly identifies a flash array and analog circuits, but not every internal encoding, converter, or accumulation detail. The flow below is a generic differential or bit-sliced ACiM contract whose exact choices must be supplied by the target descriptor. 1. Program Encode fixed weights Map quantized weight slices into conductance states, verify writes, and record achieved values. Wq -> G+, G- 2. Drive Encode activations DACs, pulse widths, or switched levels convert an input slice into row stimuli. xq -> V or t 3. Multiply Cell current Each enabled cell contributes current according to its programmed state and applied input. Iij ≈ Gij * Vi 4. Accumulate Column integration Kirchhoff summation and integration form one partial dot product per active column. Ij = ∑i Iij 5. Convert Read analog result ADC or charge-to-pulse circuitry digitizes the integrated result using a calibrated range. qj = ADC(Ij) 6. Rebuild Digital correction Combine signs, slices, arrays, and chips; apply scale, bias, saturation, and optional residual correction. y = requant(sum(q)) y_hat = D(ADC(sum_i A(G_ij, x_i, theta)))) The software-visible result is not only W × x. A includes device and circuit behavior, theta identifies calibration and environment state, and D is digital reconstruction. A compiler must preserve all three in the executable and debug map. Decision Hardware owns Compiler owns Runtime/firmware owns Weight representation Cell levels, differential support, spare rows/columns, programming limits Quantization, clipping, sign encoding, bit slicing, placement Programming, verify/retry, checksum, provenance Input representation DAC or pulse modes, fanout, legal ranges Activation precision, slice count, scale, schedule Command sequencing and range selection Output precision Integration window, ADC channels, saturation behavior ADC plan, partial-sum tree, digital correction Calibration binding, telemetry, retry policy Numerical guarantee Characterized error envelope by operating point Operator-specific tolerance and fallback variant Verify live state remains inside the compiled envelope Defect hierarchy

entries.heading: A bad cell, a bad ADC, and a bad tile are different problems
entries.text: Each level needs a distinct health record and recovery action. Collapsing all defects into one bitmap makes placement unstable, wastes healthy capacity, and prevents useful diagnostics. Important evidence correction: Mythic's public patent supports virtual addressing and harvesting of defective compute tiles, including removal of a minimal set of tile rows or columns. It does not by itself prove spare flash-cell rows, spare bitlines, or spare ADC channels inside Mythic's ACE array. The row/ADC example below comes from a separate EnCharge AI patent and is used only as an alternative design pattern. L0 Cell or device state Programming error, stuck cell, noise, drift, retention Mitigation Verify-and-program, differential encoding, redundant devices, sensitivity-aware placement, calibration, retraining or digital residual. CellHealth + achieved_conductance L1 Row or wordline Driver, line, or clustered cell failure Mitigation Redirect the logical row to a spare row, shift following rows, or reserve the region. Reprogram all affected weight slices. RowRemap[logical] = physical L2 Column or ADC channel Bitline, integrator, ADC, or output lane failure Mitigation Route the bitline to a spare converter, shift channels, or reduce usable output width. Rebuild the output-channel map. ColumnRemap + AdcHealth L3 Array or subarray Exhausted spares, local thermal/noise region Mitigation Quarantine the region, split the tensor differently, consume reserved capacity, or select a lower-stress precision mode. ArrayCapability + health_class L4 Compute tile Array, RISC-V, SIMD, SRAM, or router compute path Mitigation Assign only good tiles valid logical addresses. Preserve pass-through routing where hardware permits it. LogicalTileMap + harvest_mask L5 Chip, link, card, host Device, PCIe/fabric link, power, or host failure Mitigation Reform the logical mesh, reroute collectives, restore a distributed checkpoint, and rebind or recompile affected stages. ClusterTopology + route_epoch Mythic patent mechanism

entries.heading: Virtualize the tile grid
entries.text: Test tiles, mark low-performing or defective tiles, and create a physical-to-virtual coordinate map that maximizes usable compute. A null-address tile can be skipped as a compute destination while packet routing continues through it. Applications target a stable logical grid. Open US11475973B2 Alternative array mechanism

entries.heading: Redirect rows and converter channels
entries.text: EnCharge describes normally disabled redundant ADC channels, input/output selection networks, and spare rows. This is useful evidence for the required software contract, but it is a pending patent application and not evidence of Mythic or iHW product behavior. Open WO2025122556A1 Health lifecycle

entries.heading: Discover once, bind explicitly, monitor continuously
entries.text: Factory Characterize BIST cells, rows, columns, ADCs, arrays, tiles, links, and corners Provision Create base map Burn immutable IDs and repair data; sign the factory health record Boot Discover live state Merge factory map, boot tests, firmware revision, topology, and calibration Compile Place logical work Use capability classes and reserve capacity without hard-coding serial numbers Load Bind and program Select physical resources, program weights, verify checksums, publish map epoch Run Observe and recover Track drift, saturation, retries, faults, route health, and rebind at a checkpoint Artifact Mutability Owner Required fields Target descriptor Versioned per architecture/SKU Architecture + compiler Arrays, dimensions, formats, commands, converters, memory, links, legal modes Factory health Immutable and signed Manufacturing Device ID, repair map, disabled resources, characterization bins, provenance Live health Changes at boot/runtime Firmware/runtime Available resources, temperatures, errors, spare budget, route epoch, timestamps Calibration bundle Changes with chip and environment Calibration service Ranges, offsets, gains, noise envelope, temperature/voltage window, expiry Executable intent Immutable build output Compiler Logical placement, variants, tolerance, constants, collectives, fallback, debug map Binding record One per deployment epoch Runtime Logical-to-physical map, programmed-weight hashes, calibration IDs, routes, checkpoint Buildable contracts

entries.heading: The compiler targets capabilities; the runtime binds a particular device
entries.text: This is the key separation borrowed from virtual device and harvesting designs. A portable executable should express logical resource requirements and legal variants. Serial-number-specific defects remain in the binding record.

entries.heading: Stable C++ runtime boundary
entries.text: class AcimDevice { public: virtual CapabilityView capabilities() const = 0; virtual HealthView health() const = 0; virtual Binding bind(const Executable&) = 0; virtual Event program(const Binding&) = 0; virtual Event submit(const CommandBatch&) = 0; virtual RecoveryResult recover(const Fault&) = 0; }; class AcimMesh { public: virtual MeshTensor distribute(const Tensor&, ShardSpec) = 0; virtual Event collective(Collective, MeshTensor&) = 0; virtual Checkpoint checkpoint() = 0; virtual void reform(const TopologyView&) = 0; }; Security and correctness: firmware validates descriptor bounds, executable signatures, ABI versions, programmed-weight hashes, calibration validity, DMA ranges, and route epochs. Host metadata is never trusted merely because it came from the compiler. Fault-aware compiler

entries.heading: Placement is a constrained optimization, not a rectangular tiling exercise
entries.text: Compiler and runtime placement algorithm Compile against capability classes; bind against one health epoch. for op in topological_order(graph): variants = legal_lowerings(op, target, accuracy_policy) for variant in variants: shards = tile_tensor(variant, logical_mesh) candidates = resources_matching(shards, capability_class) score = ( estimated_latency + lambda_energy * estimated_energy + lambda_error * predicted_numerical_error + lambda_comm * collective_bytes + lambda_wear * programming_and_aging_cost + lambda_risk * spare_consumption ) choose pareto_feasible_variant_or_fallback() at load time: verify health_epoch and calibration envelope match logical shards to physical arrays apply row/column/tile remaps program and verify weights publish signed binding record on fault: retry -> recalibrate -> local remap -> tile rebind -> mesh reform/checkpoint restore -> digital fallback Accuracy cost

entries.heading: Predict layer sensitivity
entries.text: Use quantization sweeps, measured nonideality models, activation statistics, calibration state, and selective digital residuals. Sensitive layers can request wider ADC plans or digital execution. Capacity cost

entries.heading: Reserve without wasting the fleet
entries.text: Compile variants for nominal and degraded capacity classes. Keep spare rows, columns, arrays, and tiles out of normal placement unless policy explicitly spends them. Communication cost

entries.heading: Place around collectives
entries.text: Estimate bytes and hops for activation shards and partial sums. Local weights remove weight traffic, not all inter-chip traffic. Research input: the 2026 Dyn-A-Map paper ranks vulnerable subarray regions and relocates important weights to healthier regions without retraining. Its evidence is pre-silicon SPICE and architecture simulation, so use it as a mapping heuristic to validate on real devices, not as a proven field-repair result. Read Dyn-A-Map . Open-source architecture audit

entries.heading: What to adapt from Tenstorrent, and what must remain ACiM-native
entries.text: Reuse decisions apply to selected modules and contracts after dependency and license review. Repository names are not blanket approval to copy an implementation. Reference ACiM decision Concrete adaptation Do not import TT-MLIR + TT-XLA + Forge ONNX Adapt frontend and pass patterns Keep StableHLO/ONNX import, diagnostics, pass pipelines, and plugin boundaries; introduce ACiM target dialects and capability interfaces. TTNN, TTMetal, TTKernel operations and Tensix legality assumptions. TT-UMD SoC/cluster descriptors Adapt isolated descriptor machinery Use a grid descriptor as the compiler/runtime contract; extend harvesting into row, column, ADC, array, tile, and calibration views. Tenstorrent discovery, PCIe transport, TLB, memory map, firmware, and device implementation. MeshDevice + MeshTensor Adapt virtual-device semantics Create AcimMesh , explicit sharding/replication, mesh command queues, and explicit all-gather/reduce-scatter/all-reduce. Assumed TT link topology, tensor layouts, kernels, and dispatch implementation. Cluster descriptors + tt-run Adapt topology/test patterns Store static and discovered topologies independently; test subsets, fallback mappings, multi-host SPMD, and pipeline groups without hardware. Tenstorrent-specific YAML fields and launcher/device behavior. TT-Fabric Study control-plane architecture Separate persistent health/routing control from the data plane; pause, flush, reroute, reform a mesh, and restore checkpoints. Fabric router, protocol, link, and firmware code tied to TT hardware. tt-emule Adapt same-API backend pattern Run compiler/runtime tests against a functional ACiM emulator selected behind the same HAL as hardware. Tensix core threads, circular buffers, NoC, SRAM, and kernel semantics. ttnn-visualizer + tt-perf-report Adapt reports and UX selectively Visualize graph placement, analog ranges, defect maps, calibration epochs, converter use, collectives, and first divergent layer. TT trace schemas, counters, memory layouts, and operation assumptions. TT-Metal, UMD transport, KMD, firmware Replace Build ACiM commands, programming service, HAL, driver, firmware scheduler, power/reset, safety, and telemetry from the target ABI. All device-specific implementations unless a narrow utility passes semantic, test, dependency, and license review. Why the UMD decision changed

entries.heading: Descriptor concepts are explicitly reusable
entries.text: Tenstorrent's custom-SoC guide calls the SoC descriptor reusable for other grid-like SoCs and identifies it as a higher-stack contract. That supports adapting the descriptor/coordinate boundary while replacing transport and device code. Read the custom-SoC guide Other foundations

entries.heading: Use target-neutral projects where they fit better
entries.text: MLIR supplies IR infrastructure, OpenXLA PJRT supplies a framework plugin contract, TVM supplies a target-extensible compiler reference, and AIHWKit/CrossSim supply analog-aware numerical modeling. Evaluate each behind the same target contract. Open the SDK implementation structure Scale-up and scale-out

entries.heading: A logical mesh spans six physical scopes
entries.text: "Weights stay in memory" removes repeated model-weight fetches. It does not remove activation, partial-sum, KV-cache, expert-routing, control, checkpoint, and telemetry traffic. Level 0 Array One MVM slice, converter group, local spares Level 1 Tile Arrays, digital core, SRAM, local router Level 2 Chip Logical tile grid, NoC, shared services Level 3 Card Several chips, switch/fabric, power domain Level 4 Host Runtime executor, memory, queues, checkpoint shard Level 5 Cluster Distributed mesh, serving scheduler, fleet health

entries.heading: Data plane
entries.text: Weights Program once per model/binding epoch; verify and retain locally. Activations Shard, multicast, pipeline, and exchange between analog and digital stages. Partial sums Reduce across row-parallel shards with declared accumulation precision. KV cache Allocate and page in write-friendly digital or specialized dynamic memory. Collectives All-gather, reduce-scatter, all-reduce, broadcast, all-to-all.

entries.heading: Control plane
entries.text: Discovery Enumerate chips, arrays, links, topology, firmware, and capacity class. Health Track calibration, temperature, saturation, retries, faults, and spare budget. Placement Bind logical programs to a health epoch and route epoch. Recovery Pause, drain, remap, reprogram, reform mesh, restore checkpoint, resume. Governance Sign artifacts, enforce ABI, record provenance, support rollback. Parallel mode Analog placement Required communication Primary risk Column-parallel linear Shard output channels and their local weights All-gather output shards when the next operator needs the full tensor Output/ADC imbalance and gather latency Row-parallel linear Shard input channels and produce partial outputs Reduce-scatter or all-reduce partial sums in an explicit accumulator format Reduction bandwidth and numerical order Pipeline parallel Place layer ranges on chips/cards/hosts Point-to-point activation transfer and microbatch scheduling Bubbles, stage imbalance, recovery scope Expert parallel Store different MoE experts in local arrays Top-k routing and all-to-all token exchange; return weighted expert outputs Hot experts, dynamic traffic, stranded capacity Data parallel serving Replicate the model or pipeline for independent requests Request routing and model/adapter distribution; no per-token gradient reduction Weight programming time and replica capacity Mythic's statement that future APUs do not need a GPU-like high-speed APU-to-APU link is a company claim. Whether it holds depends on model partitioning, batch, context, topology, and how much activation/KV/partial-sum traffic remains. The runtime must model and measure that traffic rather than encode the claim as an assumption. Hybrid LLM mapping

entries.heading: Place operators by state behavior, not by the word "MatMul"
entries.text: Digital Norm + RoPE Reductions, reciprocal/sqrt, position-dependent transforms Analog Q/K/V projections Static dense weights; shard by head or hidden dimension Digital/dynamic CIM Attention + KV Per-token writes, QK, mask, softmax, AV, paging Analog Output + MLP Static dense projections, gate/up/down matrices Mixed Residual + sample Digital accumulation, LM head option, logits, top-k/p sampling LLM work Default target Why Compiler/runtime requirement Embedding / LM head Analog when capacity and lookup behavior fit; otherwise digital memory Static weights but irregular lookup or very wide output Vocabulary partition, gather/top-k strategy, tied-weight handling Q/K/V and output projections Analog CIM Large fixed dense matrices with repeated use Head-aware sharding, activation scales, calibration, collectives MLP gate/up/down Analog CIM Usually the largest fixed-weight compute share Fuse digital activation where legal; balance array and converter use QK T and attention-value product Digital engine by default Both operands depend on runtime tokens; NVM reprogramming is a poor fit Specialized gain-cell/dynamic-CIM capability may override this explicitly KV cache SRAM/DRAM/HBM or write-friendly dynamic CIM Grows per request and changes every token Paged allocation, eviction, sharing, compression, context policy LayerNorm/RMSNorm, RoPE, softmax, SiLU/GELU Digital vector/scalar engine Reductions, transcendental/approximate functions, control, precision Stable kernels, fusion, scratch planning, numerical contract MoE router and top-k Digital Dynamic sparse decision and load balancing Expert placement, capacity factors, all-to-all, hot-expert telemetry LoRA / accuracy adapter Digital companion Small, updateable correction avoids reprogramming base analog weights Version adapters separately and overlap their GEMM with analog MVM Prefill

entries.heading: High parallelism favors array utilization
entries.text: Many prompt tokens turn projection and MLP work into matrix-matrix execution. Tile tokens and output channels together, overlap digital attention with analog projections, and pipeline collectives. Time-to-first-token remains the product metric. Decode

entries.heading: Weight locality helps, but dynamic state dominates
entries.text: Each step is sequential and often matrix-vector at low batch. Converter latency, digital companion balance, KV-cache access, inter-chip activation traffic, and synchronization can dominate. Measure inter-token latency and energy/token. Software pattern worth reusing: vLLM's PagedAttention shows why the KV cache needs a virtualized, dynamically allocated memory layer. Reuse the paging and serving concepts; replace GPU-specific kernels and memory APIs with the ACiM hybrid runtime. Read the PagedAttention paper . Four-bit LLMs

entries.heading: Four logical bits do not automatically mean one cheap analog operation
entries.text: Representation

entries.heading: Separate model bits from physical cost
entries.text: Logical weight format W4 may be symmetric/asymmetric and per-tensor, per-channel, or group-scaled. Cell representation One logical weight may use one multi-level cell, a differential pair, several devices, or bit slices. Activation execution A8/A16 may require serial input slices and multiple integration cycles. Output reconstruction ADC width, partial-sum count, scale precision, and digital accumulation determine effective accuracy. Accuracy policy

entries.heading: Use selective precision, not one global fidelity
entries.text: Quantize with measured ranges Calibrate group scales and clipping using representative prompts and target nonideality. Protect sensitive paths Keep norms, accumulators, logits, outlier channels, and selected layers in higher-precision digital execution. Train or adapt for hardware Use noise-aware fine-tuning or a small digital LoRA/residual adapter when model access permits. Promote on evidence Choose more slices, wider conversion, repeat-and-average, or fallback only when accuracy gain exceeds latency/energy cost. The M1076 brief reports capacity in "weight parameters," not packed bytes. A 4-bit software checkpoint cannot be assumed to double M1076 weight capacity. Physical packing depends on unpublished cell encoding, differential representation, redundancy, slicing, and metadata. The compiler must query a target-specific physical_slots_per_logical_weight function. A recent transformer adaptation study places fixed base-model weights on analog tiles and small LoRA corrections on digital cores; it reports simulation through LLaMA 3.1 8B, not full-system LLM silicon. This is a useful software architecture for preserving programmable adaptation without repeatedly reprogramming NVM arrays. Read the AHWA-LoRA study . Capacity sanity check

entries.heading: Legacy M1076 numbers show why a new scale architecture is necessary
entries.text: Illustrative lower bounds assume one model parameter consumes one advertised weight slot and ignore spares, replication, calibration data, digital state, and unavailable capacity. They are not performance estimates. 80M weights per M1076 Legacy product brief 320M weights per 4-chip card MP10304 product brief 1.28B weights per claimed 16-chip card 2021 company announcement ceil(P/C) minimum capacity units Before reserve and system overhead Model parameters M1076 chips at 80M 4-chip cards at 320M 16-chip units at 1.28B Interpretation 7B 88 22 6 Minimum advertised slots; practical count is higher. 70B 875 219 55 Communication, power, host, and yield become system-level constraints. 1T 12,500 3,125 782 Mythic's current 1T claim necessarily refers to a rebuilt architecture, not simple M1076 scaling. A capacity fit is not an execution proof. The next gates are supported operators, physical weight encoding, programming time, yield reserve, activation/partial-sum bandwidth, collectives, digital companion capacity, KV memory, accuracy at scale, thermal limits, and end-to-end tokens/second. Runtime state machine

entries.heading: Recovery escalates from cheap local action to distributed restart
entries.text: Observe Detect anomaly Timeout, checksum, saturation, drift, ECC, route, or numerical sentinel Retry Repeat safely Replay idempotent command or use repeat-and-average within policy Correct Recalibrate Refresh offset/range/drift state and verify the operating envelope Remap Spend local spare Redirect row/column/ADC or bind an alternate array/tile; reprogram weights Reform Change mesh Drain queues, update route epoch, restore distributed checkpoint Degrade Fallback or reject Use digital variant, lower service tier, quarantine device, or fail explicitly Recovery invariant Reason Test No stale physical address survives a map epoch Prevents commands from reaching harvested or reassigned resources Inject remap between queued batches and reject old-epoch descriptors Weights match the binding record Row/column/tile movement changes physical storage Corrupt a programmed block and require checksum failure before execution Calibration matches operating conditions Converter and device behavior changes with time and environment Cross temperature/voltage boundary and force recalibration or fallback Collectives use one topology epoch Mixed route views can deadlock or corrupt partial sums Drop a link during reduce-scatter and verify drain/reform/restart Retries preserve request semantics Duplicate execution can alter stateful work or output ordering Replay at every command boundary with idempotency and sequence checks Implementation plan

entries.heading: Build one fault-aware distributed linear layer before a full LLM
entries.text: 0 / 8 complete Version the schemas Define target, health, calibration, executable, binding, topology, and trace schemas with compatibility tests. Implement the functional backend Execute ACiM MVM plus injected noise, saturation, drift, row/column/tile defects, and digital fallback behind the production HAL. Import one transformer block Use ONNX or StableHLO; preserve QKV, attention, norm, residual, and MLP boundaries with support diagnostics. Lower one distributed linear Generate column- and row-parallel variants, logical array placement, ADC plan, accumulator format, and collective intent. Bind around injected defects Apply row/column remaps and tile harvesting, program weights, verify hashes, and emit a reproducible binding record. entries.heading: Study a pattern, expose its assumptions, then rebuild it for ACiM
The question to ask at every layer
entries.text: Which concept is a general accelerator-software pattern, and which part exists only because Tenstorrent executes digital dataflow kernels on Tensix cores? Write both answers before designing the ACiM equivalent. 1. Trace Observe the working path Follow one tensor, IR operation, command, buffer, and trace ID. 2. Explain Name the invariant State the general compiler or runtime responsibility in hardware-neutral language. 3. Contrast Expose target assumptions Mark every Tensix core, tile, NoC, circular-buffer, and device-ABI dependency. 4. Translate Define the ACiM contract Substitute arrays, converters, calibration, programming, digital fallback, and device state. 5. Verify Build and correlate Run the same vectors through reference, simulator, runtime, and hardware levels. High-value code-reading targets: TT-MLIR's dialect boundaries, TT-UMD's SoC descriptor, MeshDevice's virtual topology, tt-emule 's alternate backend, TT-Fabric's control/data planes, and Tenstorrent's trace/report tooling. Each becomes a concrete exercise in the transfer map below. Step A | Target architecture worksheet

entries.heading: Learn which hardware facts create software requirements
entries.text: IHW's public patent record reveals part of the numerical architecture: positional digit-sliced weights, adaptive converter range, grouped quantization, and signed-current cancellation. It does not show that every pending mechanism is implemented in a product, or disclose the complete array, command, calibration, compiler, firmware, and runtime contract. Use the checklist to construct a target descriptor and to mark each field as measured, specified, assumed for simulation, or still unknown. This section inventories the inputs; the discovery workbook later converts them into implementation rules and tests. Why this comes first: every item below changes an IR type, legalization rule, mapping cost, artifact field, runtime state, or validation test. The iHW patent deep read is one example of extracting possible software-visible mechanisms from hardware evidence. 0% 0 / 12 complete Compute primitive Array dimensions, cell technology, MVM direction, supported shapes, and accumulation structure. Numerical formats Activation, weight, accumulator, signed encoding, bit slicing, scales, saturation, and rounding. Converter path DAC/input encoding, ADC count and sharing, range control, resolution, latency, and energy. Weight programming Pulse algorithm, write verification, programming time, endurance, retention, and update granularity. Variation and faults Per-cell/per-array spread, unusable cells, fault maps, remapping, aging, and production yield policy. Calibration lifecycle Factory, boot, periodic, thermal, and workload calibration ownership and stored state. Digital companion Vector/scalar engines, nonlinear operators, reductions, control flow, fallback, and precision recovery. Memory and interconnect SRAM, external memory, DMA, NoC, coherency, tensor layouts, bandwidth, and multicast behavior. Command model ISA or descriptors, queues, dependencies, synchronization, preemption, timeout, and reset semantics. Existing software Importer, IR, simulator, compiler, runtime, firmware, driver, profiler, and debugger maturity. Artifact and ABI Target identifiers, code, mappings, programmed weights, calibration data, debug maps, and compatibility fields. Product acceptance First models, accuracy SLA, latency, energy, programming time, thermal corners, and field-update requirements. Learning output: a versioned target descriptor whose required fields are explicit. A simulator may carry clearly labeled assumptions; a production compiler should diagnose any unresolved field needed for correct lowering. Tenstorrent learning map

entries.heading: Turn each code-reading target into an ACiM implementation exercise
entries.text: Read a narrow path, identify the architectural pattern, build its ACiM equivalent, and retain a concrete artifact that proves what you learned. Filter by the layer you want to study next.
