entries.heading: A digital dataflow processor and an analog array expose different contracts
entries.text: 1 Compute Primitive and placement 2 Numerics Error and precision 3 State Weights and calibration 4 Scheduling Movement and lifetime 5 Product Qualification and recovery Different primitive

entries.heading: Core-grid kernels versus physical array mappings
entries.text: Tenstorrent Programs reader, compute, and writer kernels across Tensix cores using tiles, circular buffers, and NoC traffic. Analog CIM Programs conductance cells, encodes inputs, performs array MVM, digitizes columns, and combines slices or partial sums. Compiler consequence Replace core placement with physical array tiling, signed mapping, converter assignment, and analog/digital partitioning. Proof One matrix must map to arrays and produce an explainable artifact with no hidden Tensix assumptions. Different error contract

entries.heading: Quantization is only one part of analog numerical behavior
entries.text: Digital path Declared formats, rounding, saturation, and deterministic instruction semantics dominate. Analog path Converter quantization, programming error, read noise, nonlinear response, wire effects, temperature, and drift interact. Compiler consequence Carry range, slice, ADC, calibration, and tolerance metadata through lowering and preserve it in the artifact. Proof Layerwise error distributions and task accuracy must correlate across reference, simulator, model, and silicon. New persistent state

entries.heading: The executable depends on the physical device population
entries.text: Digital path Weights are ordinary bytes loaded into memory; two compliant devices should execute the same bits. Analog path Programmed conductances, calibration coefficients, fault maps, drift age, and thermal state can differ by chip. Runtime consequence Version and bind model artifacts to device-specific state without making builds irreproducible. Proof Cold boot, recalibration, field update, rollback, replacement device, and corrupted-state recovery all pass. Different cost model

entries.heading: Programming and conversion join compute and data movement
entries.text: Tenstorrent focus Tile locality, SRAM capacity, NoC bandwidth, kernel overlap, and core utilization. Analog additions Array residency, programming amortization, ADC contention, slice count, calibration, remapping, and digital fallback. Scheduler consequence Optimize end-to-end latency and energy under accuracy, endurance, temperature, and memory constraints. Proof Cost predictions explain measured bottlenecks and remain stable across representative shapes and corners. Wider qualification

entries.heading: Correctness is a population and lifecycle claim
entries.text: Digital qualification Instruction correctness, timing, memory, concurrency, firmware compatibility, power, and reliability. Analog additions Device distributions, yield, retention, endurance, drift, recalibration overhead, thermal corners, and aging. Operations consequence Telemetry and health policy need thresholds, fallback, quarantine, reset, and service decisions. Proof Population statistics support the product SLA rather than one favorable chip or one benchmark run. TT-Metal performance patterns translated

entries.heading: Keep the dataflow machinery, but move it around resident analog weights
entries.text: TT-Metal optimizes a digital machine whose operands move through DRAM, local SRAM, circular buffers, a NoC, and compute engines. ACiM removes most steady-state weight traffic when conductances remain programmed, but it still has commands, activations, converter traffic, partial sums, digital epilogues, and outputs to move. The useful abstraction is therefore not "no data movement"; it is "weight-stationary dataflow with explicit movement and synchronization around the array." Keep Double buffering Ping-pong activation ingress and digitized-result egress so DMA and digital work can overlap array execution. Adapt Prefetch Prefetch commands and activations every run. Stage weights only before planned program/verify work; do not page conductances per token. Keep Fast dispatch Let a device controller consume queued descriptors without waiting for one host call per layer or array firing. Extend Program cache Cache schedules and digital kernels, but bind every hit to the target, weight map, calibration, health, and ABI epochs. CB : bounded producer-consumer storage CQ : ordered device work stream DMA : transfer engine without CPU copying NoC : on-chip packet network DAC : optional multi-level input converter ADC : sensed analog result to digital code MVM : array compute primitive Recommended ACiM execution flow Control, persistent physical state, and per-inference tensor traffic remain separate. Control Host SDK Bind buffers and enqueue CQ + events Dependencies and fences Device dispatcher Validate and issue Resident program Trace or command template Array scheduler Converters, power, hazards State Weight package Logical tensors and scales Program + verify Rare load or remap path Resident weight handle Arrays and conductance map Bind device state Calibration, defects, health Validated binding Weight, profile, and health epochs Data Input source Host, camera, or LPDDR Ingress CB A/B Activation prefetch Input encode / drive Bits, pulses, or DAC levels Array MVM Resident weights ADC / rebuild Digitize and combine slices Egress CB A/B Result ping-pong Digital epilogue Bias, scale, activation, reduce Output DMA Next layer or host

entries.heading: The bottleneck moves; it does not disappear
entries.text: In steady state, an ACiM layer should not stream its full weight matrix from DRAM. The likely critical path is activation delivery, input encoding, row/word-line drive, optional DAC conversion, array settle time, ADC conversion, bit-slice reconstruction, digital reduction, and output movement. Once the pipeline is filled, its ideal tile interval is approximately max(Tin, Tfront_end + Tmvm + Tadc, Tepilogue, Tout) , but only stages backed by independent hardware can overlap. Shared converters, power rails, thermal limits, or SRAM banks must be modeled as one serialized resource even when software exposes several queues. Ping-pong schedule

entries.heading: Double buffering is still useful on both sides of the array
entries.text: The diagram shows a legal overlap only when input DMA, analog execution, digital epilogue, and output DMA use independent resources. Three activation tiles moving through two ingress and two egress slots Engine t0 t1 t2 t3 t4 t5 Input DMA A0 A1 A2 Encode/drive + MVM + ADC A0 A1 A2 Digital epilogue A0 A1 A2 Output DMA A0 A1 A2 Storage Producer to consumer Initial policy ACiM-specific rule Command ring Host runtime to device dispatcher Enough descriptors to keep the device ahead of the host; use sequence numbers and completion fences. Descriptors reference immutable weight handles and explicit calibration/profile epochs. Ingress CB DMA or sensor to encoder/DAC Two activation macro-tiles, banked as ping and pong. Layout must match row drive, bit-plane order, scale group, and multicast destinations. Weight residency table Programmer to array scheduler Metadata and handles, not a per-inference copy of the weight bytes. Invalidate on reprogram, remap, failed verify, incompatible calibration, or device replacement. Egress CB ADC/reconstruction to digital epilogue Two result blocks; use more only after a measured consumer-jitter problem. Entries carry ADC mode, saturation flags, slice count, and uncertainty or retry status. Partial-sum scratch Array slices or chips to reduction Keep local until all slices are combined; avoid round-tripping through external memory. Accumulator width and reduction order are part of the numerical contract. Calibration cache Calibration service to array and digital stages Pin the active profile and publish an immutable epoch during execution. A profile change drains dependent queues before replacing scales, ranges, or trims. Output ring Digital epilogue to next layer, CPU, or host Use events or credits so a producer never overwrites unread output. Prefer direct layer-to-layer routing; host readback is a graph boundary, not a default after every MVM. Cache lifetime model

entries.heading: Reuse three different objects without confusing their validity
entries.text: 1. Kernel binary cache Compiler and ISA lifetime Stores DSP/vector kernels and firmware fragments. Key by source or IR, compiler flags/version, ISA, target revision, and firmware ABI. Invalidated by code generation or binary compatibility changes. 2. Program template cache Structural schedule lifetime Stores placement, CB plan, engine sequence, synchronization, and parameter slots. Mutable addresses and state handles remain runtime arguments. Invalidated by shape, layout, precision, topology, mapping, resource, or ABI changes. 3. Bound trace / residency cache Device-state lifetime Stores replayable descriptors bound to concrete buffers, programmed weights, calibration, health, and stable dependencies on one device. Invalidated by address movement, reprogram/remap, profile update, drift/health epoch, reset, or replacement device. Technique-by-technique decision

entries.heading: What survives the architecture change
entries.text: "Keep" means the mechanism transfers directly. "Adapt" preserves the pattern with a different cache key, tile, or producer. "Conditional" requires measured independence or a specific workload. "Replace" rejects the literal Tensix assumption. TT-Metal technique Decision ACiM implementation Evidence before enabling it Reader / compute / writer pipeline Adapt Use activation-ingest, array-sequencer, and result-drain roles. Keep explicit producer/consumer ownership, but do not require a Tensix-style RISC-V core for every role. Timeline shows each role executing independently and queue starvation has an attributable owner. Two-page CB / double buffering Keep Start with two activation slots and two ADC-result slots. Alternate ownership with credits or semaphores while the array works on the other slot. Lower ingress/egress stall cycles without violating SRAM, power, thermal, or numerical limits. Deeper circular buffers Conditional Add a third or deeper slot only for bursty DMA, variable ADC retries, multicast skew, or digital-consumer jitter. Queue-depth histogram reaches two and deeper storage improves end-to-end throughput enough to justify SRAM cost. Async DMA and retained transfer state Keep Preprogram common source, destination, stride, page, route, and format state, then issue compact descriptors for repeated activation blocks and outputs. Descriptor and firmware overhead falls; explicit barriers still prove descriptor, payload, and completion ordering. DRAM prefetcher + global CB Adapt Use a persistent producer for activation streams. Weight prefetch means staging bytes before rare program/verify work; frequently used layers or experts should occupy separate resident arrays or chiplets. The plan includes program/verify latency, endurance, and eviction cost. It never assumes that changing conductance is as cheap as filling SRAM. Fast dispatch Keep Place descriptor validation, dependency tracking, and engine issue in device firmware. The host submits graphs or batches, not one blocking command per layer. queue_empty_cycles approach zero and host scheduling gaps disappear from the device timeline. Program cache Two-level reuse Cache structural command templates, placements, buffer plans, and digital kernels under an exact canonical key. Bind mutable addresses, weight handles, and profile handles as checked runtime arguments. The structural key includes op, shape, layout, precision, target revision, ISA/firmware/ABI, macro-tile, converter topology, mapping version, and power mode. Submission separately rejects stale residency, calibration, or health epochs. Kernel compilation cache Keep narrowly Reuse binaries for DSP/vector kernels, device firmware fragments, and format converters. Keep this distinct from physical weight and calibration state. A cache clear and cold compile are testable; binary compatibility is tied to compiler, ISA, and firmware versions. Metal Trace-style replay High value Capture a static graph's already-validated descriptors on device and replay them against stable buffers, resident weights, and profile bindings. Build trace families for bounded dynamic shapes. Commands, addresses, weight handles, calibration/health epochs, and dependencies still match. A changed binding invalidates or patches the trace through a defined validation path. Multiple CQs + events Conditional Use one queue for input/output transfers and another for execution, or independent queues for resource-disjoint array groups. Synchronize with device-visible events. The queues use independent DMA/array/converter resources; concurrent execution improves throughput instead of overloading shared ADCs, NoC, or power delivery. Tensor sharding Essential Shard output channels, input rows, bit slices, experts, or batches across physical arrays. Placement must include converter groups, spare rows/columns, and calibrated quality. Mapping report predicts utilization, cross-shard reductions, converter occupancy, defects, communication bytes, and error impact. Multicast + semaphores Keep Broadcast one activation block to several arrays that hold different output-channel weights. Use receiver-ready credits before overwriting the source slot. One injected copy replaces many unicasts, receivers do not starve, and skew does not force excessive buffering. Block reuse + intermediate CB Keep Retain activation blocks, scales, and partial sums near the arrays across output blocks or slices. Choose an array-native macro-tile rather than the literal 32x32 TT tile. External and NoC bytes fall, local capacity remains legal, and the numerical reduction order remains reproducible. Fused bias and activation Keep Fuse scale, offset, bias, clamp, quantize, and supported activation into the post-ADC digital path before storing the tensor. Fusion removes a materialized tensor and preserves the reference result within the declared tolerance. SubDevices + persistent programs Conditional Partition array groups, SRAM, queues, and digital engines into independently scheduled regions; reserve one region for a persistent sensor or prefetch pipeline. The target descriptor proves that converters, routes, calibration state, power, reset, and fault domains are separable. Shared resources remain globally arbitrated. NoC ordering and barriers Keep Define ordering for payloads, descriptors, doorbells, multicast, and completion writes. Batch barriers where legal, but never infer cross-route ordering. Litmus and stress tests cover wraparound, multiple producers, reset, timeout, and weakly ordered transport behavior. TT 32x32 tile and core coordinates Replace literal form Expose an ACiM macro-tile derived from physical rows, columns, bit slices, ADC grouping, local SRAM, and digital reduction width. The tile is generated from a versioned target descriptor and changes legally across device revisions. Runtime decision graph

entries.heading: Choose an optimization from observable hardware facts
entries.text: 1 Are the required weights programmed and valid? Yes - use the resident handle; do not prefetch weights. No - enqueue program/verify or page replacement before execution. 2 Can DMA overlap converter and array use? Yes - allocate ingress ping-pong buffers. No - keep the queue contract, but do not claim hidden latency. 3 Do arrays share ADCs, input drivers/DACs, SRAM banks, routes, or power? Yes - model tokens for each shared resource and cap concurrency. No - schedule independent array groups in parallel. 4 Are shape, addresses, weights, and profile epochs stable? Yes - replay a resident trace. No - use a cached parameterized program template or compile a new variant. 5 Does one activation feed several resident weight shards? Yes - multicast once and synchronize receivers. No - use local or unicast delivery. Software ownership

entries.heading: Organize the implementation around the optimized flow
entries.text: compiler/schedule/ Pipeline and resource planner Chooses macro-tiles, CB depth, multicast groups, converter tokens, fusion, and overlap. runtime/cache/ Three cache lifetimes Separates kernel binaries, structural program templates, and device-bound traces or residency bindings. runtime/queue/ CQs, events, and trace replay Owns enqueue, dependency, capture, replay, completion, timeout, and cancellation semantics. runtime/residency/ Weight and profile handles Tracks what is programmed, verified, calibrated, pinned, stale, remapped, or evictable. firmware/dispatch/ Command prefetch and validation Consumes rings, validates epochs and ranges, resolves handles, and feeds the scheduler. firmware/dataflow/ Ingress, array, and egress stages Implements DMA, CB credits, input encoding, array firing, ADC drain, reconstruction, and barriers. firmware/resources/ Physical arbitration Owns ADC/DAC groups, SRAM banks, routes, power envelopes, thermal throttling, and reset domains. tools/profiler/ One correlated timeline Joins graph, command, buffer, array, converter, DMA, digital, calibration, power, and accuracy events. Order Implement Required counters and tests Acceptance condition P0 Resident weight handles, one CQ, device dispatch, ingress/egress ping-pong CBs, async DMA, events, local post-ADC epilogue. Queue-empty cycles, every engine's busy/stall cycles, CB occupancy, bytes, saturation/retry flags, accuracy delta, timeout/reset tests. One static MVM stream runs continuously, matches the reference tolerance, and attributes every idle interval. P1 Program cache, trace replay, activation multicast, array sharding, partial-sum locality, fusion, and two-queue I/O overlap. Cache hit/miss reason, trace replay count, multicast fanout/bytes, reduction bytes, queue event latency, power and thermal counters. Each feature improves end-to-end latency, throughput, or energy on a named workload without changing accepted accuracy. P2 Global streaming CB, persistent prefetch program, deeper buffers, subdevice concurrency, weight paging, and multi-chip scheduling. Prefetch usefulness, eviction/program time, cross-partition contention, fairness, tail latency, fault injection, recovery, and profile-epoch transitions. Measured workload demand justifies the added state and concurrency; recovery remains deterministic. Optimization rule: never approve a technique from array utilization alone. Record end-to-end latency, throughput, joules per inference or token, task accuracy, converter saturation/retries, temperature, and tail behavior. A schedule that drives every array at once can be slower or less accurate when it overloads shared ADCs, the NoC, the power network, or the digital reconstruction path. Recommended architecture

entries.heading: Keep the portable graph stack above an explicit ACiM boundary
entries.text: Tenstorrent can remain a comparison target or reference implementation without becoming the core dependency of the analog backend. Import PyTorch / ONNX / StableHLO Preserve source semantics and shape constraints Normalize Target-neutral graph IR Canonical ops, quantization intent, fallback policy Decide Capability and partition Analog, digital companion, CPU, or rejection Lower ACiM IR Arrays, slices, converters, calibration, digital ops Plan Physical mapping Placement, programming, memory, routes, schedule Package Versioned artifact Code, weights, maps, calibration schema, debug data Execute ACiM HAL and runtime Simulator and device backends behind one contract Design rule: the target-neutral IR should describe model meaning, while ACiM IR should describe physical analog intent. Neither layer should pretend that a conductance array is a Tensix core. Analog-specific work

entries.heading: The custom backend begins where physical state changes correctness
entries.text: Implementation companion: this page decides what to learn, adapt, or replace from Tenstorrent. The SDK and compiler guide turns that decision into concrete libraries, APIs, schemas, compiler passes, simulator backends, tests, and a first runnable slice. Mapping

entries.heading: Array tiling and decomposition
entries.text: Split matrices by physical rows, columns, differential representation, bit slices, ADC lanes, and available arrays. Define partial-sum combination and padding. Evidence: mapping report includes utilization, slices, conversions, predicted error, and digital work. Numerics

entries.heading: Range and converter planning
entries.text: Select scales, input encoding, accumulation range, ADC mode, saturation policy, and per-layer tolerance using calibration and workload distributions. Evidence: reference versus simulated histograms identify the first divergence and its physical cause. Partition

entries.heading: Analog and digital placement
entries.text: Keep dense supported MVMs on arrays; assign nonlinear, control, normalization, unsupported, or precision-sensitive work to digital engines or CPU fallback. Evidence: capability report states every fallback and conversion cost. Programming

entries.heading: Conductance and fault-aware placement
entries.text: Translate logical weights into programming targets, write/verify actions, remapped cells, spare resources, and per-chip state with endurance constraints. Evidence: deterministic programming manifest and post-program verification report. Calibration

entries.heading: Compensation insertion
entries.text: Attach calibration versions, converter corrections, array gains/offsets, drift models, temperature ranges, and recalibration triggers to executable regions. Evidence: stale or incompatible calibration is rejected or repaired explicitly. Artifact

entries.heading: Device-aware packaging
entries.text: Separate portable model content from device-bound programming and calibration state so builds, deployment, updates, rollback, and replacement remain auditable. Evidence: schema validation and ABI compatibility tests cover every section. Runtime lifecycle

entries.heading: Inference is only the steady-state middle
entries.text: 1 Discover Identify revision, arrays, faults, firmware, features 2 Validate Check artifact, target, ABI, calibration, shapes, and required features 3 Program Write and verify weights under endurance policy 4 Calibrate Load or measure coefficients and health state 5 Execute Schedule mixed analog/digital work and trace it 6 Maintain Monitor drift, temperature, faults, updates, recovery Accuracy and performance evidence

entries.heading: Use a correlation ladder, not a single simulator result
entries.text: IBM AIHWKit and CrossSim are useful analog-behavior study tools. They are not substitutes for a target specification, circuit model, RTL, or measured silicon. Declare which effects and timing each model includes. Level 0 Framework FP32 Semantic golden model and dataset baseline Level 1 Digital quantized Isolate format, rounding, clipping, and scaling loss Level 2 Ideal array Validate decomposition, signed mapping, slices, ADC range Level 3 Nonideality model Variation, noise, drift, parasitics, faults, converters Level 4 C++ / SystemC Artifact, runtime, queues, memory, cycles, trace, recovery Level 5 RTL / mixed signal Protocol, timing, firmware, circuit corners, co-simulation Level 6 Silicon population Task SLA across chips, temperature, age, and recalibration Evidence family Required measurements Failure question Numerical Task metric, first divergent layer, absolute/relative error, distribution tails, saturation, slice and ADC contribution. Which declared mechanism explains the loss? Performance End-to-end and layer latency, throughput, array utilization, converter stalls, memory traffic, programming and calibration time. Did reuse preserve the wrong cost model? Energy and thermal System and subsystem energy, ADC/DAC share, idle/control overhead, thermal steady state, DVFS or power-mode behavior. Is the analog advantage visible at product boundaries? Reliability Chip distribution, defects, yield policy, drift versus time, retention, endurance, temperature corners, recovery and fallback rate. Does the product SLA hold beyond a favorable sample? Correlation Same vectors, artifact hash, calibration version, device state, seeds, trace IDs, and uncertainty across every level. Can another engineer reproduce and localize the difference? Architecture choice flow

entries.heading: See the available paths, when each fits, and what to learn first
entries.text: "Best" depends on the immediate learning question. The highlighted option is the recommended starting point for this study; the other choices remain useful at a later integration stage or for a different product goal. 1 Model entry ONNX, ORT plugin, or StableHLO/PJRT 2 Compiler base MLIR, TVM, or a minimal custom IR 3 Execution model Functional, queued/cycle, or real hardware 4 Operator home Analog array, DSP, or CPU 5 Device access Simulator HAL, VFIO, or UMD/KMD Decision 1 | 3 choices

entries.heading: Which model entry should you implement first?
entries.text: Choose the boundary that matches the models and framework behavior you need to observe. Recommended first Direct ONNX importer Best for learning compiler semantics with YOLO and common deployment models. It keeps the first debug path small: model, importer, IR, lowering, simulator. Integration stage ONNX Runtime plugin EP Best when applications already use ORT and the compiler/runtime API is stable enough to support subgraph capability, compilation, caching, and CPU fallback. OpenXLA path StableHLO plus PJRT Best when JAX, XLA, or StableHLO portability is a product requirement. PJRT provides a uniform device API, not the ACiM lowering itself. Recommended sequence: direct ONNX import for the first runnable slice, then an ORT plugin EP; add StableHLO/PJRT when OpenXLA clients are an explicit requirement. Decision 2 | 3 choices

entries.heading: Which compiler foundation should carry ACiM semantics?
entries.text: Choose based on how many abstraction levels, custom types, and target legality rules the compiler must express. Recommended product path MLIR dialect stack Best for a real ACiM backend with target-neutral tensors, analog-aware operations, physical mapping, command IR, verifiers, and progressive legalization. Exploration path TVM backend Useful for schedule search, tensor-expression experiments, and Python-centered prototyping when the analog state and artifact model remain modest. Smallest experiment Custom C++ or Python IR Useful for one operator and quick cost-model experiments. It becomes expensive when adding graph regions, diagnostics, serialization, rewrites, and multiple targets. Recommended for this architecture: MLIR, because ACiM needs several explicit levels: model meaning, analog intent, physical placement, and executable commands. Use a minimal Python model alongside it as the numerical oracle. Decision 3 | 3 levels

entries.heading: Which execution backend should you build now?
entries.text: These are successive fidelity levels rather than competitors; each reveals a different class of bug. Start here Functional and nonideality model Tests operator semantics, mapping, quantization, converter range, variation, and layerwise accuracy without queue or timing complexity. Build second Queued or cycle-oriented fake device Tests artifacts, buffers, dependencies, command ordering, timing estimates, trace IDs, timeouts, and recovery while hardware is unavailable. Correlate third FPGA or silicon backend Tests actual transport, firmware, converters, calibration, PVT behavior, faults, performance, and energy. Recommended flow: implement all three behind one HAL in this order. Skipping the functional model mixes numerical bugs with runtime bugs; skipping the queued model makes hardware bring-up unnecessarily opaque. Decision 4 | 4 choices

entries.heading: Where should each graph operation execute?
entries.text: The compiler should choose per operation and shape; no single engine is best for the whole model. Recommended policy Hybrid cost-based partition Evaluate accuracy, conversion, transfer, memory, latency, and energy for every candidate placement, then keep every fallback visible in the artifact and report. Dense compute ACiM array Best for large, supported, weight-resident MVM or convolution regions whose mapping, converter range, and measured accuracy satisfy the target. Digital companion DSP or vector engine Best for activation, normalization, reduction, softmax, partial-sum repair, small tensors, and precision-sensitive work near the arrays. Host fallback CPU Best for rare unsupported operations, dynamic control, preprocessing, postprocessing, and early bring-up; transfer and synchronization costs must be visible. Recommended rule: place an operation on ACiM only when end-to-end cost includes conversions, partial sums, calibration, and error recovery. Otherwise choose the closest digital engine, with CPU as the explicit final fallback. Decision 5 | 3 maturity stages

entries.heading: How should host software reach the device?
entries.text: Match the access path to the hardware stage and isolation requirements. Start here Simulator HAL No kernel driver is needed. The runtime calls an in-process or service backend implementing the same buffer, submit, wait, trace, and reset contracts. Trusted lab VFIO prototype Useful for a single-purpose PCIe lab path with IOMMU-protected userspace access while the production UAPI is still changing. Production device UMD plus KMD Best for multi-process isolation, DMA ownership, interrupts, reset, power, firmware, security, cleanup, and stable deployment. An integrated SoC uses equivalent platform-driver responsibilities. Recommended flow: stabilize the HAL with simulator backends, use VFIO only for controlled bring-up when appropriate, then implement the production UMD/KMD boundary from the measured device contract. Applied implementation labs

entries.heading: Six connected builds that teach the complete software path
entries.text: Each lab has a learning objective and a reviewable output. Complete them in order because every later lab consumes contracts and test vectors from the earlier ones. Lab 1 Trace Tenstorrent model-to-device path Lab 2 Model Digital and analog numerical ladder Lab 3 Specify Target descriptor and ACiM IR Lab 4 Lower One operator to physical mapping Lab 5 Execute Artifact, HAL, queues, and trace Lab 6 Correlate Accuracy, latency, energy, and faults 0% 0 / 6 complete Lab 1 Trace one Tenstorrent operation Follow MatMul from StableHLO or ONNX through TT-MLIR dialects, layout decisions, runtime calls, command queues, buffers, and device completion. Annotate every target-specific concept. Output: stack diagram, IR snapshots, call trace, and a one-page explanation of each boundary. Lab 2 Build the numerical reference ladder Implement FP32, INT8/INT4, ideal-array, and nonideality models. Sweep ADC range, slices, programming error, noise, drift, and clipping with identical test vectors. Output: reproducible notebook, layerwise error plots, and the first-divergence report. Lab 3 Specify the ACiM machine Create a target descriptor and MLIR ODS definitions for arrays, conductance formats, converters, SRAM, digital engines, calibration classes, defects, and command capabilities. Output: schemas, sample target, verifier tests, and an architecture-to-software field map. Lab 4 Lower MatMul end to end Import MatMul, legalize it, tile rows and columns, select signed/bit-sliced mapping, assign ADCs, plan partial sums, insert digital epilogue work, and emit executable commands. Output: pass pipeline, mapping report, command listing, debug map, and simulator result. Lab 5 Run the artifact through a fake device Package commands, constants, layouts, and calibration requirements. Implement sessions, buffers, submit/wait, trace, timeout, reset, and functional plus queued backends behind one HAL. Output: C API, artifact schema, backend conformance tests, trace viewer input, and recovery transcript. Lab 6 Correlate and optimize the full path Compare reference, nonideality, queued/cycle, RTL/FPGA, and silicon when available. Explain accuracy loss, converter stalls, memory traffic, programming time, energy, and fault behavior. Output: correlation dashboard, bottleneck report, model-fidelity statement, and prioritized optimization list. Capstone: a runnable repository in which one ONNX MatMul compiles into an ACiM artifact, executes unchanged on numerical and queued backends, emits a layer-to-command trace, and reproduces the reference comparison. Use the accelerator repository blueprint for directory ownership, GoogleTest/pytest placement, CI gates, performance tests, contribution rules, and debugging artifacts. Step B | Architecture discovery workbook

entries.heading: Convert every unknown hardware fact into a software task
entries.text: This section consumes the Step A worksheet. For each answer, update a machine-readable contract, implement the affected rule, and add the test that proves the rule. 1. Observe Hardware fact Specification, measured data, simulator behavior, or an explicitly labeled assumption. 2. Record Target descriptor Typed field, units, range, version, source, confidence, and required/optional status. 3. Compile IR and mapping rule Verifier, legality, cost, placement, precision, and fallback behavior. 4. Execute Artifact and runtime state Commands, calibration binding, programming data, queues, telemetry, and recovery. 5. Prove Correlation test Golden vectors, corners, trace IDs, expected errors, and acceptance threshold. Fact to learn Evidence to inspect or measure Software you can implement after learning it Compute primitive Array dimensions, MVM direction, supported shapes, cell encoding, differential mapping, bit slices, and accumulation path. ACiM op semantics, shape verifier, tiling rule, physical layout, utilization report, and partial-sum plan. Converter path Input encoding, DAC or bit-serial drive, ADC count/sharing, range modes, ENOB, sample rate, latency, and energy. Range planner, converter allocator, saturation estimator, schedule resource, and performance/energy cost model. Programming behavior Pulse algorithm, write-verify, target tolerance, programming time, endurance, retention, update granularity, and verify readback. Programming manifest, weight lifecycle state machine, cache policy, update/rollback flow, and endurance-aware placement. Variation and defects Cell/array distributions, unusable rows or columns, spare resources, remap rules, yield data, temperature, and aging. Fault-map schema, logical/physical remapper, calibrated cost, spare allocation, degraded mode, and population tests. Memory and interconnect SRAM banks, external memory, NoC topology, multicast, DMA paths, bandwidth, alignment, coherency, and address spaces. Buffer planner, tensor layouts, transfer operations, double buffering, route schedule, and bandwidth diagnostics. Digital companion DSP/vector/scalar ISA, supported nonlinear and reduction operators, local memory, synchronization, and conversion formats. Capability partitioner, digital dialect, fusion rules, precision-repair path, and analog/digital boundary cost. Command and device model Descriptors or ISA, queues, dependencies, interrupts, preemption, timeout, reset, firmware ABI, and telemetry counters. Command IR, artifact encoder, HAL, runtime queues/events, UMD/KMD contract, profiler, and recovery tests. Calibration lifecycle Factory, boot, thermal, periodic, per-model, and drift-triggered calibration; storage format and invalidation rules. Calibration schema, compatibility check, runtime state owner, recalibration scheduler, stale-state error, and trace fields. Existing software path Current importer, simulator, compiler passes, runtime API, firmware, driver, profiler, debugger, tests, and example models. Gap map showing what already runs, which contracts are implicit, and the smallest new vertical slice to implement. First workload Representative tensor shapes, operator mix, accuracy metric, batch, latency, throughput, power, and update requirements. Benchmark manifest, compiler priorities, fallback policy, acceptance thresholds, and regression suite. Study exercise: add status = specified , measured , assumed , or unknown to every target field. Attach its source and confidence, then make the compiler reject any unknown field required by the selected lowering. Primary sources

entries.heading: Mythic and Videantis: What the Acquisition Solves
entries.text: Analyze product and acquisition evidence around Mythic and Videantis as a bounded industry case study. Company case study | research snapshot 2026-07-11 Mythic and Videantis: What the Acquisition Solves Mythic acquired Videantis GmbH on May 19, 2026. The deal adds a production-proven digital processor architecture and software stack to Mythic's analog compute-in-memory platform. That can make the system complete and create a digital path for sensitive operations, but it is not evidence that flash-cell error, converter error, drift, aging, or analog effective precision has been eliminated. Read the verdict Trace the accuracy stack Trace hybrid execution Audit the acquisition Mythic Analog flash for dense matrix operations Videantis Programmable digital processing and mature tools Strategic value Complete hybrid execution and faster productization Evidence gap No public post-deal silicon accuracy benchmark yet Research verdict

entries.heading: A strong system acquisition, not a demonstrated cure for analog error
entries.text: The best-supported interpretation is build-versus-buy for the digital half of a hybrid computer. Mythic already used digital SRAM, SIMD, RISC-V control, routing, conversion, calibration, and compilation around analog matrix engines. Videantis adds a much broader VLIW/SIMD processor, explicit memory control, complete-network execution, a compiler/SDK, simulation and debug tools, and automotive production experience. This can contain accuracy-sensitive work in digital execution, but the companies have not published the partition policy, numerical contract, calibration interface, or measured post-acquisition results. Confirmed disclosure Hybrid architecture is intentional Mythic says analog will execute efficient matrix operations while Videantis digital cores handle control, attention, non-max suppression, codecs, SLAM, and other high-performance work. Engineering inference Digital fallback can protect accuracy A compiler could route sensitive layers or unsupported operators to deterministic digital cores. The public announcement does not confirm that this sensitivity-based policy exists. Not yet demonstrated The combined accuracy claim remains open No public report gives same-model digital-INT8 versus hybrid accuracy across multiple chips, temperature, voltage, calibration age, device age, and analog coverage. Company disclosure Independent or academic source Engineering inference

entries.heading: Public paper boundary
entries.text: As of July 11, 2026, this review found Mythic architecture presentations, product documentation, software documentation, demonstrations, press releases, and trade reporting, but no peer-reviewed Mythic silicon paper publishing end-to-end model accuracy across chip populations, PVT corners, calibration age, and device aging. Related flash-CIM papers explain plausible techniques, but they are not proof of Mythic's proprietary design. Mythic execution flow chart

entries.heading: Separate the disclosed analog-flash path from the proposed hybrid platform
entries.text: Mythic has disclosed graph conversion, analog-aware optimization, flash weight programming, analog MVM, ADC readout, and digital tile support. The acquisition announcement discloses the intent to combine those engines with Videantis cores. It does not disclose the unified runtime, partition cost model, or recovery protocol drawn below. Disclosed model and compiler path Flash programming and calibration Proposed hybrid inference Required health and fallback loop Disclosed Prepare the Mythic model Public workflow material describes a mostly offline graph-to-analog deployment path. 1 Import graph Framework or ONNX model and reference accuracy 2 Set ranges Quantization, clipping, calibration data, ANA8 target 3 Analog-aware adapt Retraining for supported analog execution 4 Map graph Analog matrices, digital tile work, tensor layout 5 Pack and generate Weight image, commands, code, deployment artifact 6 Qualify Compare converted model with the named digital baseline Bind to physical flash and converters Partly disclosed Program and calibrate Programming, stored truth, refresh, and internal calibration are described; their detailed contract is proprietary. 1 Select tiles Capacity, supported matrix shapes, healthy resources 2 Program flash Map weights into multilevel conductance targets 3 Verify or refresh Compare physical state with stored digital truth 4 Calibrate Analog/digital correction, converter range, PVT state 5 Bind artifact Device identity, programmed image, calibration version Proposed post-acquisition steady state Proposed integration Execute one hybrid region This is the software contract the combined platform needs, not a published implementation. 1 Digital prepare Videantis control, normalization, layout, scale, routing 2 Choose target Analog coverage, sensitivity, deadline, locality, health 3 Drive inputs Range-controlled activation bits or phases enter the tile 4 Flash MVM and ADC Conductance MAC, integration, conversion, status 5 Digital finish Accumulate, attention, nonlinear, codec, SLAM, control 6 Apply policy Accept, repeat, recalibrate, refresh, or run digitally Required closed loop Converter and tile telemetry → accuracy/health policy → calibration or flash refresh → sensitivity-aware digital fallback → auditable device-state update Evidence boundary: the individual Mythic and Videantis building blocks are disclosed, and the acquisition announcement states the hybrid intent. The sequence below is a testable engineering model for integration. Until Mythic publishes the unified compiler/runtime and measured combined silicon, it must not be cited as the behavior of a shipping product. Proposed Mythic-Videantis sequence diagram

entries.heading: One request needs one owner for analog accuracy and digital fallback
entries.text: The critical interface is not only a command queue. It carries numerical ranges, calibration identity, health state, placement rationale, and the cost of crossing from analog to digital execution. Application Model and request Unified runtime Proposed owner Videantis cores Digital execution Mythic tile Flash MVM and ADC Calibration control Device-bound state Load, program, and bind Load hybrid artifact and reference policy Query device, programmed state, calibration, and health Program/refresh flash and calibrate tile Return bound device state to runtime Request and repeated graph-region loop Submit input and latency/accuracy policy Run control, preprocessing, and partition decision Execute unsupported, sensitive, dynamic, and control work Send matrix command, activation phases, range, and calibration ID Input phases → flash MVM → integrate → ADC Return output, saturation, converter, and health status Rescale, accumulate, finish operator, and continue graph Return region result, coverage, and measured cost Only when health or numerical policy fails Request recalibration, refresh, remap, or quarantine Return updated state or reject analog coverage Rerun rejected region with deterministic digital fallback Return output, trace, coverage, and health status Mythic-specific bottleneck map

entries.heading: Videantis can remove system gaps, but it can also expose the true analog cost
entries.text: The acquisition helps most with flexible compute, scheduling, memory control, tools, and productization. Flash programming, converter quality, calibration, retention, and analog effective precision remain Mythic responsibilities. Boundary traffic and excessive fallback can erase the claimed analog advantage. Analog ceiling Flash and converter behavior Programming spread, multilevel retention, ADC effective precision, calibration, range, noise, PVT, and aging. Hybrid ceiling Coverage and boundary traffic Input phases, output conversion, partial sums, local SRAM, NoC movement, digital fallback, and low analog utilization. Product ceiling Integration and proof Two software histories, unified IR/runtime ownership, automotive qualification, fleet maintenance, and missing post-deal silicon evidence. Bottleneck Why it matters for Mythic What Videantis can contribute What still must be proved Flash programming precision Mapping a weight to one of many conductance levels introduces programming spread and cell-dependent error before inference begins. Nothing at the device level; digital cores can orchestrate programming, verification, remapping, and fallback. Production distributions, write-verify policy, failed-cell handling, programming time, energy, yield, and capacity loss. Retention, drift, and refresh Stored analog state changes with time and environment, so model correctness has a calibration age and refresh history. Health-vector execution, deterministic maintenance scheduling, telemetry, and a digital path while arrays are refreshed. Refresh trigger, interval, accuracy recovery, downtime, endurance consumption, field policy, and lifetime corners. ADC effective precision Digitization follows every analog MVM. Offset, nonlinearity, noise, range, PVT, and saturation can set the real accuracy ceiling. Range analysis, output correction, sensitive-region fallback, profiling, and software-visible status handling. ENOB, INL/DNL, noise, offset, saturation rate, converter energy/area, chip variation, temperature, voltage, and aging. Input-bit or phase delivery Applying multibit activations over separate phases can serialize work and repeatedly charge array lines. Input preparation, sparsity, scheduling, overlap, local buffering, and deterministic phase control. Actual phase count, activation precision, DAC/input energy, overlap efficiency, utilization, and latency per mapped layer. MVM dynamic range Eight-bit weights do not imply an eight-bit dot-product result; long reductions can clip or lose small contributions. Per-layer scaling, outlier routing, high-precision digital accumulation, extra passes, and digital execution for narrow error budgets. Accumulator precision, output ranges, partial-sum policy, saturation statistics, model sensitivity, and correction energy. Analog/digital boundary traffic Every fallback or hybrid split may require conversion, SRAM storage, NoC transport, synchronization, and format changes. Explicit memory management, multicore scheduling, local-data placement, fusion, and deterministic communication. Bytes and conversions per inference, boundary latency/energy, buffer capacity, contention, and whether overlap hides the cost. Digital fallback dilution Fallback protects accuracy, but too much Videantis execution can reduce analog coverage and erase the energy advantage. Efficient deterministic execution and a graceful path for unsupported or sensitive work. Analog coverage by model and layer, fallback frequency, quality recovery, total energy, latency, area, and breakeven point. Attention and KV state Dynamic attention, normalization, softmax, control, and KV-cache traffic do not match static weight-stationary flash MVM cleanly. Programmable VLIW/SIMD execution, memory control, and complete-network processing. Memory hierarchy, KV capacity/bandwidth, long-context scaling, attention latency, and end-to-end LLM evidence. Model loading and updates Flash writes are slower and less update-friendly than ordinary SRAM or DRAM model loading. Transactional deployment, digital adapters, staged rollout, rollback, and host/runtime control. Cold-start time, update granularity, endurance, partial-write recovery, concurrent serving, and fleet rollout cost. Unified compiler and runtime Mythic and Videantis bring separate mapping assumptions, backends, tools, and performance models. Videantis contributes mature analysis, code generation, simulation, profiling, debugging, and memory analysis. One IR, numerical contract, partition objective, calibration ABI, debugger timeline, versioning, and ownership model. Roadmap and evidence gap Most detailed public Mythic architecture material describes older parts, while the company says it rebuilt architecture and software. Production discipline and tools can improve reproducibility and qualification. Post-acquisition silicon, same-model digital baseline, chip population, PVT/lifetime data, analog coverage, correction cost, and independent reproduction. Mythic critical path First prove converter and flash accuracy across devices and time. Then prove that the unified compiler keeps sensitive work digital without excessive boundary traffic. Finally report end-to-end accuracy, latency, energy, analog coverage, calibration, refresh, and fallback together. A peak analog TOPS/W number cannot answer those questions. System continuation: the scale-out, defect-tolerance, and LLM design specifies how tile harvesting, row/column repair patterns, logical meshes, collectives, KV memory, digital attention, and recovery fit into one compiler/runtime contract. Public record

entries.heading: The architecture evolved from an analog accelerator toward a hybrid platform
entries.text: 2018 Hot Chips architecture Mythic presented embedded-flash matrix memory, 8-bit weight levels, ADC output, digital input approximation, SRAM, SIMD, RISC-V, and a tile network. 2020 M1108 demonstration Mythic described more than 27,000 converters, 8-bit conversion targets, internal variation handling, and ResNet-50 operation near a digital INT8 baseline. 2021 M1076 product brief The 76-tile device advertised 25 TOPS, 80 million weights, 3-4 W typical model power, pre-qualified networks, and no external DRAM for model weights. December 2025 Funding and rebuild Mythic raised $125 million and stated that it had rebuilt its architecture, roadmap, software, and strategy. New performance figures were identified as internal benchmarks. February 2026 Honda co-development Honda announced investment and joint automotive-SoC development, combining Honda models and ECU expertise with Mythic's analog CIM and SDK work. May 2026 Videantis acquisition Mythic bought the German processor-IP company and retained all five founders. Financial terms were not disclosed in the public announcement. Mythic accuracy stack

entries.heading: Public disclosures show several correction layers, but not a complete proof
entries.text: Mythic has not publicly disclosed every circuit or calibration algorithm. The flow below separates stated mechanisms from the measurements that would still be required for an engineering sign-off. 1. Import Model graph ONNX, PyTorch, or framework graph enters an offline deployment flow. 2. Normalize Ranges and INT8 Quantization and numerical-range choices bound converter inputs and outputs. 3. Program Flash weights Weights are represented by programmed conductance levels; stored truth can support refresh. 4. Stimulate Digital approximation Early architecture material applies input bits separately instead of a monolithic input DAC. 5. Compute Analog MVM Flash currents multiply and sum in parallel inside the memory array. 6. Convert 8-bit ADC target Compact high-speed converters digitize outputs; calibration must contain mismatch and PVT error. 7. Complete Digital tile SRAM, SIMD, RISC-V, routing, and software execute non-MVM work and move tensors. Disclosed mechanism Problem it addresses What is publicly supported Remaining evidence gap 8-bit flash weight representation Maps a digital model into dense nonvolatile analog storage. Hot Chips material describes 256 levels per weight and conductance-based multiplication. No public distribution of programmed error, retention, endurance, or effective bits across production chips. Refresh from off-chip true values Can restore weights after drift or retention loss. Mythic's 2018 explanation explicitly says flash resistance can be refreshed from stored truth. Refresh interval, detection policy, write cost, downtime, endurance, and field telemetry are not disclosed. Compact high-speed 8-bit conversion Limits quantization error at the analog/digital boundary. Mythic reported designing and production-testing tens of thousands of on-chip ADC/DAC elements. No public INL, DNL, ENOB, offset, noise, temperature, voltage, yield, or aging tables. Internal analog and digital calibration Compensates mismatch, manufacturing variation, and environmental change. Company statements and independent trade reporting describe calibration as central to reaching the 8-bit target. The calibration equations, per-chip state, runtime triggers, cost, and failure policy remain proprietary. Range setting, quantization, and retraining Avoids clipping and makes the model robust to low-precision execution. Public descriptions show an offline graph-to-analog-INT8 compilation path and pre-qualified models. No complete public model table reports baseline, converted accuracy, analog accuracy, and calibration conditions. Digital support inside each tile Executes control and operations for which analog MVM is unsuitable. M1076 documentation lists RISC-V, SIMD, SRAM, and NoC resources beside every analog engine. The supported-operator list, fallback precision, conversion traffic, and accuracy impact are not public.

entries.heading: "INT8 accuracy" is not "perfect 8-bit analog arithmetic"
entries.text: A model can finish close to a digital INT8 baseline even when individual analog operations have fewer effective bits, because quantization, calibration, retraining, error averaging, and digital execution can absorb some error. A valid proof must report task accuracy against the same digital baseline and also expose effective precision, saturation, chip variation, PVT, retention time, calibration age, and correction cost. What Mythic bought

entries.heading: Videantis contributes the programmable digital system around the analog engine
entries.text: Digital processor IP

entries.heading: VLIW plus SIMD unified cores
entries.text: Scalable identical cores execute deep learning, classical vision, signal processing, imaging, video, attention, non-max suppression, and SLAM. Accuracy relevance: deterministic digital execution is a natural home for sensitive, nonlinear, control-heavy, and unsupported graph regions. Production software stack

entries.heading: Compiler, SDK, simulator, and debug
entries.text: The v-NN SDK performs data-type analysis, dataflow analysis, graph partitioning, multicore mapping, and optimization. The tool suite includes a C compiler, code generation, simulation, profiling, debugging, coverage, and runtime memory analysis. Accuracy relevance: the tools can host a future sensitivity-aware hybrid partitioner, but the Mythic integration has not been published. System and automotive maturity

entries.heading: Explicit memory and deterministic deployment
entries.text: Videantis emphasizes local data, explicit memory management, predictable execution, automotive sign-off tooling, ASPICE history, and deployed processor IP. Accuracy relevance: repeatable scheduling and observability improve validation, but field reliability of prior digital IP does not prove the new analog subsystem's numerical accuracy. Important boundary: Videantis does not publicly claim a flash-programming, ADC-calibration, analog-noise, or drift-remediation technology. It solves digital completeness, programmability, data movement, tooling, and productization. Any direct benefit to analog model accuracy comes through partitioning, fallback, orchestration, and validation, unless Mythic later discloses a deeper integration. Build-versus-buy analysis

entries.heading: The acquisition is strategically coherent because it buys time, software, and production discipline
entries.text: High fit Architecture complement Analog MVM and programmable digital execution solve different workload regions and share a data-locality philosophy. High leverage Time to product Mythic obtains roughly two decades of processor-IP work, a mature toolchain, founders, and deployed automotive experience instead of rebuilding all of it. Indirect Accuracy benefit Digital fallback and partitioning can reduce exposure to analog error, but no public combined benchmark proves the gain. Low direct effect Cell and converter error Videantis does not directly remove flash drift, programming spread, ADC/DAC nonlinearity, PVT sensitivity, noise, or aging. High value Automotive readiness Tooling, deterministic execution, existing production programs, and safety-process experience align with the Honda SoC schedule. Unknown Financial return The public announcement does not disclose purchase price, consideration, revenue, integration cost, or financial targets. System problem Mythic before the deal Videantis contribution Assessment Dense matrix energy Embedded-flash analog MVM. Orchestration and surrounding digital work. Mythic remains the primary solution. Attention, NMS, SLAM, codecs, control Small SIMD/RISC-V resources and host execution. Scalable VLIW/SIMD cores and software libraries. Direct and explicitly stated acquisition benefit. Accuracy-sensitive graph regions Calibration, conversion, digital support, and model qualification. Potential deterministic fallback target. Strong engineering inference; public policy and results are missing. Graph partitioning and scheduling Proprietary Mythic compiler flow. v-NN data-type/dataflow analysis and multicore mapping. Promising, but the unified IR and cost model are undisclosed. On-chip data movement Tile SRAM and NoC. Explicit memory management, hierarchical storage, and intelligent scheduling. Can reduce boundary traffic if the analog/digital interface is co-designed. Flash, ADC, PVT, drift, aging Mythic analog design, calibration, refresh, and software compensation. No disclosed device-level solution. Not solved by the acquisition itself. Automotive deployment Honda co-development and Mythic SDK experience. Long production history, sign-off tools, ASPICE experience, and automotive customers. Major schedule and execution-risk reduction, but the new hybrid SoC needs its own qualification.

entries.heading: Why acquire instead of license?
entries.text: The transaction retains all five Videantis founders and keeps Videantis as a wholly owned subsidiary. That gives Mythic control of the architecture roadmap, compiler/runtime integration, safety process, customer support, and scarce engineering knowledge. A normal IP license would provide cores and tools, but less control over the cross-layer numerical contract that a new analog-digital machine requires. This is an inference from the disclosed structure of the deal; Mythic did not publish its internal build-versus-buy analysis. Required combined architecture

entries.heading: A hybrid chip needs one compiler contract, not two accelerators connected after the fact
entries.text: 1. Characterize Analog target profile Noise, programming error, converters, PVT, drift, faults, calibration cost 2. Analyze Graph sensitivity Layer error budget, precision, unsupported ops, fallback value, safety criticality 3. Partition Analog or digital Joint latency, energy, accuracy, capacity, conversion, locality, and risk objective 4. Lower Two coordinated backends Flash programming and array mapping plus VLIW/SIMD code generation 5. Schedule Explicit tensor movement Local buffers, NoC routes, synchronization, conversion, deterministic deadlines 6. Package Bound artifact Model, digital code, analog weights, calibration, chip identity, fallback policy 7. Maintain Runtime health loop Monitors, recalibration, refresh, remap, digital fallback, rollback, provenance 8. Prove Evidence report Accuracy, coverage, PVT, lifetime, latency, energy, conversion traffic, safety AnalogTargetProfile Measured capability Per-chip array, converter, noise, fault, PVT, energy, latency, drift, and calibration data. NumericalContract Operator tolerance Accepted input/output range, error distribution, saturation, precision, accumulation, and fallback rule. PartitionDecision Auditable placement Why each graph region runs on analog, Videantis digital, host CPU, or a rejected path. CalibrationArtifact Deployment state Programming targets, scales, offsets, chip identity, temperature assumptions, age, and refresh policy. RuntimeHealth Field maintenance Sentinel results, drift score, converter health, refresh count, fallback events, and rollback status. EvidenceReport Claim boundary Baseline, datasets, analog coverage, chip count, conditions, accuracy delta, correction cost, and exclusions. Source-labeled claim ledger

entries.heading: Separate disclosed facts, independent concerns, and reasonable inference
entries.text: All claims Company Independent Inference Mythic, 2018

entries.heading: Flash levels and refresh
entries.text: Mythic described 8-bit weights as 256 programmed flash conductance levels and stated that resistance values could be refreshed from an off-chip true copy. Boundary: architecture disclosure, not a population/lifetime measurement. Mythic, 2020-2021

entries.heading: Converters, calibration, and INT8 target
entries.text: Mythic reported compact high-speed 8-bit converters, manufacturing test, variation handling, model quantization, and production intent near a digital INT8 baseline. Boundary: no complete public benchmark table or converter characterization. Trade reporting

entries.heading: Internal calibration is essential
entries.text: Independent coverage describes analog and digital calibration inside M1076 and reports Mythic's close-to-INT8 accuracy claims. Boundary: reporting based substantially on vendor briefings, not an independent silicon reproduction. Industry critique

entries.heading: Effective precision and aging remain disputed
entries.text: Semiconductor Engineering highlights concerns around multi-level flash precision, aging, manufacturing spread, analog noise, and ADC/DAC energy. Boundary: the article does not identify the cause of Mythic's earlier commercial setback and should not be treated as a Mythic failure analysis. Acquisition release

entries.heading: Videantis is the digital half
entries.text: Mythic explicitly assigns dense matrix work to analog and flexible control, attention, NMS, codecs, SLAM, and other high-performance work to Videantis digital execution. Boundary: combined silicon, scheduling, accuracy, and energy results were not published. Videantis disclosure

entries.heading: Mature mapping and validation tools
entries.text: The v-NN SDK performs data-type and dataflow analysis, partitioning, and mapping. The tool suite includes simulation, profiling, debugging, coverage, memory analysis, and automotive sign-off support. Boundary: these are digital-platform capabilities; their integration with Mythic calibration is not public. Engineering inference

entries.heading: Sensitivity-aware digital fallback is plausible
entries.text: A unified compiler could route layers with narrow error budgets, converter saturation, unsupported math, or safety constraints to Videantis cores. Boundary: plausible architecture, not a disclosed feature or measured result. Current roadmap claim

entries.heading: 100x energy efficiency remains a claim
entries.text: Mythic's 2025-2026 releases cite internal benchmarks and a 100x advantage over GPU systems; Honda independently confirms co-development and investment. Boundary: partnership validates interest and diligence, not the advertised benchmark without public methodology and results. What would prove the strategy

entries.heading: Require an ablation that measures both accuracy recovery and its digital cost
entries.text: Baseline Same model, same data Report FP32 and production digital INT8 before any analog conversion. Analog-only Expose raw weakness Measure Mythic mapping with calibration but without Videantis fallback. Hybrid Measure recovered accuracy Add sensitivity-based digital placement and publish the exact analog coverage. Ablation Price every correction Disable calibration, retraining, refresh, and fallback one at a time. Population Multiple chips and lots Publish mean, tails, weak arrays, yield, remapping, and rejected devices. Corners Voltage and temperature Sweep the operating envelope and repeat before and after recalibration. Lifetime Retention and aging Measure drift, read disturb, refresh frequency, endurance, and field policy. System cost End-to-end energy Include converters, digital cores, NoC, buffers, host traffic, and idle power. Study and interview labs

entries.heading: Turn the acquisition into testable engineering work
entries.text: 0 / 6 complete INT8 claim audit Define digital INT8, analog effective precision, task accuracy, and the measurements needed to connect them. Hybrid partitioner Score ResNet and transformer graph regions by sensitivity, operator support, energy, conversion cost, and deadline. Calibration lifecycle Design program, verify, scale/offset calibration, health checks, refresh, digital fallback, and rollback state. Accuracy-cost ablation Compare digital INT8, analog-only, and hybrid execution while reporting analog coverage and every correction cost. Build-versus-buy memo Evaluate roadmap control, schedule, IP, talent, automotive process, integration risk, and undisclosed financial terms. Interview design review Present the combined target profile, numerical contract, compiler partition, runtime health loop, and proof plan. Sources and evidence boundaries

entries.heading: What this study can and cannot claim
entries.text: Mythic's exact interview loop is not public and can vary by role. This guide does not invent one. It derives preparation areas from Mythic's public architecture, papers, and current role descriptions for analog design, mixed-signal verification, architecture modeling, RTL, compiler, AI software, product, test, and systems work. Company brief

entries.heading: Know which facts are established and which are roadmap
entries.text: Topic Interview-ready statement Evidence discipline Core technique Mythic stores inference weights as analog states in embedded flash and performs dense matrix operations in or through that array. Documented in Mythic technical material and the M1076/ISSCC disclosures. First-generation system The M1076 product brief describes 76 tiles, up to 80M weights, up to 25 TOPS, and 3-4 W for typical complex models. Vendor product figures; quote the source and do not generalize to every workload. Software The public workflow converts FP32 to ANA8, offers analog-aware retraining, and compiles graph mapping, packing, scheduling, and code generation. Documented workflow; implementation details remain proprietary. Current direction Mythic now describes an analog-plus-digital platform, reinforced by its May 2026 acquisition of Videantis for unified digital compute and software. Current company announcement and strategy. Next-generation metrics The company claims roughly 100x energy advantage and 120 TOPS/W for its current architecture, with edge-to-datacenter ambitions. Roadmap/internal benchmark claim; public independent reproduction was not found in this review. Choose a primary lane

entries.heading: Four interview tracks with a shared architecture core
entries.text: Master your role deeply, then learn enough of the adjacent layers to make clean interfaces and credible tradeoffs. Analog and mixed signal

entries.heading: Signal integrity becomes numerical accuracy
entries.text: Prepare: MOS operation, noise, mismatch, PVT, current mirrors, integrators, comparators, ADC/DAC architectures, references, calibration, layout effects, Monte Carlo, and Verilog real-number models. Be ready to design: a column readout with a stated range, ENOB, settling time, power budget, calibration path, and corner plan. Architecture, RTL, and verification

entries.heading: Make a probabilistic primitive behave like a system block
entries.text: Prepare: pipelines, SRAM, NoCs, dataflow, fixed-point arithmetic, power and clock domains, RISC-V/SIMD roles, performance modeling, SystemVerilog, UVM, RNM, assertions, and coverage. Be ready to design: a tile scheduler and verification plan that covers analog latency, backpressure, saturation, faults, reset, and power transitions. Compiler and ML systems

entries.heading: Turn graph semantics into fixed physical resources
entries.text: Prepare: modern C++ and Python, SSA/graph IR, ONNX, MLIR/LLVM, TVM/XLA/IREE concepts, lowering, fusion, tiling, scheduling, memory allocation, quantization, error injection, and heterogeneous partitioning. Be ready to design: an IR and cost model for array shapes, ADC phases, partial sums, local SRAM, digital fallback, and route pressure. Silicon, product, and test

entries.heading: Prove the chip across units, corners, and time
entries.text: Prepare: bring-up, characterization, ATE, wafer sort, yield analysis, correlation, guardbands, binning, screening, DFT/MBIST, failure analysis, reliability, automation, and statistical data analysis. Be ready to design: a test flow that separates device defects, analog variation, digital logic faults, package effects, and model-level escapes. Six-week plan

entries.heading: Build from equations to a defensible system review
entries.text: Week 1 Math and precision GEMV/GEMM, convolution lowering, fixed point, quantization, SNR, ENOB Week 2 Memory devices Flash, PCM, RRAM, SRAM; program/read, drift, endurance, variation Week 3 Circuits and arrays Drivers, Ohm/Kirchhoff MVM, ADC/DAC, IR drop, references, calibration Week 4 Tiles and compiler Mapping, dataflow, SRAM, NoC, partial sums, digital fallback, utilization Week 5 Accuracy evidence NeuRRAM, IBM PCM, mixed CIM, ALBERT, fault-free matrix review Week 6 Mock loop Derivation, coding, design review, debug scenario, paper critique, questions Daily 45 minutes

entries.heading: Recall before reading
entries.text: Write the MVM equation, one non-ideality per layer, and one mitigation with its cost. Then check the source. Twice each week

entries.heading: Explain on a whiteboard
entries.text: Give a two-minute architecture explanation, then a ten-minute version that includes precision and data movement. End of each week

entries.heading: Produce evidence
entries.text: Complete one calculation, one plot or table, one design decision, and one written critique that can enter a portfolio. Portfolio lab

entries.heading: Build a noisy MVM study that exposes tradeoffs
entries.text: A small, honest experiment is more persuasive than a broad slide deck with ideal TOPS. Experiment

entries.heading: Model the signal chain
entries.text: Start with an FP32 matrix-vector reference. Quantize weights and activations with explicit scales. Map signed weights to differential conductances. Add programming error, drift, read noise, IR drop, clipping, and ADC quantization one at a time. Measure MVM error and model accuracy across random seeds and time. Mitigation study

entries.heading: Pay for every recovery
entries.text: Compare per-tensor and per-channel scaling. Add write-verify or measured-error calibration. Try noise-aware fine-tuning. Route one sensitive layer to a precise digital path. Report extra cells, cycles, conversions, digital operations, and calibration frequency. Deliverables: a reproducible notebook or test program, one error-budget plot, one accuracy-versus-energy proxy curve, a short design memo, and a limitations section that distinguishes measured assumptions from guessed ones. Mock technical loop

entries.heading: Questions and the signal a strong answer should contain
entries.text: Architecture

entries.heading: Derive analog MVM from first principles.
entries.text: State V-to-input and G-to-weight mappings, derive cell current and column sum, then list the linearity, independence, range, and readout assumptions. Numerical design

entries.heading: Why is ANA8 not simply ordinary INT8?
entries.text: Separate quantization error from analog programming/read error, explain calibration and analog-aware retraining, and define the digital reference. Mapping

entries.heading: Map a 4096 by 4096 projection onto 1024 by 1024 arrays.
entries.text: Find the 4 by 4 partition, explain broadcast and partial-sum reduction, account for signed and bit-sliced representation, then identify bottlenecks. Converters

entries.heading: Choose ADC precision for a layer.
entries.text: Use output distribution, signal range, noise floor, clipping budget, ENOB, area/energy, conversion phases, and model sensitivity rather than naming a bit count. Debug

entries.heading: Accuracy drops after one week in the field.
entries.text: Reproduce by chip and temperature, compare reference paths, separate common gain drift from per-cell drift, test recalibration, and check whether model margins changed. Verification

entries.heading: Verify a digital controller around an analog array.
entries.text: Define a real-number model, bounded error contract, saturation and latency behavior, randomized PVT/error distributions, assertions, coverage, and transistor-level correlation. Compiler

entries.heading: Partition a transformer between analog and digital compute.
entries.text: Favor dense projections for analog; evaluate outlier-sensitive early/output layers; leave softmax, normalization, dynamic indexing, and control on flexible digital units. Evidence review

entries.heading: Did Nature prove accuracy is solved?
entries.text: Say no as a universal claim, then cite one measured success, its baseline and mitigation, one open issue, and the end-to-end experiment needed to generalize it. Answer frameworks

entries.heading: Keep technical answers structured under pressure
entries.text: Explain a block

entries.heading: Purpose, equation, boundary, error, metric
entries.text: What work does it own? What relation implements it? What enters and exits? How does it fail? Which measurement proves it works? Design a system

entries.heading: Workload, mapping, budget, mitigation, validation
entries.text: Fix tensor shapes and targets, place work, allocate precision/error/energy, price each mitigation, then define end-to-end tests and corners. Debug silicon

entries.heading: Reproduce, localize, separate, correlate, prevent
entries.text: Control variables, narrow the layer, split analog/digital and static/dynamic causes, correlate models to measurements, then add coverage or monitoring. Questions for the team

entries.heading: Ask about the real engineering boundary
entries.text: Which workload and system boundary define the current performance-per-watt target? How does the compiler decide between analog arrays and digital execution for a sensitive operator or channel? Which non-ideality currently consumes the largest accuracy, area, or calibration budget? How are array models correlated from transistor simulation to post-silicon and model-level accuracy? What calibration is factory-only, boot-time, periodic, temperature-triggered, or workload-specific? How does the team measure yield and guardband model accuracy across chips rather than on a golden unit? What changed most between the M1076 generation and the current hybrid analog-digital architecture? What would a strong first 90 days look like for this role? Role and preparation sources
